checks.why: If put on while in wudu, you may wipe over them instead of washing your feet, for a set time.

checks.q: How long may a traveller wipe over leather socks (khuffs)?
checks.why: A resident wipes one day and night; a traveller three.

checks.q: When wiping over leather socks (khuffs), when does the time limit start?
checks.a: From the first thing that breaks wudu after wearing them
w: From the moment you put them on in wudu
From the next Fajr after putting them on
From the first time you wipe over them
checks.why: Put them on in wudu at Fajr, and your wudu breaks at noon: the count starts at noon.

checks.q: When wiping over leather socks (khuffs), what is the least you must wipe?
checks.a: Three fingers' width on the top of each foot
w: The whole sock, top and bottom
checks.why: The fard is the size of three of the hand's small fingers on the top front of each foot.

lessons.title: Menstruation and post-natal bleeding
lessons.about: Its length and what is not allowed during it.

cards.x: Hayd is menstruation, the monthly period. Nifas is the bleeding after giving birth. The shortest hayd is three days and the longest ten. Nifas is at most forty days, with no minimum: it can end after a day.
During menstruation and nifas: prayer, fasting, reciting a verse of the Qur'an, touching the Qur'an without a cover, entering a masjid, tawaf, and intercourse.
She makes up the fasts she missed, but not the prayers.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, making up the obligations

cards.x: Bleeding shorter than three days, longer than ten, or beyond forty after birth is istihadah (irregular bleeding). It does not stop prayer or fasting: she makes wudu for each prayer time and prays.

checks.q: What is nifas?
w: Bleeding from a cut or wound
checks.why: Nifas is post-natal bleeding. Hayd is the monthly period.

checks.q: In the Hanafi school, what is the longest a period (hayd) can last?
checks.why: The shortest hayd is three days and the longest ten. Bleeding beyond that is not hayd.

checks.q: What is the longest nifas (bleeding after giving birth) can last?
checks.why: Nifas is at most forty days, with no minimum: it may end after a day.

checks.q: After her period, what does a woman make up?
checks.why: She makes up missed fasts. Missed prayers are forgiven, a mercy from Allah.

lessons.title: Constant bleeding, wounds and casts
lessons.about: For anyone with a flow they cannot stop, or a dressing they cannot remove.

cards.x: Someone with a constant flow that breaks wudu, such as drops of urine, wind, a bleeding wound or irregular bleeding (istihadah), is excused (ma'dhur) once it continues through a whole prayer time without a break long enough to make wudu and pray the fard.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, when an excuse is established

cards.ar: لَا يُكَلِّفُ اللَّهُ نَفْسًا إِلَّا وُسْعَهَا لَهَا مَا كَسَبَتْ وَعَلَيْهَا مَا اكْتَسَبَتْ رَبَّنَا لَا تُؤَاخِذْنَآ إِن نَّسِينَآ أَوْ أَخْطَأْنَا رَبَّنَا وَلَا تَحْمِلْ عَلَيْنَآ إِصْرٗا كَمَا حَمَلْتَهُ عَلَى الَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِنَا رَبَّنَا وَلَا تُحَمِّلْنَا مَا لَا طَاقَةَ لَنَا بِهِ وَاعْفُ عَنَّا وَاغْفِرْ لَنَا وَارْحَمْنَآ أَنتَ مَوْلَىٰنَا فَانصُرْنَا عَلَى الْقَوْمِ الْكَٰفِرِينَ ﴿٢٨٦﴾
cards.x: Allah does not burden a soul beyond what it can bear.

They make wudu once the prayer time has begun, and pray with it every fard and voluntary prayer they wish in that time. That flow does not break it, though anything else does. When the time ends, the wudu ends.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, the ruling of istihadah and similar cases

cards.x: Once established, the excuse continues as long as the flow appears at least once in each later prayer time. If a whole prayer time passes without it, the person is no longer excused.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, when an excuse is established

cards.x: If a limb has a cast, splint or dressing and washing it or taking it off would cause harm, wipe once over most of it with a wet hand in wudu or ghusl, and wash the rest. It has no time limit and need not be put on in wudu.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, splints and the like

cards.x: Women's bleeding has detailed rulings built on each woman's habit. Note the start and end of every period and every bleeding, and ask a qualified teacher when it is irregular.

checks.q: Drops of urine come throughout every prayer time. With one wudu, the person may pray…
checks.a: Every prayer they wish until that time ends
w: One fard prayer, then wudu again
No prayer; each drop breaks the wudu
Every prayer until the next day
checks.why: The flow they are excused for does not break their wudu until the time ends.
checks.src: Nur al-Idah, the ruling of istihadah and similar cases

checks.q: Your arm is in a cast and washing it would harm you. In wudu you…
checks.a: Wipe over most of the cast and wash the rest
w: Do tayammum for the whole wudu
Leave the arm and pray anyway
checks.why: Wiping over a splint or dressing stands in place of washing beneath it.
checks.src: Nur al-Idah, splints and the like

checks.q: When does an excused person's wudu end?
checks.why: The excused person's wudu lasts until the prayer time ends, unless something else breaks it.
checks.src: Nur al-Idah, the ruling of istihadah and similar cases

lessons.title: The five prayer times
lessons.about: When each prayer starts and ends, and the forbidden times.

cards.x: Fajr is from true dawn (when light spreads across the horizon) until just before sunrise. Zuhr is from when the sun passes its highest point until an object's shadow is twice its length (once, in the view of the two companions), not counting its midday shadow.

cards.ar: فَإِذَا قَضَيْتُمُ الصَّلَوٰةَ فَاذْكُرُواْ اللَّهَ قِيَٰمٗا وَقُعُودٗا وَعَلَىٰ جُنُوبِكُمْ فَإِذَا اطْمَأْنَنتُمْ فَأَقِيمُواْ الصَّلَوٰةَ إِنَّ الصَّلَوٰةَ كَانَتْ عَلَى الْمُؤْمِنِينَ كِتَٰبٗا مَّوْقُوتٗا ﴿١٠٣﴾
cards.x: Truly, the prayer is prescribed for the believers at set times.

cards.ar: حَٰفِظُواْ عَلَى الصَّلَوَٰتِ وَالصَّلَوٰةِ الْوُسْطَىٰ وَقُومُواْ لِلَّهِ قَٰنِتِينَ ﴿٢٣٨﴾
cards.x: Guard the prayers, and the middle prayer, and stand before Allah in devotion.
'Asr is from the end of Zuhr until sunset. Maghrib is from sunset until the red twilight disappears. 'Isha' and witr are from then until dawn; witr is not prayed before 'Isha'.

No prayer is valid at sunrise until the sun has risen, or when it is at its height. When the sun turns yellow before setting, no prayer is valid except that same day's 'Asr: if you have not prayed it, pray it then, though delaying it that late is sinful. Voluntary prayer is also disliked after the Fajr prayer until sunrise, and after the 'Asr prayer until sunset.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, the times when prayer is not valid

checks.q: When does the time of Fajr end?
w: At the first light of dawn
checks.why: Fajr lasts from true dawn until just before the sun rises.

checks.q: When does Maghrib end in the Hanafi fatwa?
checks.why: Nur al-Idah: until the red twilight is gone, on the view the fatwa follows.

checks.q: Which is a time when prayer is not valid?
w: In the middle of the night
checks.why: Sunrise, the sun's height and its setting are the three forbidden times.
checks.src: Nur al-Idah, the times when prayer is not valid

checks.q: When does the time of Zuhr begin?
checks.a: When the sun passes its highest point
w: When shadows are twice their length
checks.why: Zuhr begins just after the sun passes its zenith and starts to decline.

checks.q: You have not prayed 'Asr and the sun is turning yellow. What do you do?
checks.a: Pray it now; it is still valid today
w: Wait and pray it after Maghrib
Leave it; it is a forbidden time
checks.why: Today's 'Asr is the exception. Pray it, and repent for delaying it so late.
checks.src: Nur al-Idah with Maraqi al-Falah, The five prayer times

lessons.title: The adhan and iqamah
lessons.about: Their ruling and their words.

cards.x: The adhan and iqamah are a stressed sunnah for every fard prayer, for men, whether praying alone or in a group, at home or travelling, on time or making up.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, the ruling of the adhan and iqamah

cards.x: Say 'Allahu akbar' four times at the start, then each phrase twice, ending with 'Allahu akbar' twice and 'La ilaha illa Allah'. The iqamah is the same.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, how the adhan is given

cards.x: Allahu akbar: Allah is the Greatest. Ashhadu an la ilaha illa Allah: I bear witness there is no god but Allah. Ashhadu anna Muhammadan rasulullah: I bear witness Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah. Hayya 'ala al-salah: come to prayer. Hayya 'ala al-falah: come to success. La ilaha illa Allah: there is no god but Allah.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, the ruling of the adhan and iqamah

cards.x: In the adhan of Fajr add 'al-salatu khayrun min al-nawm' (prayer is better than sleep) twice after 'hayya 'ala al-falah'. In the iqamah add 'qad qamat al-salah' (the prayer has begun) twice. Give the adhan slowly and the iqamah quickly.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, how the adhan is given

checks.q: What does 'hayya 'ala al-falah' in the adhan mean?
checks.why: 'Hayya 'ala al-salah' is 'come to prayer'; 'hayya 'ala al-falah' is 'come to success'.

checks.q: What is the ruling of the adhan for a fard prayer?
checks.why: A stressed sunnah for every fard prayer, for men.

checks.q: In the adhan of Fajr, what is added, and what does it mean?
checks.a: 'Al-salatu khayrun min al-nawm': prayer is better than sleep
w: 'Qad qamat al-salah': the prayer has begun
'Hayya 'ala al-falah': come to success, said four times
'Allahu akbar': Allah is the Greatest, said six times
checks.why: It is said twice after 'hayya 'ala al-falah', reminding the sleeper.

checks.q: What is added in the iqamah, and what does it mean?
checks.a: 'Qad qamat al-salah': the prayer has begun
w: 'Al-salatu khayrun min al-nawm': prayer is better than sleep
'Hayya 'ala khayr al-'amal': come to the best of deeds
'Allahu akbar': Allah is the Greatest, a fifth time
checks.why: 'Qad qamat al-salah' means 'the prayer has begun', said twice in the iqamah.

lessons.title: Before you pray
lessons.about: The conditions that must be in place before your prayer starts.

cards.x: You must be in wudu (and ghusl if needed), and your body, clothes and the place you pray on must be clean of impurity.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, the conditions of the prayer

cards.x: The 'awrah is the part of the body that must be covered. In prayer, for a man it is from the navel to the knees, the knees included. For a woman it is the whole body except the face, the hands and the feet.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, the conditions of the prayer

cards.x: Face the qiblah, pray after the time has come in, and intend the prayer you are praying, such as today's Zuhr.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, the conditions of the prayer

cards.x: Begin with 'Allahu akbar' while standing, saying it so that you hear yourself.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, the conditions of the prayer

checks.q: In prayer, the 'awrah (what must be covered) for a man is…
checks.a: From the navel to below the knees
w: From the waist to the mid-thigh
From the chest to the ankles
The whole body except the face
checks.why: A man's 'awrah is from the navel to below the knees; a woman's is all but the face, hands and feet.

checks.q: You pray Zuhr before its time has come in. Is it valid?
checks.a: No, the time must have come in
w: Yes, if you did not know
checks.why: A prayer before its time is not valid; pray it again once the time comes in.

checks.q: Which of these is a condition for the prayer to be valid?
checks.a: A clean body, clothes and place
w: Praying in a masjid, in congregation
Praying at the start of the time
checks.why: Purity of body, clothes and place, covering the 'awrah, facing the qiblah, the time and the intention.

lessons.title: The pillars of prayer
lessons.about: The parts of the prayer it cannot be valid without.

cards.x: Inside the prayer, four things are pillars: standing, reciting, bowing (ruku') and prostrating (sujud).
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, the pillars of the prayer

cards.x: Nur al-Idah names these four, then adds that the final sitting, for as long as it takes to recite the tashahhud, is also said to be a pillar. Either way it is fard: the prayer is not valid without it.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, the pillars of the prayer

cards.x: If a pillar is missed, the prayer is not valid and must be prayed again. The prostration of forgetfulness cannot fix it.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, the pillars of the prayer

checks.q: Which of these is a pillar (fard part) inside the prayer?
w: Placing the right hand over the left
checks.why: The pillars inside the prayer: standing, reciting, ruku' and sujud, and the final sitting.

checks.q: You left out a pillar (fard part) of the prayer and the prayer has ended. What follows?
checks.a: It is not valid; pray it again
w: Two prostrations of forgetfulness fix it
Add one rak'ah to your next prayer
checks.why: A missing pillar cannot be repaired by sajdat al-sahw.

checks.q: How long must the final sitting of the prayer be, at least?
checks.why: The final sitting is fard for at least the length of the tashahhud.

lessons.title: The wajib acts of prayer
lessons.about: The wajib acts, and what to do if you miss one.

cards.x: Wajib acts include: reciting al-Fatihah, adding a surah or three verses, calmness in every position, the first sitting, the tashahhud, and ending with 'al-salam'.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, the wajib acts, and the prostration of forgetfulness

cards.x: If you leave a wajib act by mistake, make two prostrations of forgetfulness (sajdat al-sahw) at the end, with tashahhud and salam.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, the wajib acts, and the prostration of forgetfulness

cards.x: If you leave a wajib act deliberately, you are sinful and must repeat the prayer.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, the wajib acts, and the prostration of forgetfulness

checks.q: In the Hanafi school, reciting al-Fatihah is…
w: Recommended only in the first rak'ah
checks.why: In the Hanafi school, reciting al-Fatihah is wajib, not a pillar.
checks.src: Nur al-Idah, the wajib acts, and the prostration of forgetfulness

checks.q: You forgot the first sitting. What do you do?
checks.a: Make the two prostrations of forgetfulness at the end
w: Start the prayer again straight away
checks.why: The first sitting is wajib. Leaving it by mistake is fixed with two prostrations of forgetfulness at the end.
checks.src: Nur al-Idah, the wajib acts, and the prostration of forgetfulness

checks.q: You left a wajib act of prayer by mistake. What repairs it?
checks.why: Leaving a wajib by mistake is repaired by sajdat al-sahw; leaving a pillar is not.
checks.src: Nur al-Idah, the wajib acts, and the prostration of forgetfulness

checks.q: Which of these is wajib in prayer, not a pillar?
checks.a: The first sitting in a four-rak'ah prayer
checks.why: The first sitting is wajib; ruku', sujud and the final sitting are pillars.

lessons.title: How to pray (1): from takbir to ruku'
lessons.about: The prayer step by step, as Nur al-Idah describes it.

cards.x: Raise the hands to the ears (a woman to her shoulders) and say 'Allahu akbar', intending the prayer. A man places his right hand over his left below the navel; a woman places them on her chest.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, how the prayer is put together

cards.ar: قَدْ أَفْلَحَ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ ﴿١﴾ الَّذِينَ هُمْ فِي صَلَاتِهِمْ خَٰشِعُونَ ﴿٢﴾
cards.x: Successful indeed are the believers: those who are humble in their prayer.
Say the opening praise: 'Subhanaka Allahumma wa bi-hamdika, wa tabaraka ismuka, wa ta'ala jadduka, wa la ilaha ghayruk.' Then seek refuge (a'udhu billah) and say bismillah quietly.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, how the prayer is put together

cards.x: Recite al-Fatihah, say 'amin' quietly, then a surah or three verses.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, how the prayer is put together

cards.x: Say 'Allahu akbar' and bow, back straight with the head level with it, holding the knees with fingers spread. Say 'Subhana rabbiya al-'azim' three times, the least of the sunnah.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, how the prayer is put together

checks.q: Where does a man place his hands after the takbir?
checks.a: Right over left, below the navel
w: Right over left, on the chest
Left over right, below the navel
checks.why: Nur al-Idah: right over left below the navel for a man; a woman places them on her chest.

checks.q: What is said straight after the opening takbir?
checks.why: The opening praise (thana') comes first, then ta'awwudh and bismillah.

checks.q: How many times is the tasbih of ruku' said at least, by the sunnah?
checks.why: Three times is the least of the sunnah.

checks.q: Where does a woman place her hands while standing in prayer?
checks.a: Right over left, on the chest
w: Right over left, below the navel
Left over right, below the navel
checks.why: A man places them below the navel; a woman on her chest, as it is more covering.

lessons.title: How to pray (2): from rising to salam
lessons.about: Prostration, sitting, tashahhud and ending the prayer.

cards.x: Rise saying 'Sami' Allahu li-man hamidah, rabbana laka al-hamd' (a follower says only the second part), and stand still for a moment.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, how the prayer is put together

cards.x: Go down with 'Allahu akbar', placing knees, then hands, then face between the hands, nose and forehead on the ground. Say 'Subhana rabbiya al-a'la' three times. Sit calmly, then make the second sujud the same way.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, how the prayer is put together

cards.x: After the second rak'ah, sit on the left foot with the right foot upright, hands on the thighs, and recite the tashahhud: 'Al-tahiyyatu lillahi wa al-salawatu wa al-tayyibat…'

In the final sitting, after the tashahhud send blessings on the Prophet ﷺ and make du'a in words like the Qur'an and the reported supplications. Then say 'al-salamu 'alaykum wa rahmatullah' to the right and to the left.

A woman raises her hands to her shoulders, places them on her chest, bows less deeply, and in sujud keeps her body together, stomach close to her thighs and arms on the ground. In the sitting she sits with both feet out to the right side. She recites quietly.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah with Maraqi al-Falah, How to pray (2): from rising to salam

checks.q: Which touches the ground first when going into sujud?
checks.why: Knees, then hands, then the face.

checks.q: What does a follower say when rising from ruku'?
checks.why: The imam or one praying alone says both; the follower says only the praise.

checks.q: What comes after the tashahhud in the final sitting?
checks.a: Blessings on the Prophet ﷺ, then du'a, then salam
w: Salam straight away, then du'a afterwards
Du'a, then blessings on the Prophet ﷺ, then salam
Another sujud, then blessings, then salam
checks.why: Al-Quduri: tashahhud, blessings on the Prophet ﷺ, du'a, then salam right and left.

checks.q: What is said three times in sujud?
checks.why: 'Subhana rabbiya al-a'la' (glory to my Lord, the Most High) in sujud; 'al-'azim' (the Magnificent) is said in ruku'.

checks.q: How does a woman sit in the tashahhud?
checks.a: Both feet out to the right side, sitting on the ground
w: On her left foot with the right upright
checks.why: A man sits on his left foot with the right upright; a woman sits with both feet out to the right.
checks.src: Nur al-Idah with Maraqi al-Falah, How to pray (2): from rising to salam

lessons.title: The five prayers, rak'ah by rak'ah
lessons.about: How many rak'ahs each prayer has, and how a whole prayer flows.

cards.x: Fard: Fajr 2, Zuhr 4, 'Asr 4, Maghrib 3, 'Isha' 4, and Jumu'ah 2 in place of Zuhr on Friday. Witr is 3 after 'Isha'. The imam recites aloud in Fajr, Jumu'ah, and the first two rak'ahs of Maghrib and 'Isha'; the rest is quiet.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah with Maraqi al-Falah, The five prayers, rak'ah by rak'ah

cards.x: Takbir, opening praise, al-Fatihah and a surah, ruku', standing, two sujud: that is one rak'ah. Stand and do the same again without the opening praise, then sit for the tashahhud, blessings on the Prophet ﷺ, du'a and salam.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah with Maraqi al-Falah, The five prayers, rak'ah by rak'ah

cards.x: After the second rak'ah, sit for the tashahhud only, then stand for the third. In the third and fourth rak'ahs of a fard prayer, recite only al-Fatihah. After the last rak'ah, sit for the final tashahhud, blessings, du'a and salam.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah with Maraqi al-Falah, The five prayers, rak'ah by rak'ah

cards.x: In sunnah and witr prayers, recite al-Fatihah and a surah in every rak'ah.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah with Maraqi al-Falah, The five prayers, rak'ah by rak'ah

checks.q: How many fard rak'ahs is Maghrib?
checks.why: Fajr 2, Zuhr 4, 'Asr 4, Maghrib 3, 'Isha' 4.

checks.q: In the third rak'ah of the fard of Zuhr, what do you recite?
checks.why: In the last two rak'ahs of a fard prayer, al-Fatihah alone is enough.

checks.q: In a four-rak'ah prayer, what happens after the second rak'ah?
checks.a: Sit for the tashahhud only, then stand
w: Recite the whole final sitting with du'a
checks.why: The first sitting is wajib: tashahhud only, then stand for the third.

checks.q: In which prayers is the imam's recitation silent?
checks.why: Zuhr and 'Asr are silent. The imam recites aloud in Fajr, Jumu'ah, the two Eids, tarawih, witr in Ramadan, and the first two rak'ahs of Maghrib and 'Isha'.

lessons.title: What you recite in prayer
lessons.about: Every word a beginner must know by heart to pray, with its meaning.

cards.x: These are the words of the prayer, in order. Al-Fatihah and a short surah are wajib; the rest are sunnah or wajib as the earlier lessons explain. Turn on Transliteration (Aa) if you cannot yet read Arabic, and learn one a day. The How to pray guide in Tools has the same words with audio.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, how the prayer is put together

cards.ar: سُبْحَانَكَ اللَّهُمَّ وَبِحَمْدِكَ، وَتَبَارَكَ اسْمُكَ، وَتَعَالَى جَدُّكَ، وَلَا إِلَهَ غَيْرُكَ
cards.x: Glory be to You, O Allah, and praise. Blessed is Your name, exalted is Your majesty, and there is no god besides You.

cards.ar: أَعُوذُ بِاللَّهِ مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ الرَّجِيمِ، بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ
cards.x: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed devil. In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Kind.

cards.ar:
بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ
الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ
الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ
مَالِكِ يَوْمِ الدِّينِ
إِيَّاكَ نَعْبُدُ وَإِيَّاكَ نَسْتَعِينُ
اهْدِنَا الصِّرَاطَ الْمُسْتَقِيمَ
صِرَاطَ الَّذِينَ أَنْعَمْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ غَيْرِ الْمَغْضُوبِ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا الضَّالِّينَ
cards.x: In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Kind. Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds, the Most Merciful, the Most Kind, Master of the Day of Judgement. You alone we worship and You alone we ask for help. Guide us on the straight path, the path of those You have blessed, not of those who earned anger, nor of those who went astray.

cards.ar:
بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ
اللَّهُ الصَّمَدُ
لَمْ يَلِدْ وَلَمْ يُولَدْ
وَلَمْ يَكُن لَّهُ كُفُوًا أَحَدٌ
cards.x: Say: He is Allah, One. Allah, the Everlasting Refuge. He does not beget, nor was He begotten, and there is none equal to Him.

cards.ar: سُبْحَانَ رَبِّيَ الْعَظِيمِ
cards.x: Glory be to my Lord, the Magnificent.

cards.ar: سَمِعَ اللَّهُ لِمَنْ حَمِدَهُ — رَبَّنَا لَكَ الْحَمْدُ
cards.x: Allah hears the one who praises Him. Our Lord, to You is all praise.

cards.ar: سُبْحَانَ رَبِّيَ الْأَعْلَى
cards.x: Glory be to my Lord, the Most High.

cards.ar: التَّحِيَّاتُ لِلَّهِ وَالصَّلَوَاتُ وَالطَّيِّبَاتُ، السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكَ أَيُّهَا النَّبِيُّ وَرَحْمَةُ اللَّهِ وَبَرَكَاتُهُ، السَّلَامُ عَلَيْنَا وَعَلَى عِبَادِ اللَّهِ الصَّالِحِينَ، أَشْهَدُ أَنْ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ، وَأَشْهَدُ أَنَّ مُحَمَّدًا عَبْدُهُ وَرَسُولُهُ
cards.x: All greetings, prayers and good things are for Allah. Peace be on you, O Prophet, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. Peace be on us and on the righteous servants of Allah. I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger.
cards.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, how to pray; Sahih al-Bukhari (831) and Muslim (402), from Ibn Mas'ud رضي الله عنه

cards.ar: اللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَعَلَى آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ، كَمَا صَلَّيْتَ عَلَى إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَعَلَى آلِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، إِنَّكَ حَمِيدٌ مَجِيدٌ، اللَّهُمَّ بَارِكْ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَعَلَى آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ، كَمَا بَارَكْتَ عَلَى إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَعَلَى آلِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، إِنَّكَ حَمِيدٌ مَجِيدٌ
cards.x: O Allah, send blessings on Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, as You sent blessings on Ibrahim and the family of Ibrahim; You are Praiseworthy, Glorious. O Allah, bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, as You blessed Ibrahim and the family of Ibrahim; You are Praiseworthy, Glorious.
cards.src: Sahih al-Bukhari (3370), from Ka'b ibn 'Ujrah رضي الله عنه

cards.ar: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي ظَلَمْتُ نَفْسِي ظُلْمًا كَثِيرًا، وَلَا يَغْفِرُ الذُّنُوبَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ، فَاغْفِرْ لِي مَغْفِرَةً مِنْ عِنْدِكَ، وَارْحَمْنِي، إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ الْغَفُورُ الرَّحِيمُ
cards.x: O Allah, I have wronged myself greatly, and none forgives sins but You. So forgive me with forgiveness from You, and have mercy on me; You are the Forgiving, the Merciful.
cards.src: Sahih al-Bukhari (834) and Muslim (2705): Abu Bakr رضي الله عنه asked for a du'a to say in his prayer, how to pray

cards.ar: السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ وَرَحْمَةُ اللَّهِ
cards.x: Peace be on you, and the mercy of Allah.

cards.ar: اللَّهُمَّ إِنَّا نَسْتَعِينُكَ، وَنَسْتَهْدِيكَ، وَنَسْتَغْفِرُكَ، وَنَتُوبُ إِلَيْكَ، وَنُؤْمِنُ بِكَ، وَنَتَوَكَّلُ عَلَيْكَ، وَنُثْنِي عَلَيْكَ الْخَيْرَ كُلَّهُ، نَشْكُرُكَ وَلَا نَكْفُرُكَ، وَنَخْلَعُ وَنَتْرُكُ مَنْ يَفْجُرُكَ، اللَّهُمَّ إِيَّاكَ نَعْبُدُ، وَلَكَ نُصَلِّي وَنَسْجُدُ، وَإِلَيْكَ نَسْعَى وَنَحْفِدُ، نَرْجُو رَحْمَتَكَ، وَنَخْشَى عَذَابَكَ، إِنَّ عَذَابَكَ الْجِدَّ بِالْكُفَّارِ مُلْحِقٌ
cards.x: O Allah, we ask You for help and guidance and forgiveness, we turn to You, believe in You and rely on You, and we praise You with all good. We thank You and are not ungrateful, and we cast off and leave whoever disobeys You. O Allah, You alone we worship, to You we pray and prostrate, to You we hasten and serve. We hope for Your mercy and fear Your punishment; Your true punishment overtakes the disbelievers.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, the wording of the qunut

checks.q: What is said in ruku'?
checks.why: 'Al-'azim' (the Magnificent) in ruku', 'al-a'la' (the Most High) in sujud.

checks.q: Which words begin the tashahhud?
checks.a: Al-tahiyyatu lillahi wa al-salawatu wa al-tayyibat
checks.why: The tashahhud of Ibn Mas'ud رضي الله عنه, which the Hanafis follow.

checks.q: Which is recited in the third rak'ah of witr before ruku'?
checks.why: The qunut is wajib in witr, said after raising the hands with takbir.
checks.src: Nur al-Idah, the wording of the qunut

lessons.title: Sunnahs and dislikes of prayer
lessons.about: What perfects the prayer, and what spoils its beauty.

cards.x: Raising the hands at the opening takbir, the opening praise (thana'), seeking refuge, bismillah, 'amin', the takbirs when moving, the glorifications in ruku' and sujud, and blessings on the Prophet ﷺ in the last sitting.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, Sunnahs and dislikes of prayer

cards.x: Playing with clothes or body, cracking the fingers, looking around, hands on the hips, yawning without covering the mouth, closing the eyes without need, and praying while needing the toilet.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, Sunnahs and dislikes of prayer

cards.x: It is disliked to pray facing a picture of a living being, on a path, in a bathroom, or with someone's face turned towards you.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, Sunnahs and dislikes of prayer

checks.q: Which of these is a sunnah of prayer?
checks.why: Al-Fatihah is wajib, the final sitting is fard, facing the qiblah is a condition; 'amin' is sunnah.

checks.q: You need the toilet badly as the prayer starts. What is best?
checks.a: Use the toilet first, then pray
checks.why: Praying while holding it in is disliked, as it takes away humility.

checks.q: Which of these is disliked in prayer?
w: Looking at the place of sujud
Keeping the feet apart a little
checks.why: The eyes stay on the place of sujud while standing.

checks.q: Is it disliked to pray facing a picture of a living being?
w: No, if it is a photo
checks.why: Nur al-Idah lists it among what is disliked.

lessons.title: The prostration of forgetfulness
lessons.about: How to fix a mistake in prayer.

cards.x: Sajdat al-sahw, the prostration of forgetfulness, is two extra prostrations at the end of the prayer that repair a mistake, such as forgetting the first sitting.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, sujud al-sahw: its ruling

cards.x: Two prostrations, with tashahhud and salam, become wajib when a wajib act of the prayer is left out by mistake, even if it happens more than once.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, sujud al-sahw: its ruling

cards.x: The sunnah is to do it after the salam: give one salam to the right, make the two sujud, then sit for tashahhud and end with salam. Doing it before salam is mildly disliked.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, the time of the prostration

cards.x: If a wajib act is left on purpose, the person is sinful and the prayer must be repeated; the prostration of forgetfulness does not fix it.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, leaving a wajib on purpose

cards.x: If this is the first time you have ever had such a doubt, start the prayer again. If it happens to you often, go with what you think most likely. If you cannot decide, take the smaller number, sit after each rak'ah that could be the last, and make sajdat al-sahw.
cards.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, The prostration of forgetfulness

checks.q: What is sajdat al-sahw?
checks.a: Two prostrations at the end of the prayer to repair a mistake
w: One prostration on reciting certain verses
A short voluntary prayer at night
A prostration made out of thanks
checks.why: It repairs a wajib act left out by mistake.

checks.q: By the sunnah, when is the prostration of forgetfulness (sajdat al-sahw) made?
checks.a: After one salam to the right
w: In the middle of the prayer
checks.why: Give one salam to the right, two sujud, then tashahhud and salam.

checks.q: What makes the prostration of forgetfulness (sajdat al-sahw) wajib?
checks.a: Leaving a wajib act by mistake
checks.why: It repairs a forgotten wajib. A missed pillar needs the prayer repeated.

checks.q: You left a wajib act of prayer on purpose. What follows?
checks.a: You are sinful and repeat the prayer
w: Nothing is needed, it was small
Pray two extra rak'ahs at the end
checks.why: The prostration is for mistakes, not deliberate omissions.

checks.q: You often doubt whether you prayed three or four. What do you do?
checks.a: Go with what you think most likely
w: Make sajdat al-sahw and give salam straight away
checks.why: Restarting is for the first time it ever happens. If it is frequent, act on your strongest thought.
checks.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, The prostration of forgetfulness

lessons.title: The prostration of recitation
lessons.about: Fourteen verses of the Qur'an call for a prostration: who owes it, and how to make it.

cards.x: There are fourteen places in the Qur'an where whoever recites the verse, or hears it, makes one prostration. In the Hanafi school this prostration is wajib. The places are marked in the mushaf with the sign ۩.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, prostration of recitation: its cause, ruling and time

cards.ar: فَمَا لَهُمْ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ ﴿٢٠﴾ وَإِذَا قُرِئَ عَلَيْهِمُ الْقُرْءَانُ لَا يَسْجُدُونَ ﴿٢١﴾
cards.x: So what is the matter with them that they do not believe, and when the Qur'an is recited to them, they do not prostrate?
The Prophet ﷺ prostrated when he ﷺ finished reciting Surat al-Najm, and the Muslims with him ﷺ prostrated too.
cards.src: Sahih al-Bukhari (4856), The prostration of recitation

cards.x: In al-A'raf, al-Ra'd, al-Nahl, al-Isra', Maryam, the first one in al-Hajj, al-Furqan, al-Naml, al-Sajdah, Sad, Fussilat (Ha-Mim al-Sajdah), al-Najm, al-Inshiqaq and al-'Alaq (Iqra').
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, the verses of prostration

cards.x: The one who recites the verse, and anyone who hears it, even without meaning to listen. A woman in menstruation or post-natal bleeding does not owe it. Hearing an echo does not make it due, and many Hanafi scholars say the same of a recording; prostrating anyway is good.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, on whom it is wajib, and on whom not

cards.x: With wudu, clothes covered and facing the qiblah, as for prayer: say 'Allahu akbar' and go straight down into one prostration, say 'Subhana rabbiya al-a'la' three times, then say 'Allahu akbar' and rise. There is no raising of the hands, no tashahhud and no salam.
cards.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, the prostration of recitation

cards.x: If you recite the verse in prayer, the best is to go down at once into a prostration for it, rise, and carry on reciting. If you go into the prayer's own ruku' or sujud within two or three verses, that also covers it. A prostration owed inside the prayer cannot be made up after it.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, how and when it is performed

cards.x: Outside the prayer it may be delayed, but doing it straight away is better; delaying is mildly disliked. Repeating the same verse in one sitting needs only one prostration. Reading it again after getting up and moving on needs another.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, how and when it is performed

checks.q: You read a verse of prostration from the mushaf at home. In the Hanafi school the prostration is…
checks.why: It is wajib on the reciter and on whoever hears the verse.
checks.src: Nur al-Idah, prostration of recitation: its cause, ruling and time

checks.q: How is the prostration of recitation made outside the prayer?
w: One prostration, with no wudu needed
checks.why: Takbir, one prostration saying Subhana rabbiya al-a'la, takbir rising; no tashahhud or salam.
checks.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, the prostration of recitation

checks.q: You repeat the same verse of prostration three times while memorising, in one sitting. You owe…
w: None, since it was for memorising
checks.why: One sitting, one verse: one prostration.
checks.src: Nur al-Idah, how and when it is performed

checks.q: Who does not owe the prostration on hearing the verse?
w: Someone who did not mean to listen
checks.why: Menstruation and post-natal bleeding lift it; hearing without meaning to does not.
checks.src: Nur al-Idah, on whom it is wajib, and on whom not

lessons.title: Praying when you are ill
lessons.about: The prayer is never dropped while you can still pray in some way: here is how.

cards.x: As long as a person is conscious and can at least move his head, the prayer stays due on time. Illness changes how he prays, not whether he prays. Each easier way is used only when the one before it is truly hard.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, how the sick person prays

cards.ar: فَاتَّقُواْ اللَّهَ مَا اسْتَطَعْتُمْ وَاسْمَعُواْ وَأَطِيعُواْ وَأَنفِقُواْ خَيْرٗا لِّأَنفُسِكُمْ وَمَن يُوقَ شُحَّ نَفْسِهِ فَأُوْلَـٰٓئِكَ هُمُ الْمُفْلِحُونَ ﴿١٦﴾
cards.x: So be mindful of Allah as much as you are able, listen, obey and spend for your own good. Whoever is saved from the greed of his own soul, it is they who succeed.

If standing is impossible, or causes severe pain, or will make the illness worse or slower to heal, pray sitting, with ruku' and sujud, sitting in whatever way is easiest. If you can stand for part of it, even just the opening takbir, stand for that much.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, how the sick person prays

cards.x: If ruku' and sujud are impossible, pray sitting and make them by bending the head, lowering it further for sujud than for ruku'. If sujud is not lower, it is not valid. Do not raise a cushion or object to your face to prostrate on.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, how the sick person prays

cards.x: In the Hanafi school, someone who can stand but cannot prostrate on the ground no longer has to stand: he may pray the whole prayer sitting, gesturing for ruku' and sujud. Sitting on a chair is allowed when sitting on the floor is hard.

If even sitting is too hard, pray lying on the back with the feet towards the qiblah and the head raised on a pillow so the face looks towards the qiblah, knees raised if possible; or lying on the right side facing the qiblah. On the back is better. Gesture with the head.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, how the sick person prays

cards.x: Do not gesture with the eyes, eyebrows or heart. If a person cannot even move his head, the prayers wait: if this lasts a day and a night or less, he makes them up when able; if it lasts longer than five prayers, they are dropped, according to the view the fatwa is on.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, how the sick person prays

cards.x: If water will harm you, make tayammum. Wipe over a cast or dressing you cannot remove. If someone cannot clean his clothes or turn to the qiblah and has nobody to help, he prays as he is and does not miss the time.

checks.q: Standing causes you severe pain. You…
checks.a: Pray sitting, with ruku' and sujud
w: Leave the prayer until you recover
checks.why: Severe pain is enough to pray sitting; ruku' and sujud stay if you can make them.
checks.src: Nur al-Idah, how the sick person prays

checks.q: Praying sitting by gestures, sujud must be…
checks.why: If sujud is not lower than ruku', it is not valid.
checks.src: Nur al-Idah, how the sick person prays

checks.q: You can stand but cannot get down to the floor. In the Hanafi school you may…
checks.a: Pray the whole prayer sitting, gesturing
w: Stand, and leave out ruku' and sujud
checks.why: If prostration is impossible, standing is no longer required.

checks.q: A patient cannot move even his head for two days, though he is awake. His missed prayers…
w: Are prayed for him by his family
checks.why: Complete inability for more than a day and a night (five prayers) drops them, on the view the fatwa is on.
checks.src: Nur al-Idah, how the sick person prays

lessons.title: What breaks the prayer
lessons.about: Speech, food, movement and replies that end a prayer.

cards.x: Speaking breaks the prayer, even by forgetfulness or mistake.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, what breaks the prayer

cards.x: Eating or drinking anything, even a little, breaks it.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, what breaks the prayer

cards.x: A lot of movement, or turning the chest away from the qiblah, breaks it.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, what breaks the prayer

cards.x: Returning a greeting, or replying to someone with words such as 'al-hamdu lillah' as an answer, breaks it.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, what breaks the prayer

checks.q: You forgot you were praying and said a word. Is the prayer broken?
w: Yes, if it was a long sentence
No, if no one heard it
checks.why: Speaking breaks the prayer even if you forgot or it was a mistake.
checks.src: Nur al-Idah, what breaks the prayer

checks.q: Someone greets you while you pray. If you reply 'wa 'alaykum al-salam'…
w: It is fine if said quietly
checks.why: Returning a greeting while praying breaks the prayer.
checks.src: Nur al-Idah, what breaks the prayer

checks.q: Which breaks the prayer?
checks.a: Turning the chest away from the qiblah
w: Glancing to the side without turning
checks.why: Turning the chest away from the qiblah breaks the prayer.
checks.src: Nur al-Idah, what breaks the prayer

checks.q: Does weeping in prayer out of fear of Allah break the prayer?
checks.why: Weeping at the mention of Paradise or the Fire does not break it; crying aloud from pain or worldly grief does.

lessons.title: Witr
lessons.about: Its ruling, how it is prayed, and the qunut.

cards.x: In the Hanafi school, the witr prayer is wajib.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, chapter on witr and qunut

cards.x: Witr is three rak'ahs with one salam at the end, and a surah after al-Fatihah in every rak'ah.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, chapter on witr and qunut

cards.x: In the third rak'ah, before bowing, say 'Allahu akbar', raise the hands and recite the qunut.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, chapter on witr and qunut

checks.q: In the Hanafi school, witr is…
checks.why: In the Hanafi school, witr is wajib.
checks.src: Nur al-Idah, chapter on witr and qunut

checks.q: How many rak'ahs is witr in the Hanafi school?
w: Two, then one with its own salam
checks.why: Witr is three rak'ahs, ending with one salam: the closing 'al-salamu 'alaykum wa rahmatullah' to the right and left that ends the prayer.
checks.src: Nur al-Idah, chapter on witr and qunut

checks.q: When is the qunut recited in witr?
checks.a: In the third rak'ah, before bowing
w: In the third rak'ah, after bowing
In the second rak'ah, before bowing
After the salam, with raised hands
checks.why: In the third rak'ah, before bowing, say 'Allahu akbar', raise the hands and recite the qunut.
checks.src: Nur al-Idah, chapter on witr and qunut

checks.q: Until when may witr be prayed?
w: Until the first third of the night ends
checks.why: Its time is after 'Isha' until true dawn; the end of the night is best for one sure to wake.

lessons.title: The regular sunnah prayers
lessons.about: The sunnahs the Prophet ﷺ kept with the five prayers, and tarawih.

cards.x: Two rak'ahs before Fajr (the most important), four before Zuhr and two after, two after Maghrib, two after 'Isha', and four before Jumu'ah and four after it.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, The regular sunnah prayers

cards.x: Four before 'Asr, four before 'Isha' and six after Maghrib are recommended, not stressed.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, The regular sunnah prayers

cards.x: In Ramadan, twenty rak'ahs after 'Isha', in sets of two, is a stressed sunnah for men and women. Praying it in congregation is a sunnah too.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, The regular sunnah prayers

checks.q: Which is the most important sunnah prayer?
checks.why: The Prophet ﷺ never left them, even when travelling.

checks.q: How many stressed sunnah rak'ahs are there before Zuhr?
checks.why: Four before Zuhr and two after.

checks.q: How many rak'ahs is tarawih in the Hanafi school?
checks.why: Twenty rak'ahs, as the Companions prayed in the time of 'Umar رضي الله عنه.

checks.q: Which sunnah comes after Maghrib?
checks.why: Two stressed rak'ahs after Maghrib.

lessons.title: Recommended prayers: awwabin, tahajjud, duha
lessons.about: The extra prayers Nur al-Idah recommends beyond the sunnahs: after Maghrib, at night, in the forenoon, on entering the masjid, and for a decision.

cards.x: Besides the fard, wajib and stressed sunnah prayers, Nur al-Idah lists prayers that are recommended (mandub). They carry great reward for whoever keeps them, and there is no sin in leaving them.

Nur al-Idah recommends six rak'ahs after Maghrib, prayed in twos. They are known as salat al-awwabin, the prayer of those who often turn back to Allah. Many scholars count the two sunnah rak'ahs of Maghrib among the six.
It is also recommended to pray four rak'ahs before 'Asr, and four before and four after 'Isha'.

Prayer at night is better than prayer in the day, and long standing is more beloved than many prostrations. Allah says: 'And in part of the night, pray tahajjud, as an extra for you' (al-Isra' 79). It is best in the last part of the night, after some sleep.

Nur al-Idah recommends four rak'ahs or more at Duha, the forenoon, from when the sun has risen well until shortly before midday. Prayed early, soon after sunrise, it is often called ishraq: whoever prays Fajr in congregation, stays in dhikr until sunrise, then prays two rak'ahs, has the reward of a complete Hajj and 'umrah (al-Tirmidhi).

cards.t: Greeting the masjid and after wudu
cards.x: It is sunnah to greet the masjid with two rak'ahs before sitting; a fard or any other prayer prayed on entering takes their place. Two rak'ahs after wudu, before it dries, are also recommended.

When you face a decision, pray two rak'ahs and then the du'a of istikharah, asking Allah to choose what is best. For a need, pray two rak'ahs of hajah and then ask Allah. Both are recommended in Nur al-Idah.

checks.q: How many rak'ahs are recommended after Maghrib (salat al-awwabin)?
checks.why: Six rak'ahs after Maghrib, in twos; many count the two sunnah rak'ahs among them.

checks.q: When is tahajjud best prayed?
checks.a: In the last part of the night, after some sleep
w: Just before the time of 'Isha' comes in
After Fajr, before the sun rises
checks.why: The night prayer is better than prayer in the day, and its best time is the last part of the night. After Fajr until sunrise, extra prayers are disliked.

checks.q: How many rak'ahs of Duha are recommended?
checks.why: Nur al-Idah says: four or more at Duha.

checks.q: You enter the masjid as the fard prayer starts, and join it. What about the two rak'ahs of greeting the masjid?
checks.a: The fard prayer takes their place
w: They are missed for that visit
checks.why: Any prayer prayed on entering, fard or sunnah, counts as greeting the masjid, even without intending it.

checks.q: Which prayer of two rak'ahs is prayed when facing a decision?
checks.why: Istikharah: two rak'ahs, then asking Allah to choose what is best for your religion and your life.

lessons.title: Praying in congregation
lessons.about: Its ruling, who leads, and following the imam.

cards.x: Praying in congregation is a stressed sunnah.
The most entitled to lead is the one who knows the sunnah best; if equal, the best reciter; then the most scrupulous; then the oldest.
Whoever joins another's prayer needs two intentions: the prayer itself and following the imam. In the Hanafi school the follower does not recite behind the imam.

If you join while the imam is in ruku' and bow before he rises, you have caught that rak'ah. If you join after he rises, that rak'ah is not counted. Do not give salam with the imam: when he finishes, stand and make up the rak'ahs you missed. A traveller behind a resident imam prays four.

checks.q: Who has most right to lead the prayer?
checks.a: The one who knows the sunnah best
w: The best reciter of the Qur'an
The one with the best voice
checks.why: Al-Quduri puts knowledge of the sunnah first, then recitation, then scrupulousness, then age.

checks.q: Does a follower recite al-Fatihah behind the imam in the Hanafi school?
checks.why: Al-Quduri: the follower does not recite behind the imam.

checks.q: What two intentions does a follower need?
checks.a: The prayer and following the imam
w: The prayer and the time of the prayer
Following the imam and facing the qiblah
The prayer only; following needs none
checks.why: Two intentions: the prayer and following.

checks.q: Where does a single follower stand when praying with an imam?
checks.why: One follower stands on the imam's right; two or more stand behind.

checks.q: You reach the imam after he has risen from ruku'. Have you caught that rak'ah?
checks.a: No; make it up after the imam finishes
w: Yes, joining at any point counts
Yes, if you say the takbir quickly
Yes, if the imam is still standing
checks.why: A rak'ah is caught by joining the ruku'. After the imam's salam, stand and complete what you missed.

checks.q: You joined late. When the imam gives salam, you…
checks.a: Stand and make up what you missed
checks.why: Do not give salam with the imam; complete your missed rak'ahs, then give salam.

lessons.title: The traveller's prayer
lessons.about: When to shorten, and for how long.

cards.x: Someone who sets out intending a journey of three days (about 77 km by the usual modern estimate) shortens the four-rak'ah fard prayers (Zuhr, 'Asr and 'Isha') to two, once he has passed the buildings of his town.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, shortening the prayer; conditions of travel

cards.ar: وَإِذَا ضَرَبْتُمْ فِي الْأَرْضِ فَلَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ جُنَاحٌ أَن تَقْصُرُواْ مِنَ الصَّلَوٰةِ إِنْ خِفْتُمْ أَن يَفْتِنَكُمُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوٓاْ إِنَّ الْكَٰفِرِينَ كَانُواْ لَكُمْ عَدُوّٗا مُّبِينٗا ﴿١٠١﴾
cards.x: When you travel in the land, there is no blame on you if you shorten the prayer…
In the Hanafi school shortening is required ('azimah), not just allowed. A traveller who prays four on purpose is sinful; if he did not sit after the second rak'ah, the fard is not valid.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, the ruling of shortening

cards.x: He keeps shortening until he returns home or intends to stay fifteen days or more in one town. If he intends less, or does not know when he will leave, he keeps shortening even for years.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, the period of shortening

checks.q: Which prayers does a traveller shorten?
checks.why: They become two rak'ahs. Fajr and Maghrib stay as they are.

checks.q: How far must a journey be for prayers to be shortened?
w: Any trip outside your town, about 5 km
checks.why: Al-Quduri: three days' travel at a normal pace, commonly estimated today at about 77 km.

checks.q: A traveller arrives in a town. How long must he intend to stay to stop shortening?
checks.why: Intending fifteen days or more in one town ends the travel ruling.

checks.q: In the Hanafi school, is shortening the prayer while travelling optional?
checks.why: Shortening is 'azimah (the rule), not just a permission.

lessons.title: Making up missed prayers
lessons.about: Missed prayers stay owed until made up.

cards.x: A missed prayer must be made up. A prayer missed while travelling is made up as two rak'ahs, and one missed at home as four, whenever it is made up.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, making up missed prayers

cards.x: Someone who owes fewer than six prayers must make them up in order, before the current prayer. The order falls away if the time is too short, if he forgot he owed them, or once six or more prayers are owed.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, the ruling of order

cards.x: Leaving a prayer deliberately out of laziness is so serious that the jurists set a punishment for it in an Islamic state. Make up what you missed, and repent.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, the one who leaves the prayer

checks.q: You missed 'Asr while travelling and make it up at home. How many rak'ahs?
checks.why: A prayer is made up as it was missed: two for a traveller.

checks.q: You owe two missed prayers. Must you make them up in order, before the current prayer?
checks.a: Yes, while you owe fewer than six
checks.why: Order is required for one who owes fewer than six, unless time is short or he forgot.

checks.q: What happens to a prayer that was missed?
checks.a: It stays owed and must be made up
w: It is forgiven if you repent
It is dropped after a year
checks.why: Make it up, and repent if it was missed deliberately.

lessons.title: The Jumu'ah prayer
lessons.about: Who must attend, and the khutbah.

cards.x: Jumu'ah is fard on a man who is free, resident in a town, healthy, safe, able to see and able to walk.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, Jumu'ah: conditions of obligation

cards.ar: يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْ إِذَا نُودِيَ لِلصَّلَوٰةِ مِن يَوْمِ الْجُمُعَةِ فَاسْعَوْاْ إِلَىٰ ذِكْرِ اللَّهِ وَذَرُواْ الْبَيْعَ ذَٰلِكُمْ خَيْرٞ لَّكُمْ إِن كُنتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ ﴿٩﴾
cards.x: O you who believe, when the call is made for the prayer on Friday, hasten to the remembrance of Allah and leave off trade. That is better for you, if only you knew.

Its sunnahs include purity, standing, facing the people, beginning with praise of Allah, the two testimonies, blessings on the Prophet ﷺ, admonition, reciting a verse, and two khutbahs with a sitting between them.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, the khutbah and its sunnahs

cards.x: Women and travellers do not have to attend. If someone not obliged attends and prays it, it counts in place of Zuhr.

Jumu'ah replaces Zuhr for that day. Once the imam comes out for the khutbah, there is no voluntary prayer and no talking: listen in silence, even if you cannot hear. Even telling someone 'be quiet' is not allowed.

checks.q: Is Jumu'ah fard on a traveller?
w: Yes, if he is near a masjid
checks.why: Residence is one of its conditions of obligation.

checks.q: How many khutbahs are given, by the sunnah?
checks.a: Two, with a sitting between them
checks.why: Two khutbahs with a sitting in between are among its sunnahs.

checks.q: A woman attends Jumu'ah and prays it. Then…
checks.a: It counts in place of Zuhr
checks.why: If those not obliged attend and pray it, it is valid for them in place of Zuhr.

checks.q: Who must attend Jumu'ah?
checks.a: Every free, resident, healthy adult Muslim man
w: Every adult Muslim, man or woman
Every Muslim man, resident or travelling
Every free Muslim man, ill or healthy
checks.why: Women, travellers and the ill are excused; if they attend, it counts in place of Zuhr.

lessons.title: The funeral prayer
lessons.about: Its ruling, conditions and how it is prayed.

cards.x: Praying over a Muslim who has died is fard kifayah: if some pray it, the rest are excused. Its pillars are the takbirs and standing.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, the funeral prayer: ruling and pillars

cards.x: The deceased must be Muslim, washed, present and placed in front of the people, on the ground.

Four takbirs. After the first, praise Allah; after the second, send blessings on the Prophet ﷺ; after the third, make du'a for the deceased; after the fourth, give salam. The imam stands level with the chest.

checks.q: The funeral prayer is…
checks.why: If some pray it, the obligation is lifted from the rest.

checks.q: What is said after the third takbir?
checks.why: First praise, second blessings, third du'a, fourth salam.

checks.q: How many takbirs are in the funeral prayer?
checks.why: The prayer is four takbirs and standing.

checks.q: What is recited after the first takbir of the funeral prayer?
checks.why: After the first takbir the thana', after the second the blessings on the Prophet ﷺ, after the third du'a, then salam after the fourth.

lessons.title: When someone dies
lessons.about: What to do from the last moments to the burial, and what follows.

cards.x: Turn the dying person towards the qiblah on the right side, and say the Shahadah gently near them so they may remember it, without pressing them to repeat it.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, what is done for one who is dying

cards.ar: الَّذِينَ إِذَآ أَصَٰبَتْهُم مُّصِيبَةٞ قَالُوٓاْ إِنَّا لِلَّهِ وَإِنَّآ إِلَيْهِ رَٰجِعُونَ ﴿١٥٦﴾
cards.x: …those who, when struck by a calamity, say: 'Truly we belong to Allah, and to Him we return.'
Close the eyes, tie the jaw, straighten the limbs and cover the body. Say: 'Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un.' Hurry to wash, pray over and bury him, and settle his debts quickly.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, what is done when he dies

cards.x: Washing the deceased is fard kifayah. Men wash men and women wash women. A wife may wash her husband, but in the Hanafi school a husband does not wash his wife. Give him wudu first without rinsing the mouth and nose, then wash an odd number of times.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, preparing and washing him

cards.x: The sunnah shroud is white: three cloths for a man (a wrap, a long shirt and an outer sheet) and five for a woman (those three, a headscarf and a chest cloth).
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, the shroud according to the Shari'ah

cards.x: After the funeral prayer, carry the bier quickly. Lay him in the grave on his right side facing the qiblah, saying 'Bismillahi wa 'ala millati Rasulillah.' Building over graves for show is disliked.

Weeping is allowed; wailing, tearing clothes and striking oneself are forbidden. Condolence is sunnah for three days. From his wealth come first the funeral costs, then his debts, then any bequest up to a third, then the shares of inheritance. A widow keeps an 'iddah of four months and ten days.

checks.q: How is the deceased laid in the grave?
checks.a: On the right side, facing the qiblah
w: On the back, feet to the qiblah
checks.why: Facing the qiblah on the right side, saying 'Bismillahi wa 'ala millati Rasulillah'.

checks.q: How many cloths make the sunnah shroud for a man?
checks.why: Three for a man, five for a woman.
checks.src: Nur al-Idah, the shroud according to the Shari'ah

checks.q: From a deceased's wealth, what is paid after the funeral costs?
checks.why: Funeral costs, then debts, then a bequest up to a third, then inheritance.

checks.q: Crying at a death is…
checks.why: Tears are a mercy; the Prophet ﷺ wept. Wailing, striking the face and tearing clothes are forbidden.

checks.q: What is the 'iddah of a widow who is not pregnant?
checks.why: Al-Baqarah 234 sets four months and ten days.

lessons.title: The two Eid prayers
lessons.about: Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha: how the prayer is done.

cards.x: The Eid prayer is wajib on those for whom Jumu'ah is fard. It is two rak'ahs, prayed after sunrise until midday, with the khutbah after the prayer.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, The two Eid prayers

cards.x: In the first rak'ah, after the opening praise, say three extra takbirs raising the hands, then recite. In the second, recite, then say three extra takbirs before going into ruku'.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, The two Eid prayers

cards.x: Ghusl, wearing your best clothes, perfume, and saying the takbir. Eat something sweet, like dates, before Eid al-Fitr; on Eid al-Adha, delay eating until after the prayer.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, The two Eid prayers

checks.q: What is the ruling of the Eid prayer in the Hanafi school?
checks.why: Wajib on those for whom Jumu'ah is fard.

checks.q: How many extra takbirs are in each rak'ah of the Eid prayer?
checks.why: Three in the first before reciting, three in the second before ruku'.

checks.q: Is the Eid khutbah before or after the prayer?
checks.why: Unlike Jumu'ah, the Eid khutbah comes after the prayer.

checks.q: What is sunnah before going out on Eid al-Fitr?
checks.why: On Eid al-Adha, eating is delayed until after the prayer.

lessons.title: Ramadan: who fasts and how it begins
lessons.about: Conditions, the intention and sighting the moon.

cards.x: Fasting Ramadan is fard on every Muslim who is sane and has reached puberty.

cards.ar: يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ كُتِبَ عَلَيْكُمُ الصِّيَامُ كَمَا كُتِبَ عَلَى الَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِكُمْ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَتَّقُونَ ﴿١٨٣﴾
cards.x: O you who believe, fasting is prescribed for you as it was prescribed for those before you, so that you may become mindful of Allah.

cards.ar: شَهْرُ رَمَضَانَ الَّذِيٓ أُنزِلَ فِيهِ الْقُرْءَانُ هُدٗى لِّلنَّاسِ وَبَيِّنَٰتٖ مِّنَ الْهُدَىٰ وَالْفُرْقَانِ فَمَن شَهِدَ مِنكُمُ الشَّهْرَ فَلْيَصُمْهُ وَمَن كَانَ مَرِيضًا أَوْ عَلَىٰ سَفَرٖ فَعِدَّةٞ مِّنْ أَيَّامٍ أُخَرَ يُرِيدُ اللَّهُ بِكُمُ الْيُسْرَ وَلَا يُرِيدُ بِكُمُ الْعُسْرَ وَلِتُكْمِلُواْ الْعِدَّةَ وَلِتُكَبِّرُواْ اللَّهَ عَلَىٰ مَا هَدَىٰكُمْ وَلَعَلَّكُمْ تَشْكُرُونَ ﴿١٨٥﴾
cards.x: The month of Ramadan, in which the Qur'an was sent down… whoever of you witnesses the month, let him fast it.
Its essence is holding back from eating, drinking and intercourse from true dawn to sunset, with the intention.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, its pillar; Mukhtasar al-Quduri, Book of Fasting

cards.x: For a Ramadan fast, the intention is valid from the night until before the middle of the day (midway between dawn and sunset). But for a make-up (qada') fast or an expiation fast, the intention must be made before dawn.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, fasts that need no fixed intention

cards.x: Ramadan begins by sighting its crescent, or by completing thirty days of Sha'ban if the sky is cloudy.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, how Ramadan is established

checks.q: Until when can you make the intention for a Ramadan fast?
checks.a: Before the middle of the day
checks.why: Nur al-Idah: from the night until before the 'great forenoon', the middle of the day.

checks.q: If the moon cannot be seen on the 29th of Sha'ban…
checks.why: Ramadan is established by sighting or by completing thirty days.

checks.q: Fasting means holding back from…
checks.a: Eating, drinking and intercourse from dawn to sunset
w: Eating and drinking only, from dawn to sunset
Eating, drinking and talking, from dawn to dusk
Food only, from sunrise to sunset
checks.why: That is the pillar of the fast, with the intention.

checks.q: When does the fast begin each day?
w: When the Fajr prayer is prayed in the masjid
checks.why: The fast runs from true dawn, the light spreading across the horizon, until sunset. False dawn is an earlier, upright light that does not count.

checks.q: You are making up a missed Ramadan fast. When must you intend it?
checks.why: The midday allowance is for Ramadan itself. A make-up fast needs the intention before dawn.
checks.src: Nur al-Idah with Maraqi al-Falah, Ramadan: who fasts and how it begins

lessons.title: What does not break the fast
lessons.about: Forgetting, kohl, dust and other things that leave your fast intact.

cards.x: If you eat, drink or have intercourse having forgotten you are fasting, your fast is not broken.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, what does not break the fast

cards.x: Applying kohl or oil, smoke or dust entering the throat without your doing, and waking up in a state of janabah do not break the fast.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, what does not break the fast

cards.x: Backbiting does not break the fast, but it ruins its reward. Guard your tongue while fasting.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, what does not break the fast

cards.x: Forgetting is excused, but a mistake is not: if water slips down your throat while rinsing in wudu, the fast is broken and you make it up. Swallowing your own saliva, eye drops, a blood test and, according to most contemporary Hanafi scholars, an injection do not break it. An asthma inhaler, deliberately inhaling smoke and deliberately vomiting a mouthful do break it.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, Chapter on what breaks the fast

checks.q: You forgot you were fasting and drank water. Your fast…
w: Is broken and must be made up
checks.why: Eating or drinking having forgotten you are fasting does not break the fast.
checks.src: Nur al-Idah, what does not break the fast

checks.q: Does applying kohl break the fast?
w: Yes, if done in the day
checks.why: Applying kohl does not break the fast.
checks.src: Nur al-Idah, what does not break the fast

checks.q: Waking up in janabah while fasting…
w: Makes the fast disliked and void
checks.why: Waking up in a state of janabah does not break the fast. Make ghusl for the prayer.
checks.src: Nur al-Idah, what does not break the fast

checks.q: Does using a miswak break the fast?
checks.why: The miswak is sunnah at any time of the fasting day in the Hanafi school.

checks.q: While rinsing your mouth in wudu, water slips down your throat. Your fast…
checks.a: Is broken; make up one day
w: Is fine, it was a mistake
Is fine if it was a little
checks.why: Forgetting is excused; a mistake is not. One make-up day, no expiation.
checks.src: Nur al-Idah with Maraqi al-Falah, What does not break the fast

lessons.title: Breaking the fast on purpose
lessons.about: When a make-up day is enough, and when the expiation is due.

cards.x: Deliberately eating, drinking, or having intercourse during a Ramadan fast, with no excuse and not forced, requires a make-up day and the expiation.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, what breaks the fast and requires expiation

cards.x: Fast two months in a row. If you truly cannot, feed sixty poor people two meals each, or give their value.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, what breaks the fast and requires expiation

cards.x: Some things break the fast but need only a make-up day, such as swallowing a pebble, or medicine reaching the stomach.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, what breaks the fast and requires expiation

checks.q: Someone eats on purpose in Ramadan with no excuse. What is due?
checks.a: A make-up day and the expiation
checks.why: Deliberately eating in Ramadan with no excuse requires both a make-up day and the expiation.
checks.src: Nur al-Idah, what breaks the fast and requires expiation

checks.q: The expiation for breaking a Ramadan fast, for one who can fast, is…
checks.a: Fasting two months in a row
checks.why: The expiation is fasting two months in a row. Feeding sixty poor people is only for one who truly cannot fast.
checks.src: Nur al-Idah, what breaks the fast and requires expiation

checks.q: Swallowing a small pebble while fasting requires…
checks.why: Swallowing a pebble breaks the fast but needs only a make-up day, not the expiation.
checks.src: Nur al-Idah, what breaks the fast and requires expiation

checks.q: In the expiation for breaking a Ramadan fast, what if you cannot fast two months in a row?
w: Give its value to one poor person
checks.why: Two months of fasting in a row; if unable, feeding sixty poor people.

lessons.title: Who may leave the fast
lessons.about: Travellers, the ill, menstruation and the very old.

cards.x: A traveller and someone who is ill may break the fast and make it up later.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, excuses for not fasting; the fidyah

cards.x: A woman in menstruation or post-natal bleeding does not fast, and makes up the days later. She does not make up the prayers.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, excuses for not fasting; the fidyah

cards.x: Someone too old to fast who will not become able gives a fidyah for each day instead.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, excuses for not fasting; the fidyah

cards.x: A pregnant or nursing woman who fears harm to herself or her child may leave the fast and makes it up later, with no fidyah. A traveller may break the fast, but fasting is better if it is not a hardship.
cards.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, Who may leave the fast

checks.q: A woman misses fasts because of menstruation. She…
checks.why: She makes up the fasts later. She does not make up the prayers.
checks.src: Nur al-Idah, excuses for not fasting; the fidyah

checks.q: Who may break the fast and make it up later?
checks.why: A traveller may break the fast and make it up later, as may someone who is ill.
checks.src: Nur al-Idah, excuses for not fasting; the fidyah

checks.q: A very old person who cannot fast…
checks.a: Gives a fidyah for each day
checks.why: Someone too old to fast, who will not become able, gives a fidyah for each day.
checks.src: Nur al-Idah, excuses for not fasting; the fidyah

checks.q: A sick person who expects to recover misses fasts. What applies?
checks.a: He makes them up when he recovers
w: He pays fidyah for each day
checks.why: Fidyah is for one who will not be able to fast again; one who will recover makes up the days.

checks.q: A nursing mother fears fasting will harm her baby. What applies?
checks.a: She may leave it and make up the days later
w: She pays fidyah and never makes up
checks.why: She makes up the days later, with no fidyah.
checks.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, Who may leave the fast

lessons.title: Who pays zakat
lessons.about: Who owes zakat, the nisab, and what happens with debts.

cards.x: Zakat is fard on a free, adult, sane Muslim who fully owns the nisab, once a full (lunar) year has passed on it.

cards.ar: وَأَقِيمُواْ الصَّلَوٰةَ وَءَاتُواْ الزَّكَوٰةَ وَارْكَعُواْ مَعَ الرَّـٰكِعِينَ ﴿٤٣﴾
cards.x: Establish the prayer, give the zakat, and bow with those who bow.

cards.ar: يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْ إِنَّ كَثِيرٗا مِّنَ الْأَحْبَارِ وَالرُّهْبَانِ لَيَأْكُلُونَ أَمْوَٰلَ النَّاسِ بِالْبَٰطِلِ وَيَصُدُّونَ عَن سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ وَالَّذِينَ يَكْنِزُونَ الذَّهَبَ وَالْفِضَّةَ وَلَا يُنفِقُونَهَا فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ فَبَشِّرْهُم بِعَذَابٍ أَلِيمٖ ﴿٣٤﴾
cards.x: …those who hoard gold and silver and do not spend it in the way of Allah: give them tidings of a painful punishment.
The nisab is the minimum wealth on which zakat is due: 200 dirhams of silver (about 612 g) or 20 mithqals of gold (about 87.5 g), or the same value in money or trade goods.
Take away what you owe. If what remains still reaches the nisab, zakat is due on it.

Count cash, savings, gold and silver (including jewellery worn every day, in the Hanafi school) and goods bought to sell. Your home, car, furniture and clothes for use are not counted. Gold, silver and cash are added together. For money, many Hanafi scholars today use the silver nisab, as it is better for the poor.

checks.q: When does zakat become due on your wealth?
checks.a: A lunar year after owning the nisab
w: As soon as you own the nisab
At the start of every Ramadan
Once a month on what you earn
checks.why: The nisab is the minimum amount. Zakat is due after a lunar year with it.

checks.q: The nisab is the minimum wealth for zakat. What is the nisab of gold?
checks.why: Gold: 20 mithqals (about 87.5 g). Silver: 200 dirhams (about 612 g).

checks.q: A person has the nisab but also owes debts. What happens?
checks.a: Debts come off first; zakat is due if the rest reaches the nisab
w: Debts are ignored; zakat is due on everything
Zakat is paid first; debts are paid from the rest
No zakat is due at all while any debt remains
checks.why: Subtract what you owe; if what remains still reaches the nisab, zakat is due.

checks.q: In the Hanafi school, is zakat due on gold jewellery a woman wears?
checks.a: Yes, it is counted with her wealth
w: No, unless it is over 1 kg
checks.why: In the Hanafi school gold and silver are counted whether worn or stored.

checks.q: Which of these is counted for zakat?
checks.why: Cash, savings, gold, silver and trade goods are counted; things for personal use are not.

lessons.title: How much, and on what
lessons.about: The rate, trade goods, and giving zakat discreetly.

cards.x: Zakat on gold, silver, money and trade goods is a fortieth (2.5%).
cards.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, zakat on silver, gold and trade goods

cards.x: Goods bought to sell are valued, and zakat is paid on their value.
cards.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, zakat on silver, gold and trade goods

cards.x: You don't have to say 'this is zakat'. You may give it like a gift, as long as you intend it as zakat.
cards.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, zakat on silver, gold and trade goods

checks.q: What is the rate of zakat on money?
checks.why: Zakat on money, gold, silver and trade goods is a fortieth, which is 2.5%.
checks.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, zakat on silver, gold and trade goods

checks.q: Must you tell the poor person 'this is zakat'?
w: Yes, or it does not count
checks.why: You don't have to say 'this is zakat'. Intending it as zakat is enough.
checks.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, zakat on silver, gold and trade goods

checks.q: Is zakat due on goods you bought to sell?
w: No, only once they are sold
Yes, on what you paid for them
checks.why: Goods bought to sell are valued, and zakat is paid on their value.
checks.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, zakat on silver, gold and trade goods

checks.q: How is the zakat on trade goods worked out?
w: 2.5% of what you paid for them
checks.why: Goods for sale are valued at their current price on the day zakat is due.

lessons.title: Who may receive zakat
lessons.about: Who zakat may be given to, and who it may not.

cards.x: The poor, the needy, those who collect it, those in debt, those striving in the path of Allah, the stranded traveller, and (in its time) freeing captives.
cards.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, who may receive zakat

cards.ar: إِنَّمَا الصَّدَقَٰتُ لِلْفُقَرَآءِ وَالْمَسَٰكِينِ وَالْعَٰمِلِينَ عَلَيْهَا وَالْمُؤَلَّفَةِ قُلُوبُهُمْ وَفِي الرِّقَابِ وَالْغَٰرِمِينَ وَفِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ وَابْنِ السَّبِيلِ فَرِيضَةٗ مِّنَ اللَّهِ وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ حَكِيمٞ ﴿٦٠﴾
cards.x: Zakat is only for the poor and the needy, those who work to collect it, those whose hearts are to be won over, freeing captives, those in debt, the cause of Allah, and the stranded traveller: an obligation from Allah. Allah is Knowing, Wise.
You may not give your zakat to your parents, grandparents, children or grandchildren, nor to your spouse (a wife giving to her husband is also not allowed, in Imam Abu Hanifah's view).
cards.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, who may receive zakat

cards.x: Zakat may not be given to Banu Hashim, the family of the Prophet ﷺ, even if they are poor. Help them with gifts instead.
cards.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, who may receive zakat

cards.x: Zakat must be given into the ownership of a poor Muslim. It cannot be used to build a masjid, pay for a funeral, or be given to someone who owns the nisab. If you are unsure, give it through a trustworthy organisation that keeps zakat separate.
cards.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, Who may receive zakat

checks.q: Can you give your zakat to your own mother?
checks.why: Zakat may not be given to your parents or grandparents, or to your children or grandchildren.
checks.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, who may receive zakat

checks.q: How are poor descendants of Banu Hashim helped?
checks.a: With gifts and charity that is not zakat
w: With zakat, like anyone in need
With zakat, if they are very poor
checks.why: Zakat may not be given to Banu Hashim, even if they are poor. They are helped with gifts and charity instead.
checks.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, who may receive zakat

checks.q: Which may receive zakat?
checks.why: The stranded traveller is one of those who may receive zakat.
checks.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, who may receive zakat

checks.q: May you give your zakat to your poor brother?
w: No, unless he lives with you
checks.why: Zakat may not go to parents, grandparents, children, grandchildren or a spouse; brothers, sisters and other relatives may receive it, and it is better.

checks.q: May zakat money be used to build a masjid?
w: Yes, it is the best use
checks.why: Zakat must be given into the ownership of a poor person, so it cannot pay for a building.
checks.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, Who may receive zakat

lessons.title: Zakat al-Fitr
lessons.about: Who pays it, how much and when.

cards.x: It is wajib on a free Muslim who owns the nisab beyond his home, clothes, furniture and basic needs. He pays for himself and his young children.
cards.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, chapter on Sadaqat al-Fitr

cards.x: Half a sa' of wheat or wheat flour (about 1.6–2 kg), or a full sa' of dates, raisins or barley (about 3.2–4 kg), or the value of it in money, which is what most people give today. A sa' is a measure of volume from the time of the Prophet ﷺ, so the weight in kg is an estimate.
cards.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, chapter on Sadaqat al-Fitr

cards.x: It becomes due at dawn on the day of Eid. It is recommended to give it before going out to the Eid prayer; giving it earlier is allowed, and delaying it does not cancel it.
cards.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, chapter on Sadaqat al-Fitr

checks.q: When does zakat al-fitr become due?
checks.a: At dawn on the day of Eid
checks.why: Al-Quduri: it is tied to the dawn of the day of Fitr.

checks.q: Who does a father pay zakat al-fitr for?
checks.why: He pays for himself and his young children; not for his wife or adult children.

checks.q: If it is delayed past Eid…
checks.why: Delaying it does not make it fall away.

checks.q: About how much wheat is half a sa' for zakat al-Fitr?
checks.why: Half a sa' of wheat is roughly 1.6–2 kg; most people give its value in money.

lessons.title: Qurbani (udhiyah)
lessons.about: The sacrifice of Eid al-Adha: who must give it, and how.

cards.x: In the Hanafi school, the qurbani is wajib on a free, resident Muslim who owns the nisab beyond their basic needs on the days of sacrifice. It is for oneself, not for one's children.
From after the Eid prayer on the 10th of Dhu al-Hijjah until sunset on the 12th. Where there is no Eid prayer, from dawn on the 10th.
A sheep or goat of at least one year counts for one person. A cow (two years) or a camel (five years) counts for up to seven people, each with a full share. It must be free of major defects.
It is recommended to divide it into thirds: for your family, for relatives and friends, and for the poor. The skin may be given away but not sold.

checks.q: In the Hanafi school, what is the ruling of qurbani for someone who owns the nisab?
checks.why: Wajib on the free, resident Muslim who owns the nisab on the days of sacrifice.

checks.q: How many people can share one cow for qurbani?
checks.why: A cow or camel counts for up to seven; a sheep or goat for one.

checks.q: In a town where the Eid prayer is held, when may the qurbani be slaughtered?
checks.a: From after the Eid prayer on 10 Dhu al-Hijjah until sunset on the 12th
w: From dawn on 10 Dhu al-Hijjah until sunset on the 12th
From after the Eid prayer on 10 Dhu al-Hijjah until sunset on the 13th
From the Day of 'Arafah, 9 Dhu al-Hijjah, until sunset on the 12th
checks.why: Slaughtering before the Eid prayer, where it is held, does not count.

checks.q: How old must a goat be for qurbani?
checks.why: A sheep of six months that looks like a yearling is also accepted.

lessons.title: Who must perform Hajj
lessons.about: The conditions, and the months of Hajj.

cards.x: Hajj is fard on free, adult, sane and healthy Muslims who can afford the provision and transport, beyond their home, their needs and their family's maintenance until they return, when the road is safe.

cards.ar: فِيهِ ءَايَٰتُ بَيِّنَٰتٞ مَّقَامُ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ وَمَن دَخَلَهُ كَانَ ءَامِنٗا وَلِلَّهِ عَلَى النَّاسِ حِجُّ الْبَيْتِ مَنِ اسْتَطَاعَ إِلَيْهِ سَبِيلٗا وَمَن كَفَرَ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ غَنِيٌّ عَنِ الْعَٰلَمِينَ ﴿٩٧﴾
cards.x: Pilgrimage to the House is a duty owed to Allah by people who are able to find a way there.
A woman must have a mahram or her husband with her if Makkah is three days' journey or more away. She may not go for Hajj without one of them.
The months of Hajj are Shawwal, Dhu al-Qa'dah and the first ten days of Dhu al-Hijjah.

checks.q: Hajj is fard on someone who…
checks.a: Can afford travel beyond his needs and his family's upkeep
w: Has any savings at all, even if he is in debt
Can afford the travel, even if his family is left in need
Has already done 'umrah and lives near Makkah
checks.why: Al-Quduri ties it to affording provision and transport beyond needs and family maintenance, with a safe road.

checks.q: May a woman travel three days' journey or more for Hajj without her husband or a mahram?
checks.why: Al-Quduri: she may not perform Hajj without a mahram or husband if the journey is three days or more.

checks.q: Which are the months of Hajj?
checks.a: Shawwal, Dhu al-Qa'dah and ten days of Dhu al-Hijjah
w: The first ten days of Dhu al-Hijjah
Dhu al-Qa'dah, Dhu al-Hijjah and Muharram
checks.why: Al-Quduri defines them in the chapter on tamattu'.

checks.q: A child performs Hajj before puberty. Does it count as his fard Hajj?
checks.a: No, he performs it again as an adult
w: Yes, if his parents paid for it
Yes, if he was over ten
checks.why: A child's Hajj is valid and rewarded, but the fard Hajj is still due once he is an adult and able.

lessons.title: The miqat and entering ihram
lessons.about: Where to enter ihram, and how.

cards.x: Do not pass these without ihram: Dhu al-Hulayfah for the people of Madinah, Dhat 'Irq for Iraq, al-Juhfah for Syria, Qarn al-Manazil for Najd, and Yalamlam for Yemen. Entering ihram before them is allowed.
cards.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, chapter on the miqats

cards.x: Make ghusl (or wudu, but ghusl is better), put on two clean sheets, a lower and an upper one, apply perfume if you have it, and pray two rak'ahs.

Say: 'O Allah, I intend Hajj, make it easy for me and accept it from me.' Then say the talbiyah: 'Labbayk Allahumma labbayk, labbayk la sharika laka labbayk, inna al-hamda wa al-ni'mata laka wa al-mulk, la sharika lak.' With the talbiyah you are in ihram.

checks.q: What is the miqat for people coming from Madinah?
checks.why: Al-Quduri: Dhu al-Hulayfah for the people of Madinah.

checks.q: When do you actually enter ihram?
checks.a: When you say the talbiyah with the intention
w: When you put on the two sheets
When you first see the Ka'bah
checks.why: 'When he says the talbiyah, he has entered ihram.'

checks.q: Before entering ihram, which is the sunnah?
checks.why: Ghusl or wudu, and ghusl is better.

checks.q: What does a man wear in ihram?
checks.a: Two unstitched sheets, lower and upper
w: A white thawb and a cap
checks.why: An izar round the waist and a rida' over the shoulders, with nothing stitched to the shape of the body.
