lessons.title: What ihram forbids
lessons.about: What the muhrim must avoid.

cards.x: Avoid intimacy and its talk, sinning and arguing. Do not hunt, or point out or direct anyone to game.

cards.ar: الْحَجُّ أَشْهُرٞ مَّعْلُومَٰتٞ فَمَن فَرَضَ فِيهِنَّ الْحَجَّ فَلَا رَفَثَ وَلَا فُسُوقَ وَلَا جِدَالَ فِي الْحَجِّ وَمَا تَفْعَلُواْ مِنْ خَيْرٖ يَعْلَمْهُ اللَّهُ وَتَزَوَّدُواْ فَإِنَّ خَيْرَ الزَّادِ التَّقْوَىٰ وَاتَّقُونِ يَـٰٓأُوْلِي الْأَلْبَٰبِ ﴿١٩٧﴾
cards.x: Hajj is in well-known months. Whoever sets out to do Hajj in them, let there be no intimacy, no sinning and no quarrelling in Hajj.
A man does not wear a shirt, trousers, turban, cap, cloak or khuffs (unless he has no sandals, then he cuts them below the ankles), and does not cover his head or face.
Do not use perfume or anything scented, shave or remove any hair, trim the beard or cut the nails. Bathing, shade and wearing a money belt are allowed, with conditions: see the next point.

Bathing for cleanliness or to cool down is allowed, but: no scented soap, shower gel, shampoo or scented wipes, because the later Hanafi scholars count these as perfume, which brings a penalty. Al-Quduri says the muhrim does not wash his head or beard with khitmi (a cleansing plant). Use water, or unscented soap, and wash gently so that no hair falls out. Do not dry yourself with a scented towel.

A woman is like a man in all this, except that she covers her head and keeps cloth from touching her face (if needed she lets something hang in front that does not touch it), does not raise her voice in the talbiyah, does not jog in tawaf or run between the green markers, and trims her hair instead of shaving.

checks.q: May a man in ihram cover his head?
checks.why: Al-Quduri: he does not cover his head or face.

checks.q: Which is allowed in ihram?
checks.a: Bathing with water or unscented soap
checks.why: Bathing is allowed, but scented soap, shower gel and shampoo count as perfume and bring a penalty. Wash gently so no hair falls.

checks.q: In ihram, a woman…
checks.a: Covers her head and uncovers her face
w: Uncovers her head and covers her face
Covers both her head and face
Shaves her head at the end
checks.why: She keeps her head covered and her face uncovered.

checks.q: In ihram you want a shower. Which is right?
checks.a: Use water or unscented soap, and wash gently
w: Any shower gel is fine as it is only for washing
Use scented shampoo but not perfume
Showering is not allowed in ihram
checks.why: Scented soap and shampoo count as perfume. Bathing itself is allowed, without making hair fall.

lessons.title: The three ways of Hajj
lessons.about: Ifrad, tamattu' and qiran.

cards.x: Entering ihram for Hajj alone.

Entering ihram for 'umrah in the months of Hajj, completing it and leaving ihram, then entering ihram for Hajj from Makkah on the 8th (Yawm al-Tarwiyah). A sacrifice is due. If he cannot afford it, he fasts three days after entering ihram for the 'umrah, the last of them on the Day of 'Arafah (best: the 7th, 8th and 9th), and seven after the days of Hajj, best at home. If the three are not fasted before the Day of Sacrifice, fasting no longer counts: only the sacrifice will do, and it stays owed.
Entering ihram for 'umrah and Hajj together from the miqat. In the Hanafi school qiran is the best, then tamattu', then ifrad. It too requires a sacrifice.
The people of Makkah do not do tamattu' or qiran; only ifrad.

checks.q: Which way of Hajj is best in the Hanafi school?
checks.why: Al-Quduri: qiran is better than tamattu' and ifrad.

checks.q: In tamattu', when do you enter ihram for Hajj?
checks.a: On the 8th of Dhu al-Hijjah, from Makkah
w: On the 10th, after the Eid prayer
checks.why: After completing the 'umrah you stay in Makkah and enter ihram for Hajj on Yawm al-Tarwiyah.

checks.q: A mutamatti' cannot afford the sacrifice and has not fasted the three days by the Day of Sacrifice. What now?
checks.a: Fasting no longer counts; the sacrifice is owed
w: He fasts ten days at home instead
He fasts three days after Eid
checks.why: The three days must be fasted before the Day of Sacrifice, the last on 'Arafah; after that only the sacrifice will do.

checks.q: A mutamatti' who cannot afford the sacrifice fasts…
checks.a: Three days before the Day of Sacrifice and seven after Hajj
w: Three days after Eid and seven at home
checks.why: The three end on the Day of 'Arafah; the seven come after the days of Hajj.

lessons.title: 'Umrah
lessons.about: Its ruling and its acts.

cards.x: 'Umrah is a sunnah. It can be done at any time of year, but is disliked on five days: the Day of 'Arafah, the Day of Sacrifice and the three days of tashriq.
cards.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, chapter on missing Hajj

cards.x: 'Umrah is: ihram, tawaf, sa'y, and shaving or trimming.
cards.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, chapter on missing Hajj

cards.x: The one in 'umrah stops the talbiyah when he starts the tawaf.

checks.q: What is the ruling of 'umrah in the Hanafi school?
checks.why: Al-Quduri: 'umrah is sunnah.

checks.q: On which day is 'umrah disliked?
checks.why: It is disliked on 'Arafah, the Day of Sacrifice and the days of tashriq.

checks.q: What are the acts of 'umrah?
checks.a: Ihram, tawaf, sa'y, then shaving or trimming
checks.why: Al-Quduri lists exactly these.

lessons.title: Tawaf and sa'y
lessons.about: Arriving in Makkah.

cards.x: Enter al-Masjid al-Haram. On seeing the House say takbir and tahlil. Begin at the Black Stone: face it, say takbir, raise your hands and touch and kiss it if you can without harming anyone.

Go round the House seven times, with the Ka'bah on your left, outside the Hatim. Men uncover the right shoulder (idtiba') and jog (raml) in the first three circuits, then walk. Touch the Stone each time you pass it if you can, and end with it.
Pray two rak'ahs at the Station of Ibrahim, or wherever is easy in the masjid.

Go to al-Safa, face the House, say takbir and tahlil, send blessings on the Prophet ﷺ and make du'a. Walk to al-Marwah, men running between the two green markers. That is one circuit; complete seven, starting at al-Safa and ending at al-Marwah.

checks.q: Where does each circuit of tawaf begin?
w: At the door of the Ka'bah
checks.why: Al-Quduri: begin at the Black Stone.

checks.q: In which circuits do men jog (raml)?
checks.why: Raml is in the first three circuits.

checks.q: Sa'y starts at… and ends at…
checks.why: Seven circuits, starting at al-Safa and ending at al-Marwah.

lessons.title: Mina, 'Arafah and Muzdalifah
lessons.about: The 8th and 9th of Dhu al-Hijjah.

cards.x: On the 8th (Yawm al-Tarwiyah), after Fajr in Makkah, go to Mina and stay until you pray Fajr on the Day of 'Arafah.

cards.ar: لَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ جُنَاحٌ أَن تَبْتَغُواْ فَضْلٗا مِّن رَّبِّكُمْ فَإِذَآ أَفَضْتُم مِّنْ عَرَفَٰتٖ فَاذْكُرُواْ اللَّهَ عِندَ الْمَشْعَرِ الْحَرَامِ وَاذْكُرُوهُ كَمَا هَدَىٰكُمْ وَإِن كُنتُم مِّن قَبْلِهِ لَمِنَ الضَّآلِّينَ ﴿١٩٨﴾
cards.x: When you pour down from 'Arafat, remember Allah at the Sacred Landmark (Muzdalifah).

The standing at 'Arafah is the heart of Hajj. Whoever is at 'Arafah at any time from midday on the 9th until dawn on the 10th has caught the Hajj. All of 'Arafah is a place of standing except Batn 'Uranah. Strive in du'a.
After sunset, leave calmly for Muzdalifah. Pray Maghrib and 'Isha' there together. After Fajr, stand and make du'a, then leave for Mina before sunrise.

checks.q: When is the time for standing at 'Arafah?
checks.a: From midday on the 9th until dawn on the 10th
w: From sunset on the 9th until midnight
checks.why: Al-Quduri: from the sun's decline on the Day of 'Arafah to dawn on the Day of Sacrifice.

checks.q: Where are Maghrib and 'Isha' prayed on the night of the 9th?
checks.why: Praying Maghrib on the road is not valid in the view of Abu Hanifah and Muhammad.

checks.q: Which part of 'Arafah is not a place of standing?
checks.why: All of 'Arafah is valid except Batn 'Uranah.

checks.q: What is the heart of Hajj, without which it is missed?
checks.why: 'Hajj is 'Arafah.' Whoever is there between midday on the 9th and dawn on the 10th has caught it.

lessons.title: The Day of Sacrifice and after
lessons.about: Stoning, sacrifice, shaving and tawaf al-ziyarah.

cards.x: On the 10th, stone Jamrat al-'Aqabah with seven pebbles, saying takbir with each. Stop the talbiyah with the first pebble.
Then sacrifice, then shave or trim; shaving is better. Now everything is lawful except intimacy.

Go to Makkah on the 10th, 11th or 12th and perform tawaf al-ziyarah, seven circuits. This is the fard tawaf of Hajj. After it, intimacy becomes lawful. Delaying it past these days requires a sacrifice, according to Abu Hanifah.

Return to Mina. On the 11th and 12th, after midday, stone the three jamarat, starting with the one nearest the Masjid al-Khayf, seven pebbles each, stopping to make du'a after the first two. You may leave on the 12th or stay for the 13th.

checks.q: Which jamrah is stoned on the 10th?
checks.why: On the Day of Sacrifice only Jamrat al-'Aqabah is stoned.

checks.q: What is the fard tawaf of Hajj?
checks.why: Al-Quduri: 'This tawaf is the one that is fard in Hajj.'

checks.q: After stoning, sacrificing and shaving, what remains forbidden until tawaf al-ziyarah?
checks.why: Everything becomes lawful except intimacy, which becomes lawful after tawaf al-ziyarah.

lessons.title: Farewell, and the wajibs of Hajj
lessons.about: Tawaf al-Wada', and what a sacrifice repairs.

cards.x: Before leaving Makkah, perform tawaf al-sadr (the farewell tawaf), seven circuits without jogging. It is wajib, except for the people of Makkah. A woman who gets her period after tawaf al-ziyarah may leave without it.
Leaving sa'y, the standing at Muzdalifah, the stoning, or the farewell tawaf requires a sheep, and the Hajj is still complete.
cards.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, chapter on the violations of the muhrim

cards.x: Missing the standing at 'Arafah means the Hajj is missed. Tawaf al-ziyarah must be done; a sacrifice cannot replace it.
cards.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, chapter on the violations of the muhrim

checks.q: Someone left out sa'y. What follows?
checks.a: A sheep is due; the Hajj is complete
w: The Hajj is invalid and must be repeated
Nothing is due; the Hajj is complete
He fasts three days; the Hajj is complete
checks.why: Al-Quduri: 'Whoever leaves the sa'y owes a sheep, and his Hajj is complete.'

checks.q: Is the farewell tawaf wajib on the people of Makkah?
checks.why: It is wajib except on the people of Makkah.

checks.q: A woman's period starts after tawaf al-ziyarah. Before leaving she…
checks.a: May leave without the farewell tawaf
w: Must wait until she is pure
checks.why: Al-Quduri: she leaves, and owes nothing for missing tawaf al-sadr.

title: Reading the Qur'an: letters and tajweed
sub: The Arabic letters, vowel signs and the basic rules of tajweed

lessons.title: The Arabic letters (1)
lessons.about: Reading right to left, and the first fourteen letters.

cards.x: Arabic is written and read from right to left. There are 28 letters, plus the hamzah (ء). Most letters join to the letter after them, and their shape changes a little at the start, middle or end of a word.
cards.src: al-Muqaddimah al-Jazariyyah, the points of articulation

cards.x: Alif is a straight line. Ba' has one dot below; ta' two dots above; tha' three dots above (said like 'th' in 'think').
cards.src: al-Muqaddimah al-Jazariyyah, the points of articulation
cards.ar: ا   ب   ت   ث

cards.x: Jim has a dot inside. Ha' (ح) has no dot: a breathy 'h' from the middle of the throat. Kha' (خ) has a dot above: a rough sound from the top of the throat, like 'ch' in Scottish 'loch'.
cards.src: al-Muqaddimah al-Jazariyyah, the points of articulation
cards.ar: ج   ح   خ

cards.x: Dal is a 'd'; dhal has a dot and is said like 'th' in 'this'. Ra' is a rolled 'r'; zay has a dot and is a 'z'. These four never join to the letter after them.
cards.src: al-Muqaddimah al-Jazariyyah, the points of articulation
cards.ar: د   ذ   ر   ز

cards.x: Sin is 's' and shin (three dots) is 'sh'. Sad (ص) is a heavy 's' with the tongue raised; dad (ض) is a heavy letter from the side of the tongue, found only in Arabic.
cards.src: al-Muqaddimah al-Jazariyyah, the points of articulation
cards.ar: س   ش   ص   ض

checks.q: Which way is Arabic read?
checks.why: The first letter of a word is on the right.
checks.src: al-Muqaddimah al-Jazariyyah, the points of articulation

checks.q: Which of these words is 'Rahim', the Merciful (ر ح ي م)?
checks.why: رَحِيمٌ has ح, the breathy letter with no dot. رَجِيمٌ (with ج) means 'accursed': one letter changes the meaning completely.
checks.src: al-Muqaddimah al-Jazariyyah, the points of articulation

checks.q: In the word خَلَقَ ('He created'), which letter comes first?
checks.why: The first letter, on the right, is خ: the dot is above. With ح the word would be different.
checks.src: al-Muqaddimah al-Jazariyyah, the points of articulation

checks.q: Which word is written with letters that do not join forward?
checks.why: د, ا and ر never join to the letter after them, so دَارٌ is written in separate pieces. Alif, dal, dhal, ra', zay and waw never join forward.
checks.src: al-Muqaddimah al-Jazariyyah, the points of articulation

lessons.title: The Arabic letters (2)
lessons.about: The second fourteen letters, and the hamzah.

cards.x: Ta' (ط) is a heavy 't' and za' (ظ) a heavy 'th' as in 'this'. 'Ayn (ع) is a deep sound from the middle of the throat, with no English equal; ghayn (غ), with a dot, is a gargled sound from the top of the throat.
cards.src: al-Muqaddimah al-Jazariyyah, the points of articulation
cards.ar: ط   ظ   ع   غ

cards.x: Some surahs open with letters read by their names. Listen to al-Husari read them, and repeat after him.
cards.src: al-Muqaddimah al-Jazariyyah, the points of articulation
cards.ar: الم   ص   ق   ن   طه   يس   حم   عسق   كهيعص   الر

cards.x: Fa' has one dot above; qaf (ق) has two dots and is a deep 'q' from the back of the tongue; kaf (ك) is an ordinary 'k'. Lam is 'l'.
cards.src: al-Muqaddimah al-Jazariyyah, the points of articulation
cards.ar: ف   ق   ك   ل

cards.x: Mim is 'm' and nun 'n'. This ha' (ه) is a light 'h' from the deepest part of the throat. Waw is 'w' and ya' is 'y'.
cards.src: al-Muqaddimah al-Jazariyyah, the points of articulation
cards.ar: م   ن   ه   و   ي

cards.x: The hamzah (ء) is a short catch in the throat, like the break in 'uh-oh'. It often sits on an alif, waw or ya'.
cards.src: al-Muqaddimah al-Jazariyyah, the points of articulation
cards.ar: ء   أ   ؤ   ئ

cards.x: Each letter changes a little depending on where it is. Ba' at the start, middle and end of a word:
cards.src: al-Muqaddimah al-Jazariyyah, the points of articulation
cards.ar: بـ   ـبـ   ـب

checks.q: 'Alim (عَلِيمٌ, All-Knowing) and alim (أَلِيمٌ, painful) differ only in their first letter. Which letter is in عَلِيمٌ?
checks.why: عَلِيمٌ, a Name of Allah, begins with 'ayn. Saying a hamzah instead turns it into أَلِيمٌ, 'painful': this is why the throat letters must be learnt from a teacher.
checks.src: al-Muqaddimah al-Jazariyyah, the points of articulation

checks.q: Which word is qalb, 'heart'?
checks.why: قَلْبٌ begins with qaf, the deep letter from the back of the tongue. With kaf, كَلْبٌ, it means 'dog'.
checks.src: al-Muqaddimah al-Jazariyyah, the points of articulation

checks.q: How is the hamzah sound best described?
checks.a: A short catch in the throat, as in 'uh-oh'
w: A long 'a', held for two counts
A rolled sound from the tongue
checks.why: The hamzah stops the breath for a moment; it can sit on alif, waw or ya' (أ ؤ ئ) or stand alone (ء).
checks.src: al-Muqaddimah al-Jazariyyah, the points of articulation

checks.q: How many letters are in the Arabic alphabet?
checks.why: Twenty-eight letters, and the hamzah besides them.
checks.src: al-Muqaddimah al-Jazariyyah, the points of articulation

lessons.title: Vowels and signs
lessons.about: The short vowels, sukun, shaddah, tanween and the long vowels.

cards.x: Fathah (a line above) is a short 'a'; kasrah (a line below) a short 'i'; dammah (a small waw above) a short 'u'.
cards.src: al-Muqaddimah al-Jazariyyah, the points of articulation
cards.ar: بَ   بِ   بُ

cards.x: A small circle above means the letter has no vowel: it closes the syllable. أَبْ is read 'ab'.
cards.src: al-Muqaddimah al-Jazariyyah, the points of articulation
cards.ar: أَبْ

cards.x: A shaddah (like a small 'w') doubles the letter: it is read once closed and once open. رَبِّ is 'rab-bi'. Missing a shaddah can change the meaning.
cards.src: al-Muqaddimah al-Jazariyyah, the points of articulation
cards.ar: رَبِّ

cards.x: A doubled vowel at the end of a word adds an 'n' sound: -an, -in, -un.
cards.src: al-Muqaddimah al-Jazariyyah, rulings of nun sakinah and tanween
cards.ar: بًا   بٍ   بٌ

cards.x: Alif after a fathah, ya' after a kasrah and waw after a dammah lengthen the vowel for two counts: baa, bii, buu. These are the letters of madd.
cards.ar: بَا   بِي   بُو

checks.q: A small circle above a letter (sukun) means the letter is…
checks.why: Sukun closes the syllable: in قُلْ (qul) the lam has no vowel.
checks.src: al-Muqaddimah al-Jazariyyah, the points of articulation

checks.q: What does a shaddah do to a letter?
checks.why: رَبِّ is read rab-bi, and إِيَّاكَ iy-yaka.
checks.src: al-Muqaddimah al-Jazariyyah, the points of articulation

checks.q: How is بُو read?
checks.why: Waw after a dammah lengthens the 'u' for two counts, as in يَقُولُ (yaquulu).

checks.q: Tanween adds which sound at the end of a word?
checks.why: عَلِيمًا is read 'aliman, عَلِيمٍ 'alimin, عَلِيمٌ 'alimun.
checks.src: al-Muqaddimah al-Jazariyyah, rulings of nun sakinah and tanween

lessons.title: Where the letters come from
lessons.about: The points of articulation, the heavy letters, and the mistakes that change meaning.

cards.x: Ibn al-Jazari counts seventeen points of articulation, in five areas: the empty space of the mouth and throat (the long vowels), the throat, the tongue, the lips, and the nose (for ghunnah).
cards.src: al-Muqaddimah al-Jazariyyah, the points of articulation

cards.x: Hamzah and ha' (ه) from the deepest part; 'ayn and ha' (ح) from the middle; ghayn and kha' from the top.
cards.src: al-Muqaddimah al-Jazariyyah, the points of articulation
cards.ar: ء ه   ع ح   غ خ

cards.x: Fa' from the inside of the lower lip with the upper teeth; ba', mim and waw from the two lips.
cards.src: al-Muqaddimah al-Jazariyyah, the points of articulation
cards.ar: ف   ب م و

cards.x: Seven letters are always said heavy, with the back of the tongue raised. They are gathered in the phrase khuss daghtin qiz. All other letters are light, except ra' and the lam of 'Allah' at times.
cards.src: al-Muqaddimah al-Jazariyyah, the qualities of the letters
cards.ar: خُصَّ ضَغْطٍ قِظْ

cards.x: Mixing ح and ه, ع and ء, ق and ك, or س and ص changes the word. قَلْبٌ is 'heart' but كَلْبٌ is 'dog'. Practise these pairs with a teacher.
cards.src: al-Muqaddimah al-Jazariyyah, the qualities of the letters
cards.ar: قَلْبٌ   كَلْبٌ

checks.q: How many points of articulation (makharij) are there?
checks.why: Seventeen points, in five areas: the empty space of the mouth, the throat, the tongue, the lips and the nose.
checks.src: al-Muqaddimah al-Jazariyyah, the points of articulation

checks.q: Which letters come from the middle of the throat?
checks.why: Deepest: ء and ه (as in أَنْعَمْتَ, اهْدِنَا); middle: ع and ح (الْعَالَمِينَ, الْحَمْدُ); top: غ and خ (غَيْرِ, خَلَقَ).
checks.src: al-Muqaddimah al-Jazariyyah, the points of articulation

checks.q: Which phrase gathers the seven always-heavy letters?
w: ء ه ع ح غ خ (the throat letters)
checks.why: Kha', sad, dad, ghayn, ta', qaf, za'.
checks.src: al-Muqaddimah al-Jazariyyah, the qualities of the letters

checks.q: Saying كَلْب instead of قَلْب changes 'heart' to…
checks.why: Each letter has its own point of articulation, and changing it changes the word: قَلْبٌ is heart, كَلْبٌ is dog; عَلِيمٌ is All-Knowing, أَلِيمٌ is painful.
checks.src: al-Muqaddimah al-Jazariyyah, the qualities of the letters

lessons.title: Nun sakinah and tanween
lessons.about: A nun with sukun (نْ) or tanween follows one of four rules, depending on the letter after it.

cards.x: A nun sakinah is a nun with a sukun (نْ). Tanween is the doubled vowel at the end of a word (ـً ـٍ ـٌ), which sounds like a nun. Both follow the same four rules, and the letter after them decides which: izhar, idgham, iqlab or ikhfa'.
cards.src: al-Muqaddimah al-Jazariyyah, rulings of nun sakinah and tanween
cards.ar: مِنْ   سَمِيعٌ   عَلِيمًا

cards.x: Before the six throat letters, ء ه ع ح غ خ, the nun is said clearly with no ghunnah. Examples: مَنْ آمَنَ (man amana), مِنْهُمْ (minhum), أَنْعَمْتَ (an'amta), مِنْ حَكِيمٍ (min hakim), مِنْ غِلٍّ (min ghill), مِنْ خَوْفٍ (min khawf), and كُفُوًا أَحَدٌ (kufuwan ahad).
cards.src: al-Muqaddimah al-Jazariyyah, rulings of nun sakinah and tanween
cards.ar: ء   ه   ع   ح   غ   خ

cards.x: Before the six letters of يَرْمَلُونَ (ي ر م ل و ن) the nun merges into the next letter. With ghunnah into ي ن م و: مَنْ يَقُولُ (may-yaqulu), مِنْ نِعْمَةٍ, مِنْ مَاءٍ, مِنْ وَالٍ. Without ghunnah into ل and ر: مِنْ لَدُنْهُ (mil-ladunhu), مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ (mir-rabbihim). It happens only between two words: in دُنْيَا the nun stays clear.
cards.src: al-Muqaddimah al-Jazariyyah, rulings of nun sakinah and tanween
cards.ar: ي   ن   م   و  ·  ل   ر

cards.x: Before the single letter ب the nun or tanween becomes a hidden mim, with ghunnah. Examples: مِنْ بَعْدِ (mim ba'di), أَنْبِئْهُمْ (ambi'hum), سَمِيعٌ بَصِيرٌ (sami'um basir), لَنَسْفَعًا بِالنَّاصِيَةِ. Mushafs often mark it with a small mim (ـۢ).
cards.src: al-Muqaddimah al-Jazariyyah, rulings of nun sakinah and tanween
cards.ar: ب

cards.x: Before the remaining fifteen letters, ت ث ج د ذ ز س ش ص ض ط ظ ف ق ك, the nun is hidden: said through the nose with ghunnah for two counts, the tongue not pressing on its point. Examples: مِنْ جُوعٍ (min ju'), أَنْتُمْ (antum), مِنْ قَبْلِ (min qabli), عَنْ صَلَاتِهِمْ, إِنْ كُنْتُمْ, مَنْ ذَا.
cards.src: al-Muqaddimah al-Jazariyyah, rulings of nun sakinah and tanween
cards.ar: ت ث ج د ذ ز س ش ص ض ط ظ ف ق ك

cards.x: Ghunnah is the sound from the nose, held for about two counts. Besides idgham, iqlab and ikhfa', it is always there in a nun or mim with shaddah: إِنَّ, ثُمَّ, إِنَّا أَعْطَيْنَاكَ.
cards.src: al-Muqaddimah al-Jazariyyah, the doubled nun and mim
cards.ar: إِنَّ   ثُمَّ

checks.q: In مِنْ حَكِيمٍ the nun sakinah comes before ح. Which rule applies?
checks.why: ح is one of the six throat letters (ء ه ع ح غ خ), so the nun is said clearly: min hakim.
checks.src: al-Muqaddimah al-Jazariyyah, rulings of nun sakinah and tanween

checks.q: Which rule applies in مِنْ بَعْدِ?
checks.why: Before ب the nun becomes a hidden mim with ghunnah: mim ba'di.
checks.src: al-Muqaddimah al-Jazariyyah, rulings of nun sakinah and tanween

checks.q: Which rule applies in مِنْ جُوعٍ?
checks.why: ج is one of the fifteen letters of ikhfa', so the nun is hidden with ghunnah: min ju'.
checks.src: al-Muqaddimah al-Jazariyyah, rulings of nun sakinah and tanween

checks.q: In مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ the nun merges into the ra'. Is there a ghunnah?
checks.why: Before ل and ر the merging is without ghunnah: mir-rabbihim. Before ي ن م و it is with ghunnah.
checks.src: al-Muqaddimah al-Jazariyyah, rulings of nun sakinah and tanween

checks.q: Which group are the letters of idgham?
checks.a: ي ر م ل و ن (yarmalun)
w: ء ه ع ح غ خ (the throat letters)
ق ط ب ج د (qutbu jadd)
خ ص ض غ ط ق ظ (khuss daghtin qiz)
checks.why: They are gathered in the word يَرْمَلُونَ (yarmalun).
checks.src: al-Muqaddimah al-Jazariyyah, rulings of nun sakinah and tanween

lessons.title: Mim sakinah
lessons.about: A mim with sukun (مْ) follows one of three rules, depending on the letter after it.

cards.x: Before ب the mim sakinah is hidden: the lips close lightly, without pressing, with a ghunnah of two counts. Examples: تَرْمِيهِمْ بِحِجَارَةٍ (al-Fil 4), وَهُمْ بِالْآخِرَةِ, رَبَّهُمْ بِهِمْ.
cards.src: al-Muqaddimah al-Jazariyyah, the doubled nun and mim
cards.ar: ب

cards.x: Before another م the mim merges into it, making one doubled mim with ghunnah. Examples: أَطْعَمَهُمْ مِنْ جُوعٍ (at'amahum-min ju'), لَهُمْ مَا, كَمْ مِنْ.
cards.src: al-Muqaddimah al-Jazariyyah, the doubled nun and mim
cards.ar: م

cards.t: 3. Izhar shafawi: clear, before all the rest
cards.x: Before the other twenty-six letters the mim is said clearly, the lips closing fully. Take special care before و and ف, where it is easy to hide it: عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا الضَّالِّينَ, هُمْ فِيهَا, أَنْعَمْتَ.
cards.src: al-Muqaddimah al-Jazariyyah, the doubled nun and mim
cards.ar: عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا   هُمْ فِيهَا

checks.q: Which rule applies in تَرْمِيهِمْ بِحِجَارَةٍ?
checks.why: Mim sakinah before ب is hidden, the lips closing lightly with ghunnah, as in al-Fil 4.
checks.src: al-Muqaddimah al-Jazariyyah, the doubled nun and mim

checks.q: Which rule applies to the mim in أَنْعَمْتَ?
checks.why: The letter after the mim is ت, not ب or م, so the mim is said clearly.
checks.src: al-Muqaddimah al-Jazariyyah, the doubled nun and mim

checks.q: Which rule applies in لَهُمْ مَا?
checks.why: Mim sakinah before another mim merges into it with ghunnah: lahum-ma.
checks.src: al-Muqaddimah al-Jazariyyah, the doubled nun and mim

checks.q: Before which two letters must you take special care to say the mim sakinah clearly?
checks.why: The lips are close to their place, so the mim is easily hidden there by mistake, as in عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا.
checks.src: al-Muqaddimah al-Jazariyyah, the doubled nun and mim

lessons.title: Lengthening (madd)
lessons.about: The three madd letters, and how many counts to hold each kind of madd.

cards.x: Three letters lengthen a vowel: alif after a fathah (ـَا), ya' sakinah after a kasrah (ـِي), and waw sakinah after a dammah (ـُو). What comes after them decides how long they are held. One count is roughly the time to fold one finger.
cards.ar: قَالَ   قِيلَ   يَقُولُ

cards.x: When no hamzah or sukun follows the madd letter, hold it two counts. Examples: قَالَ, قِيلَ, يَقُولُ, and the alif in مَالِكِ. Every other madd is built on this one.
cards.ar: مَالِكِ يَوْمِ الدِّينِ

cards.x: When a hamzah comes after the madd letter in the same word, it must be lengthened, four or five counts. Examples: جَاءَ, السَّمَاءِ, سُوءَ, جِيءَ.
cards.ar: إِذَا جَاءَ نَصْرُ اللَّهِ

cards.x: When the madd letter ends one word and the hamzah begins the next, Hafs from 'Asim (the reading in most mushafs) lengthens it four or five counts. Examples: إِنَّا أَعْطَيْنَاكَ, بِمَا أُنْزِلَ, قُوا أَنْفُسَكُمْ.
cards.ar: إِنَّا أَعْطَيْنَاكَ

cards.x: When a shaddah or a fixed sukun comes after the madd letter, hold it six counts, always. Examples: الضَّالِّينَ, الْحَاقَّةُ, دَابَّةٍ, and the letter names at the start of surahs, like الٓمٓ (alif lam-m-mim).
cards.ar: وَلَا الضَّالِّينَ

cards.x: When you stop on a word, its last letter takes a sukun. If a madd letter comes just before it, you may hold it two, four or six counts: الرَّحِيمْ, الْعَالَمِينْ, نَسْتَعِينْ. Keep the same length each time within one recitation.
cards.ar: الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمْ

checks.q: How many counts is the madd in قَالَ?
checks.why: No hamzah or sukun follows the alif: this is the natural madd, two counts, like the alif in مَالِكِ and the waw in يَقُولُ.

checks.q: How many counts is the madd in جَاءَ?
checks.why: A hamzah follows the alif in the same word: the joined madd, which must be lengthened four or five counts.

checks.q: How many counts is the madd in الضَّالِّينَ?
checks.why: A shaddah follows the alif: the necessary madd, always six counts.

checks.q: You stop at the end of الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ. How many counts may the ya' be held?
checks.why: Stopping gives the last letter a sukun, so the madd before it may be two, four or six counts.

checks.q: In إِنَّا أَعْطَيْنَاكَ the alif ends one word and the hamzah begins the next. In the reading of Hafs, it is held…
checks.why: This is the separated madd: four or five counts in Hafs from 'Asim.

lessons.title: Qalqalah, ra' and the lam of Allah
lessons.about: The five echo letters, and when ra' and the lam of 'Allah' are heavy or light.

cards.x: Five letters, gathered in قُطْبُ جَدٍّ (qutbu jadd): ق ط ب ج د. When one has a sukun, give it a slight bounce so it is heard: يَخْلُقْ, يَطْمَعُ, أَبْوَابٌ, يَجْعَلُ, قَدْ. The bounce is strongest when you stop on the letter: أَحَدْ, الْفَلَقْ, مُحِيطْ.
cards.src: al-Muqaddimah al-Jazariyyah, the qualities of the letters
cards.ar: ق   ط   ب   ج   د

cards.x: The lam in the name 'Allah' is heavy (full-mouthed) after a fathah or dammah: قَالَ اللَّهُ, رَسُولُ اللَّهِ, اللَّهُ الصَّمَدُ. It is light after a kasrah: بِسْمِ اللَّهِ, لِلَّهِ.
cards.ar: اللَّهُ الصَّمَدُ   بِسْمِ اللَّهِ

cards.x: Ra' is heavy with a fathah or dammah: رَبِّ, رُسُلٌ. It is light with a kasrah: رِجَالٌ, فِي الرِّقَابِ. A ra' with sukun follows the vowel before it: heavy in يَرْجِعُونَ and الْقُرْآنُ, light in فِرْعَوْنَ. After a kasrah it is still heavy if a heavy letter follows it, as in مِرْصَادًا. Learn the exceptions from a teacher.
cards.ar: رَبِّ   رِجَالٌ

cards.x: Stop where the meaning is complete, at the end of a verse if you can, and stop with a sukun on the last letter. Do not start again from a place that changes the meaning.

checks.q: In أَحَدْ, stopping on the dal, the dal is given…
checks.why: Dal is one of the five letters of qutbu jadd; with a sukun it bounces, most strongly when you stop on it.
checks.src: al-Muqaddimah al-Jazariyyah, the qualities of the letters

checks.q: Which group are the letters of qalqalah?
checks.a: ق ط ب ج د (qutbu jadd)
w: ي ر م ل و ن (yarmalun)
ء ه ع ح غ خ (the throat letters)
خ ص ض غ ط ق ظ (khuss daghtin qiz)
checks.why: They are gathered in قُطْبُ جَدٍّ (qutbu jadd).
checks.src: al-Muqaddimah al-Jazariyyah, the qualities of the letters

checks.q: How is the lam of 'Allah' said in بِسْمِ اللَّهِ?
checks.why: It comes after a kasrah (the -mi of bismi), so it is light. After a fathah or dammah it is heavy.

checks.q: How is the ra' said in رِجَالٌ?
checks.why: The ra' has a kasrah, so it is light. With a fathah or dammah, as in رَبِّ, it is heavy.

lessons.title: Reciting al-Fatihah correctly
lessons.about: Putting it all together for the surah you recite in every rak'ah.

cards.x: Ibn al-Jazari says applying tajweed is an obligation: whoever does not recite the Qur'an correctly is sinful. At the least, every Muslim must avoid clear mistakes that change letters, vowels or meaning, especially in al-Fatihah.
Say ح in al-hamdu (not ه), ع in al-'alamin (not ء), ص in al-sirat, and ض in al-dallin with its six-count madd.
cards.src: al-Muqaddimah al-Jazariyyah, the qualities of the letters
cards.ar: الْحَمْدُ   الْعَالَمِينَ   الصِّرَاطَ   الضَّالِّينَ

cards.x: Al-Fatihah with the basmalah has fourteen shaddahs. In إِيَّاكَ, dropping the shaddah changes the meaning entirely, so press on it.
cards.ar: إِيَّاكَ نَعْبُدُ وَإِيَّاكَ نَسْتَعِينُ

cards.x: Tajweed is taken from a teacher by ear. Recite al-Fatihah to someone who knows, ask them to correct you, and listen to a sound reciter daily.

checks.q: Applying tajweed when reciting the Qur'an is…
checks.why: He calls it a binding obligation.

checks.q: Which letter begins the word al-hamdu (after al-) in al-Fatihah?
checks.why: It is الْحَمْدُ with ح, the breathy letter from the middle of the throat. With ه it would be a different word.
checks.src: al-Muqaddimah al-Jazariyyah, the qualities of the letters

checks.q: What is the best way to learn tajweed?
checks.a: Reciting to a teacher who corrects you
checks.why: Tajweed is taken by hearing.

title: Halal & Haram
sub: Food, dress, the gaze and earning, and the levels of carefulness

lessons.title: Why halal matters
lessons.about: Al-Ghazali on the lawful and the unlawful.

cards.x: The Prophet ﷺ said Allah is good and accepts only what is good. He ﷺ mentioned a traveller, dishevelled and dusty, raising his hands: 'O Lord!', while his food, drink and clothing are haram. 'How can he be answered?'
cards.src: Hadith, Sahih Muslim; quoted in Ihya', Book of the Lawful and Unlawful

cards.ar: يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا النَّاسُ كُلُواْ مِمَّا فِي الْأَرْضِ حَلَٰلٗا طَيِّبٗا وَلَا تَتَّبِعُواْ خُطُوَٰتِ الشَّيْطَٰنِ إِنَّهُ لَكُمْ عَدُوّٞ مُّبِينٌ ﴿١٦٨﴾
cards.x: O people, eat of what is on the earth, lawful and good, and do not follow the footsteps of Shaytan.
The Prophet ﷺ said: the halal is clear and the haram is clear, and between them are doubtful matters. Whoever avoids the doubtful has protected his religion and honour.

The Prophet ﷺ said to Ka'b ibn 'Ujrah: no flesh that grew from the unlawful but the Fire is more fitting for it. Al-Ghazali explains that haram food darkens the heart and makes worship heavy, while halal lights it.

checks.q: In the hadith of the dishevelled traveller who raised his hands to the sky, why was his du'a not answered?
checks.a: His food, drink and clothing were haram
w: He did not raise his hands high enough
He was travelling and in a hurry
checks.why: In the hadith, the reason given is that his food, drink and clothing were haram.

checks.q: Between clear halal and clear haram are…
w: Things left to each person's taste
checks.why: Between them are doubtful matters that many people do not know.

checks.q: Avoiding doubtful things protects…
checks.why: 'Whoever avoids the doubtful has protected his religion and his honour.'

lessons.title: The major sins
lessons.about: What every Muslim must avoid.

cards.x: Major sins (kaba'ir) are those Allah threatened with the Fire, curse or a set punishment. Avoiding them is fard; Allah promises to forgive the minor sins of those who avoid the major ones.

cards.ar: إِن تَجْتَنِبُواْ كَبَآئِرَ مَا تُنْهَوْنَ عَنْهُ نُكَفِّرْ عَنكُمْ سَيِّـَٔاتِكُمْ وَنُدْخِلْكُم مُّدْخَلٗا كَرِيمٗا ﴿٣١﴾
cards.x: If you avoid the major sins you are forbidden, We will remove your lesser sins and admit you through a noble entrance.

cards.ar: يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ اجْتَنِبُواْ كَثِيرٗا مِّنَ الظَّنِّ إِنَّ بَعْضَ الظَّنِّ إِثْمٞ وَلَا تَجَسَّسُواْ وَلَا يَغْتَب بَّعْضُكُم بَعْضًا أَيُحِبُّ أَحَدُكُمْ أَن يَأْكُلَ لَحْمَ أَخِيهِ مَيْتٗا فَكَرِهْتُمُوهُ وَاتَّقُواْ اللَّهَ إِنَّ اللَّهَ تَوَّابٞ رَّحِيمٞ ﴿١٢﴾
cards.x: Do not spy, and do not backbite one another. Would any of you like to eat the flesh of his dead brother? You would hate it.

Shirk, killing unjustly, magic, leaving the prayer, withholding zakat, disobeying parents, zina, drinking alcohol, riba, consuming an orphan's wealth, false witness, slandering chaste people, and fleeing the battlefield.
Backbiting (saying what a person would dislike, even if true), carrying tales, and lying are major sins too. They are easy on the tongue and heavy on the Scale.
cards.src: Ihya' 'Ulum al-Din, Book of the Banes of the Tongue

checks.q: What does Allah promise those who avoid the major sins?
w: That they will never be tested
A long life in this world
checks.why: 'If you avoid the major sins you are forbidden, We will remove your lesser sins.' (al-Nisa' 31)

checks.q: Saying something true about a person that they would dislike is…
checks.why: If it is true it is backbiting; if false it is slander, which is worse.

checks.q: Which of these is a major sin?
w: Eating with the left hand by mistake
checks.why: The Prophet ﷺ counted disobeying parents among the greatest sins.

checks.q: Leaving the prayer out of laziness is…
w: A sin only if three are missed in a row
checks.why: It is among the gravest sins; make it up and repent.

lessons.title: The four degrees of carefulness
lessons.about: Al-Ghazali's levels of wara'.

cards.x: The first degree, of the upright, is avoiding what the fatwa says is haram. The second, of the righteous, is also avoiding what is doubtful.
cards.src: Ihya', Book of the Lawful and Unlawful, the degrees of wara'

cards.x: The third, of the God-fearing, is leaving some things that are fine for fear they lead to what is not.
cards.src: Ihya', Book of the Lawful and Unlawful, the degrees of wara'

cards.x: The fourth, of the siddiqin, is leaving even what is harmless if it is taken for other than Allah, or not to gain strength for His worship.
cards.src: Ihya', Book of the Lawful and Unlawful, the degrees of wara'

checks.q: Avoiding what the fatwa calls haram is the wara' of…
checks.why: The first degree, required of everyone, is the wara' of the upright. The highest is that of the siddiqin: the truthful ones, whose faith, words and deeds are wholly true, the rank just after the Prophets.

checks.q: Leaving harmless things done for other than Allah is the wara' of…
checks.why: Al-Ghazali calls this highest degree the wara' of the siddiqin: the truthful ones, the believers of the highest rank after the Prophets, like Abu Bakr al-Siddiq رضي الله عنه.

checks.q: How many degrees of wara' (carefulness) are there?
checks.why: He describes four: of the upright, the righteous, the God-fearing and the siddiqin.

lessons.title: Food and slaughter
lessons.about: What may be eaten, and whose slaughter is lawful.

cards.x: The slaughter of a Muslim or of a Jew or Christian (Ahl al-Kitab) is halal, but only if it is a real slaughter: the throat and main vessels cut while the animal is alive, and no name other than Allah's invoked. Meat killed by stunning, a machine or any other way is not halal, whoever did it. The slaughter of a Magian, an apostate or an idol-worshipper is not eaten.
cards.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, Book of Hunting and Slaughter

cards.ar: حُرِّمَتْ عَلَيْكُمُ الْمَيْتَةُ وَالدَّمُ وَلَحْمُ الْخِنزِيرِ وَمَآ أُهِلَّ لِغَيْرِ اللَّهِ بِهِ وَالْمُنْخَنِقَةُ وَالْمَوْقُوذَةُ وَالْمُتَرَدِّيَةُ وَالنَّطِيحَةُ وَمَآ أَكَلَ السَّبُعُ إِلَّا مَا ذَكَّيْتُمْ وَمَا ذُبِحَ عَلَى النُّصُبِ وَأَن تَسْتَقْسِمُواْ بِالْأَزْلَٰمِ ذَٰلِكُمْ فِسْقٌ الْيَوْمَ يَئِسَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ مِن دِينِكُمْ فَلَا تَخْشَوْهُمْ وَاخْشَوْنِ الْيَوْمَ أَكْمَلْتُ لَكُمْ دِينَكُمْ وَأَتْمَمْتُ عَلَيْكُمْ نِعْمَتِي وَرَضِيتُ لَكُمُ الْإِسْلَٰمَ دِينٗا فَمَنِ اضْطُرَّ فِي مَخْمَصَةٍ غَيْرَ مُتَجَانِفٖ لِّإِثْمٖ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٞ رَّحِيمٞ ﴿٣﴾
cards.x: Forbidden to you are carrion, blood, the flesh of swine, and what was dedicated to other than Allah…

cards.ar: وَلَا تَأْكُلُواْ مِمَّا لَمْ يُذْكَرِ اسْمُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ وَإِنَّهُ لَفِسْقٞ وَإِنَّ الشَّيَٰطِينَ لَيُوحُونَ إِلَىٰٓ أَوْلِيَآئِهِمْ لِيُجَٰدِلُوكُمْ وَإِنْ أَطَعْتُمُوهُمْ إِنَّكُمْ لَمُشْرِكُونَ ﴿١٢١﴾
cards.x: And do not eat of that over which the name of Allah has not been mentioned.
If the one slaughtering leaves out Allah's name on purpose, the animal is carrion and may not be eaten. If he forgot, it may be eaten.
cards.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, Book of Hunting and Slaughter

cards.x: Of sea creatures, only fish are eaten in the Hanafi school, and a fish that died by itself and floats is disliked. Locusts may be eaten without slaughter.
cards.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, Book of Hunting and Slaughter

cards.x: Pork and everything from it, carrion (an animal not properly slaughtered), flowing blood, alcohol and anything that intoxicates, predators with fangs, birds with talons, and donkeys. Today, check ingredients such as gelatine, animal fat and alcohol in flavourings.

checks.q: Is meat slaughtered by a Christian halal?
checks.a: Yes, if he slaughters properly in Allah's name
w: Yes, however the animal was killed
checks.why: Al-Quduri: the slaughter of a Muslim or a Kitabi is halal. It must be a real slaughter; stunned-to-death or machine-killed meat is not halal from anyone.

checks.q: The slaughterer forgot to say bismillah. The meat…
checks.why: Leaving it out by forgetting does not make it haram; leaving it on purpose does.

checks.q: Which sea creatures may be eaten in the Hanafi school?
checks.why: Al-Quduri: of water animals, only fish are eaten.

checks.q: Gelatine in sweets usually comes from…
checks.why: Most gelatine is from pork or from animals not slaughtered Islamically, so check the label or the halal certificate before eating.

lessons.title: Gold, silk and vessels
lessons.about: What men and women may wear and use.

cards.x: Silk is not lawful for men to wear, except a trim or border up to four fingers wide. It is lawful for women.
cards.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, Book of the Forbidden and the Permitted

cards.x: Men may not wear gold or silver, except a silver ring (less than one mithqal, about 4.3 g), a belt fitting and a sword decoration of silver. Women may wear gold and silver.
cards.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, Book of the Forbidden and the Permitted

cards.x: Eating, drinking, oiling and perfuming from vessels of gold and silver is not allowed, for men or women. Glass and crystal are fine.
cards.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, Book of the Forbidden and the Permitted

checks.q: May a man wear a gold ring?
checks.why: Men may not wear gold. A silver ring of less than one mithqal (about 4.3 g) is allowed.

checks.q: Drinking from a silver cup is…
checks.a: Not allowed for men or women
checks.why: Eating and drinking from gold and silver vessels is not allowed for either.

checks.q: Wearing silk is lawful for…
checks.why: Silk is not lawful for men to wear, and lawful for women.

lessons.title: Lowering the gaze
lessons.about: What may be looked at, according to al-Quduri.

cards.x: A man may not look at a woman who is not his mahram except at her face and hands. If he is not safe from desire, he does not look even at her face, except for a need.
cards.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, Book of the Forbidden and the Permitted

cards.ar: قُل لِّلْمُؤْمِنِينَ يَغُضُّواْ مِنْ أَبْصَٰرِهِمْ وَيَحْفَظُواْ فُرُوجَهُمْ ذَٰلِكَ أَزْكَىٰ لَهُمْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ خَبِيرُ بِمَا يَصْنَعُونَ ﴿٣٠﴾ وَقُل لِّلْمُؤْمِنَٰتِ يَغْضُضْنَ مِنْ أَبْصَٰرِهِنَّ وَيَحْفَظْنَ فُرُوجَهُنَّ وَلَا يُبْدِينَ زِينَتَهُنَّ إِلَّا مَا ظَهَرَ مِنْهَا وَلْيَضْرِبْنَ بِخُمُرِهِنَّ عَلَىٰ جُيُوبِهِنَّ وَلَا يُبْدِينَ زِينَتَهُنَّ إِلَّا لِبُعُولَتِهِنَّ أَوْ ءَابَآئِهِنَّ أَوْ ءَابَآءِ بُعُولَتِهِنَّ أَوْ أَبْنَآئِهِنَّ أَوْ أَبْنَآءِ بُعُولَتِهِنَّ أَوْ إِخْوَٰنِهِنَّ أَوْ بَنِيٓ إِخْوَٰنِهِنَّ أَوْ بَنِيٓ أَخَوَٰتِهِنَّ أَوْ نِسَآئِهِنَّ أَوْ مَا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَٰنُهُنَّ أَوِ التَّـٰبِعِينَ غَيْرِ أُوْلِي الْإِرْبَةِ مِنَ الرِّجَالِ أَوِ الطِّفْلِ الَّذِينَ لَمْ يَظْهَرُواْ عَلَىٰ عَوْرَٰتِ النِّسَآءِ وَلَا يَضْرِبْنَ بِأَرْجُلِهِنَّ لِيُعْلَمَ مَا يُخْفِينَ مِن زِينَتِهِنَّ وَتُوبُوٓاْ إِلَى اللَّهِ جَمِيعًا أَيُّهَ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ ﴿٣١﴾
cards.x: Tell the believing men to lower their gaze and guard their chastity… and tell the believing women to lower their gaze and guard their chastity.
A judge, a witness and a doctor may look as their work requires.
cards.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, Book of the Forbidden and the Permitted

cards.x: A man may look at another man except between the navel and the knee.
cards.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, Book of the Forbidden and the Permitted

checks.q: If a man fears desire, may he look at a non-mahram's face?
checks.why: Al-Quduri: if he is not safe from desire he does not look even at her face, except for a need.

checks.q: Which part of a man may another man not look at?
checks.a: Between the navel and the knee
w: Between the navel and the chest
checks.why: Between the navel and the knee is 'awrah for men.

checks.q: Who may look as their work requires?
checks.why: A judge, a witness and a doctor may look as needed.

lessons.title: Covering, privacy and mixing
lessons.about: What men and women cover, from whom, and the limits between them.

cards.x: A man covers from the navel to below the knees, the knee included, in front of everyone except his wife: in public, at the gym and at sport. Clothes so tight or thin that they show the shape or colour of the skin do not cover properly.
cards.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, Book of what is forbidden and permitted

cards.ar: قُل لِّلْمُؤْمِنِينَ يَغُضُّواْ مِنْ أَبْصَٰرِهِمْ وَيَحْفَظُواْ فُرُوجَهُمْ ذَٰلِكَ أَزْكَىٰ لَهُمْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ خَبِيرُ بِمَا يَصْنَعُونَ ﴿٣٠﴾
cards.x: Tell the believing men to lower their gaze and guard their private parts. That is purer for them. Allah is aware of what they do.

cards.ar: يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا النَّبِيُّ قُل لِّأَزْوَٰجِكَ وَبَنَاتِكَ وَنِسَآءِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ يُدْنِينَ عَلَيْهِنَّ مِن جَلَٰبِيبِهِنَّ ذَٰلِكَ أَدْنَىٰٓ أَن يُعْرَفْنَ فَلَا يُؤْذَيْنَ وَكَانَ اللَّهُ غَفُورٗا رَّحِيمٗا ﴿٥٩﴾
cards.x: O Prophet, tell your wives, your daughters and the women of the believers to draw their outer garments over themselves. That is more fitting, so that they are recognised and not harmed. Allah is Forgiving, Merciful.

A woman covers her whole body before men who are not her mahram, except her face and hands, and her feet according to a strong Hanafi view. Her clothes are loose and not see-through, and her head covering (khimar) covers the hair, neck and chest.
cards.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, Book of what is forbidden and permitted

cards.x: Later Hanafi scholars said a young woman should also cover her face in front of non-mahram men when there is fear of fitnah (men looking with desire), and many say that is the case in most places today. Follow a qualified teacher on this.
cards.src: Ibn 'Abidin, Radd al-Muhtar, the conditions of prayer

cards.x: In front of her mahram men (father, brother, son, uncle and so on) a woman may show her head, hair, face, neck, chest, arms and shins, but not her back, stomach or thighs.
cards.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, Book of what is forbidden and permitted

cards.x: A woman may see of another Muslim woman what a man may see of another man: everything except from the navel to the knee.
cards.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, Book of what is forbidden and permitted

cards.x: A man may look at a non-mahram woman's face and hands only without desire; if he fears desire, only when there is a need, like a doctor, a witness or someone proposing marriage. Touching a non-mahram of the opposite sex, including shaking hands, is not allowed except for a real need such as medical treatment.
cards.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, Book of what is forbidden and permitted

cards.x: A man and a non-mahram woman must not be alone together, in a car, an office, a home or a lesson, unless a mahram is present: 'No man should be alone with a woman except with a mahram.'
cards.src: Sahih al-Bukhari (5233), Covering, privacy and mixing

cards.x: At work, study or the masjid, keep dealings with the opposite sex to what is needed, polite and businesslike: no flirting, no casual chat, no soft talk meant to attract. Avoid gatherings built on free mixing.
The Prophet ﷺ cursed men who make themselves like women and women who make themselves like men, in dress, manner and appearance.
cards.src: Sahih al-Bukhari (5885), Covering, privacy and mixing

checks.q: A man's 'awrah is from…
checks.a: The navel to below the knees
checks.why: From the navel to below the knees, with the knee included in the Hanafi school.
checks.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, Book of what is forbidden and permitted

checks.q: In front of her brother, a woman may uncover her…
checks.why: Mahrams may see the head, chest, arms and shins, not the back, stomach or thighs.
checks.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, Book of what is forbidden and permitted

checks.q: A colleague of the opposite gender offers you a lift home, just the two of you. In the Shari'ah this is…
w: Fine if the journey is short
checks.why: It is khalwah, being alone with a non-mahram, which is forbidden.

checks.q: Shaking hands with a non-mahram of the opposite sex is…
w: Allowed if there is no desire
checks.why: Touching a non-mahram of the opposite sex is not allowed, except for a real need such as medical care.
checks.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, Book of what is forbidden and permitted

checks.q: Tight clothes that show the body's shape…
w: Are fine if they are long
Are fine for men in any case
Are a problem in prayer alone
checks.why: Covering means hiding the shape and colour, not just the skin.
checks.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, Book of what is forbidden and permitted

lessons.title: Music and singing
lessons.about: The Hanafi position on instruments, what is allowed, and what to do when music is all around you.

cards.x: Playing musical instruments (ma'azif), and choosing to listen to them, is haram in the Hanafi school, as Imam Abu Hanifah and his companions held. This includes stringed, wind and keyboard instruments and drums, other than the daff.
cards.src: al-Hidayah, Book of what is disliked

cards.ar: وَمِنَ النَّاسِ مَن يَشْتَرِي لَهْوَ الْحَدِيثِ لِيُضِلَّ عَن سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٖ وَيَتَّخِذَهَا هُزُوًا أُوْلَـٰٓئِكَ لَهُمْ عَذَابٞ مُّهِينٞ ﴿٦﴾
cards.x: Among people is he who buys idle talk to lead others away from the path of Allah without knowledge, and takes it in mockery. For such there is a humiliating punishment.
The Prophet ﷺ said: 'There will be people from my Ummah who will make lawful fornication, silk, wine and musical instruments.'
Allah says: 'Among people is he who buys idle talk to lead others away from the path of Allah without knowledge.' 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud رضي الله عنه swore three times that it means singing.
Beating the daff, a simple frame drum, is allowed to announce a wedding and on the days of Eid, as girls did in the Prophet's ﷺ house.

Singing and nasheeds with the voice alone, with good words, praise of Allah and His Messenger ﷺ, qasidahs and poetry, are allowed, as long as they are free of instruments, indecent words and anything that stirs desire.
cards.src: al-Hidayah, Book of what is disliked

cards.x: There is no sin in hearing music you did not choose, in a shop, on the street or in an advert. The sin is in sitting to listen and enjoy it. Do not linger; turn it off or move away when you can.
cards.src: al-Hidayah, Book of what is disliked

cards.x: The heart that leaves music needs something better: the Qur'an, dhikr, salawat and nasheeds. Choose versions without music when you can, and ask a teacher about voice effects that imitate instruments.

checks.q: In the Hanafi school, listening to music with instruments by choice is…
w: Allowed if the words are good
checks.why: Instruments are haram to play and to listen to by choice.
checks.src: al-Hidayah, Book of what is disliked

checks.q: Which is allowed at a wedding?
checks.a: Beating the daff to announce it
w: Any music, since it is a celebration
checks.why: The daff announces a wedding; other instruments are not allowed.

checks.q: Music is playing in a supermarket while you shop. You are…
checks.a: Not sinful, but don't stay to enjoy it
w: Free to listen, since you did not choose it
checks.why: Hearing without choosing is not the sin; listening to enjoy it is.
checks.src: al-Hidayah, Book of what is disliked

checks.q: A nasheed with the voice only, praising the Prophet ﷺ, is…
checks.why: The voice alone, with good words, is allowed.
checks.src: al-Hidayah, Book of what is disliked

lessons.title: Riba (interest)
lessons.about: What riba is, and why it is so serious.

cards.x: Riba is haram. The Prophet ﷺ cursed the one who consumes riba, the one who pays it, the one who writes it and its two witnesses, and said: they are all the same.

cards.ar: الَّذِينَ يَأْكُلُونَ الرِّبَوٰاْ لَا يَقُومُونَ إِلَّا كَمَا يَقُومُ الَّذِي يَتَخَبَّطُهُ الشَّيْطَٰنُ مِنَ الْمَسِّ ذَٰلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمْ قَالُوٓاْ إِنَّمَا الْبَيْعُ مِثْلُ الرِّبَوٰاْ وَأَحَلَّ اللَّهُ الْبَيْعَ وَحَرَّمَ الرِّبَوٰاْ فَمَن جَآءَهُ مَوْعِظَةٞ مِّن رَّبِّهِ فَانتَهَىٰ فَلَهُ مَا سَلَفَ وَأَمْرُهُٓ إِلَى اللَّهِ وَمَنْ عَادَ فَأُوْلَـٰٓئِكَ أَصْحَٰبُ النَّارِ هُمْ فِيهَا خَٰلِدُونَ ﴿٢٧٥﴾
cards.x: Those who consume riba will not stand except as one stands whom Shaytan has struck with madness. That is because they say trade is just like riba, but Allah has made trade lawful and riba unlawful.

cards.ar: يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ اتَّقُواْ اللَّهَ وَذَرُواْ مَا بَقِيَ مِنَ الرِّبَوٰٓاْ إِن كُنتُم مُّؤْمِنِينَ ﴿٢٧٨﴾ فَإِن لَّمْ تَفْعَلُواْ فَأْذَنُواْ بِحَرْبٖ مِّنَ اللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ وَإِن تُبْتُمْ فَلَكُمْ رُءُوسُ أَمْوَٰلِكُمْ لَا تَظْلِمُونَ وَلَا تُظْلَمُونَ ﴿٢٧٩﴾
cards.x: O you who believe, be mindful of Allah and give up what remains of riba, if you are believers. If you do not, then be warned of war from Allah and His Messenger.
Al-Quduri: riba is in anything measured by volume or weight, when sold for the same kind with an increase. Like for like is allowed; with an increase it is not.
Al-Ghazali lists riba among the common wrongs of the marketplace that must be stopped.
cards.src: Ihya' 'Ulum al-Din, Book of Commanding Good

checks.q: Who did the Prophet ﷺ curse in the hadith on riba?
checks.a: The one who takes it, pays it, writes it and witnesses it
w: The one who takes it, not the one who pays
The one who takes it and the one who pays it
No one: he only warned against it
checks.why: All four were cursed, and he said they are all the same.

checks.q: Selling a kilo of dates for two kilos of dates, on the spot, is…
checks.why: Same kind, weighed or measured, with an increase is riba.

checks.q: Selling gold for the same weight of gold, hand to hand, is…
checks.why: Like for like of the same kind is allowed.

lessons.title: Money: riba, loans and earning
lessons.about: How to keep your income and spending halal in a world built on interest.

cards.x: Riba (interest) is among the major sins. Allah made trade lawful and riba unlawful, and told those who will not give it up to expect war from Allah and His Messenger.

cards.ar: يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْ إِنَّمَا الْخَمْرُ وَالْمَيْسِرُ وَالْأَنصَابُ وَالْأَزْلَٰمُ رِجْسٞ مِّنْ عَمَلِ الشَّيْطَٰنِ فَاجْتَنِبُوهُ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ ﴿٩٠﴾
cards.x: O you who believe, wine, gambling, idols and divining arrows are only filth from the work of Shaytan, so avoid it, that you may succeed.

cards.ar: الَّذِينَ يَأْكُلُونَ الرِّبَوٰاْ لَا يَقُومُونَ إِلَّا كَمَا يَقُومُ الَّذِي يَتَخَبَّطُهُ الشَّيْطَٰنُ مِنَ الْمَسِّ ذَٰلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمْ قَالُوٓاْ إِنَّمَا الْبَيْعُ مِثْلُ الرِّبَوٰاْ وَأَحَلَّ اللَّهُ الْبَيْعَ وَحَرَّمَ الرِّبَوٰاْ فَمَن جَآءَهُ مَوْعِظَةٞ مِّن رَّبِّهِ فَانتَهَىٰ فَلَهُ مَا سَلَفَ وَأَمْرُهُٓ إِلَى اللَّهِ وَمَنْ عَادَ فَأُوْلَـٰٓئِكَ أَصْحَٰبُ النَّارِ هُمْ فِيهَا خَٰلِدُونَ ﴿٢٧٥﴾
cards.x: Allah has made trade lawful and riba unlawful.

cards.ar: يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ اتَّقُواْ اللَّهَ وَذَرُواْ مَا بَقِيَ مِنَ الرِّبَوٰٓاْ إِن كُنتُم مُّؤْمِنِينَ ﴿٢٧٨﴾ فَإِن لَّمْ تَفْعَلُواْ فَأْذَنُواْ بِحَرْبٖ مِّنَ اللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ وَإِن تُبْتُمْ فَلَكُمْ رُءُوسُ أَمْوَٰلِكُمْ لَا تَظْلِمُونَ وَلَا تُظْلَمُونَ ﴿٢٧٩﴾
cards.x: O you who believe, be mindful of Allah and give up what remains of riba, if you are believers. If you do not, then be warned of war from Allah and His Messenger.

Any loan where you must pay back more than you borrowed is riba: a mortgage with interest, a personal loan, car finance with interest, an overdraft or a credit card that charges interest. There is no exception for buying a home, however normal it has become.

The Prophet ﷺ cursed the one who takes riba, the one who pays it, the one who writes it and its two witnesses, and said they are all the same. So a job that arranges or writes interest contracts is not halal income.
Do not take interest on savings. If a bank has paid interest into your account, do not use it for yourself: give it away to the poor without intending reward, to rid yourself of it.
Gambling is haram in every form: betting, lottery tickets, scratchcards, and paid entries where you may win more than you paid or lose it.
Earning a halal living is an obligation. Before taking out insurance, a pension, investments or any finance product, ask a qualified scholar: many contain riba or gambling hidden in the terms.
cards.src: Ihya' 'Ulum al-Din, Book of Earning and Livelihood

checks.q: Is a mortgage with interest allowed to buy a family home?
checks.a: No; any loan with interest is riba
w: Yes, a home is a necessity
Yes, if the rate is low
Yes, for a first home only
checks.why: Riba is haram whatever it is used for.

checks.q: A bank has paid interest into your savings. What do you do?
checks.a: Give it to the poor without intending reward
checks.why: It is not yours to use; you rid yourself of it.

checks.q: Buying a lottery ticket is…
w: Allowed if it is for charity
Allowed if the prize is small
checks.why: A lottery is gambling (maysir), which the Qur'an forbids, whatever the prize goes to.

checks.q: A shop offers 'buy now, pay later', with interest charged if you pay late. May you sign up?
checks.a: No: agreeing to interest is riba
w: Yes, if you plan to pay on time
checks.why: Signing a contract that includes interest is agreeing to riba, even if you hope never to pay it.

lessons.title: Honesty in trade
lessons.about: Cheating in the market, from al-Ghazali.

cards.x: Al-Ghazali names, among the common wrongs of the market, lying about what you paid for goods so you can sell at a 'profit'. Whoever knows of it should tell the buyer.
cards.src: Ihya' 'Ulum al-Din, Book of Commanding Good: wrongs of the market

cards.ar: وَيْلٞ لِّلْمُطَفِّفِينَ ﴿١﴾ الَّذِينَ إِذَا اكْتَالُواْ عَلَى النَّاسِ يَسْتَوْفُونَ ﴿٢﴾ وَإِذَا كَالُوهُمْ أَو وَّزَنُوهُمْ يُخْسِرُونَ ﴿٣﴾
cards.x: Woe to those who give short measure: who, when they take from people, take in full, but when they measure or weigh for them, give them less.
Hiding a fault in what you sell is also forbidden. Whoever knows the fault must point it out, or he is content with his brother's loss.
cards.src: Ihya' 'Ulum al-Din, Book of Commanding Good: wrongs of the market

cards.x: Giving short weight or short measure must be stopped. The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Whoever cheats us is not one of us.'
cards.src: Ihya', wrongs of the market; Hadith, Sahih Muslim

checks.q: Saying 'I bought it for ten' when you paid less is…
checks.why: Al-Ghazali lists lying in the cost price among the wrongs of the market.

checks.q: If you know a fault in an item you are selling…
checks.why: Hiding it means being content with your brother's loss.

checks.q: The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Whoever cheats us…'
checks.why: The hadith in Sahih Muslim.

lessons.title: Oaths, vows and their expiation
lessons.about: What counts as an oath, what breaking one costs, and when a vow binds you.

cards.x: An oath is made by Allah, one of His names or one of His attributes: 'Wallahi', 'Billahi', 'By the might of Allah'. Swearing by the Prophet ﷺ, the Ka'bah, your parents or your life is not an oath, and it is forbidden: 'Whoever swears, let him swear by Allah or stay silent.' Later Hanafi scholars gave the fatwa that swearing by the Qur'an counts as an oath, because people mean it as one.
cards.src: Sahih al-Bukhari (2679), Oaths, vows and their expiation

cards.ar: لَا يُؤَاخِذُكُمُ اللَّهُ بِاللَّغْوِ فِيٓ أَيْمَٰنِكُمْ وَلَٰكِن يُؤَاخِذُكُم بِمَا عَقَّدتُّمُ الْأَيْمَٰنَ فَكَفَّـٰرَتُهُٓ إِطْعَامُ عَشَرَةِ مَسَٰكِينَ مِنْ أَوْسَطِ مَا تُطْعِمُونَ أَهْلِيكُمْ أَوْ كِسْوَتُهُمْ أَوْ تَحْرِيرُ رَقَبَةٖ فَمَن لَّمْ يَجِدْ فَصِيَامُ ثَلَٰثَةِ أَيَّامٖ ذَٰلِكَ كَفَّـٰرَةُ أَيْمَٰنِكُمْ إِذَا حَلَفْتُمْ وَاحْفَظُوٓاْ أَيْمَٰنَكُمْ كَذَٰلِكَ يُبَيِّنُ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ ءَايَٰتِهِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَشْكُرُونَ ﴿٨٩﴾
cards.x: Allah will not take you to account for your unintended oaths, but He will take you to account for the oaths you make in earnest. Its expiation is feeding ten poor people with the average of what you feed your own families, or clothing them, or freeing a slave. Whoever cannot find the means, then fasting three days. That is the expiation of your oaths when you have sworn. And guard your oaths. Thus Allah makes clear His signs to you, that you may be grateful.

cards.ar: وَلَا تَجْعَلُواْ اللَّهَ عُرْضَةٗ لِّأَيْمَٰنِكُمْ أَن تَبَرُّواْ وَتَتَّقُواْ وَتُصْلِحُواْ بَيْنَ النَّاسِ وَاللَّهُ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٞ ﴿٢٢٤﴾
cards.x: Do not make Allah's name an excuse in your oaths against doing good, being mindful of Him and making peace between people. Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.

1) The false oath (ghamus): swearing about the past while knowing it is a lie. It is a major sin with no expiation except sincere repentance. 2) The mistaken oath (laghw): swearing about the past believing it true when it was not; we hope Allah does not hold it against him. 3) The binding oath: swearing to do or not do something in the future. Breaking it requires the expiation.

Feed ten poor people two full meals each, or give each the value of half a sa' of wheat (like the sadaqat al-fitr amount); or give each of them a garment; or free a slave. Only if you can do none of these, fast three days in a row. It is paid after the oath is broken, not before.

If you swear to a sin, such as not speaking to your parents or not praying, you must break the oath and pay the expiation. The Prophet ﷺ said: if you swear to something and see something better, expiate your oath and do what is better.
cards.src: Sahih al-Bukhari (6622), Oaths, vows and their expiation

cards.x: 'Wallahi I'll come tomorrow' is a binding oath even if said out of habit, and if broken it needs the expiation. Saying 'If I do this, I'm a kafir' also counts as an oath in the Hanafi school. Guard the tongue: do not make Allah's name a casual habit.

A vow to Allah to do an act of worship of a kind that is wajib, such as fasting, praying, giving charity or i'tikaf, is binding: 'I vow to fast three days', or 'If I recover, I will give £100 in charity' once you recover. A vow to do a sin is not carried out.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, when a vow must be fulfilled

cards.x: The Prophet ﷺ discouraged vows: a vow does not change what is decreed; it only draws something out of the miser. Make du'a and give charity freely instead of bargaining.
cards.src: Sahih al-Bukhari (6608), Oaths, vows and their expiation

cards.x: The specific day, place, coin or poor person named in a vow does not bind. A vow to pray two rak'ahs in Makkah is fulfilled by praying them anywhere, and a vow to give to one poor person is fulfilled by giving to another.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, when a vow must be fulfilled

checks.q: He swore 'Wallahi I won't buy a phone this year', then bought one. He owes…
checks.a: The expiation for a broken oath
checks.why: It was a binding oath about the future, and he broke it.

checks.q: Swearing by Allah about the past while knowing it is a lie is…
checks.why: The false oath (ghamus) is too grave for an expiation; only sincere repentance.

checks.q: When may the oath expiation be fasted?
checks.a: When you cannot feed or clothe ten poor
checks.why: Fasting three days in a row comes only when the others are impossible.

checks.q: 'I swear by my mother's life' is…
checks.why: Swear by Allah or stay silent.

checks.q: She vowed: 'If I pass my exam, I'll fast three days.' She passed. She…
w: May choose to fast or not
Must pay the oath expiation instead
checks.why: A vow tied to a condition binds once the condition happens.
checks.src: Nur al-Idah, when a vow must be fulfilled

title: Marriage, family and rights
sub: Marriage, the rights of spouses, parents, children, relatives and neighbours

lessons.title: Before marriage
lessons.about: Choosing a spouse, seeing them, and keeping the engagement halal.

cards.x: Marriage is a stressed sunnah, and it becomes wajib for someone who fears falling into zina and can afford it. The Prophet ﷺ said: whoever is able to marry, let him marry, for it lowers the gaze and guards chastity.

cards.ar: وَأَنكِحُواْ الْأَيَٰمَىٰ مِنكُمْ وَالصَّـٰلِحِينَ مِنْ عِبَادِكُمْ وَإِمَآئِكُمْ إِن يَكُونُواْ فُقَرَآءَ يُغْنِهِمُ اللَّهُ مِن فَضْلِهِ وَاللَّهُ وَٰسِعٌ عَلِيمٞ ﴿٣٢﴾
cards.x: Marry those among you who are single, and the righteous among your servants. If they are poor, Allah will enrich them from His bounty.

The Prophet ﷺ said a woman is married for four things: her wealth, her lineage, her beauty and her religion. 'Choose the one with religion and you will prosper.' The same holds for choosing a husband: look first at his deen and character.

It is sunnah for a man to see the woman he intends to marry, her face and hands, before proposing: the Prophet ﷺ said it is more likely to bring love between you. Pray istikharah and ask people who know them.

cards.t: The engagement is not a marriage
cards.x: An engagement (khitbah) is only a promise. Until the nikah they are still strangers to each other: no being alone together, no touching, and no private talk beyond what is needed. 'No man is alone with a woman but Shaytan is the third.'
Do not propose to someone who is already engaged to another until he withdraws or is turned down.

checks.q: What did the Prophet ﷺ say to choose a spouse for above all?
checks.why: 'Choose the one with religion and you will prosper.'

checks.q: May an engaged couple spend time alone together?
checks.a: No; they are not married yet
checks.why: The engagement is only a promise; seclusion is not allowed until the nikah.

checks.q: Before proposing, a man may look at…
checks.why: Looking at the face and hands with the intention of marriage is sunnah.

lessons.title: The marriage contract
lessons.about: What makes a nikah valid, the mahr, consent and the walimah.

cards.x: A nikah is made by an offer and an acceptance, in one sitting, spoken in the presence of two adult Muslim witnesses: two men, or one man and two women.

cards.ar: وَمِنْ ءَايَٰتِهِٓ أَنْ خَلَقَ لَكُم مِّنْ أَنفُسِكُمْ أَزْوَٰجٗا لِّتَسْكُنُوٓاْ إِلَيْهَا وَجَعَلَ بَيْنَكُم مَّوَدَّةٗ وَرَحْمَةً إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَأٓيَٰتٖ لِّقَوْمٖ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ ﴿٢١﴾
cards.x: Among His signs is that He created for you spouses from among yourselves so that you may find tranquillity in them, and He placed between you affection and mercy.

No one may marry an adult woman without her consent. In the Hanafi school her marriage is valid without her guardian, but it is sunnah for him to arrange it, and he may object if the husband is not a suitable match (kafa'ah).

The mahr is the wife's own property, owed by the husband, whether or not it was named; if none was named she is owed a mahr like that of women of her family. In the Hanafi school it is at least ten dirhams of silver.

A Muslim man may marry a Muslim woman, or a chaste Christian or Jewish woman, though the Hanafi scholars dislike it, more so where it endangers the children's faith. A Muslim woman may only marry a Muslim man.
A man may marry up to four, on condition of justice between them in nights, housing and spending. 'If you fear you will not be just, then one.' (al-Nisa' 3)
It is sunnah for the husband to hold a wedding meal (walimah) after the marriage, without waste or showing off, and to invite the poor as well as the rich.

checks.q: What makes a nikah valid?
checks.a: Offer and acceptance before two witnesses
checks.why: Al-Quduri: offer and acceptance, with two witnesses.

checks.q: Whose property is the mahr?
checks.why: It is owed to her and belongs to her alone.

checks.q: May a Muslim woman marry a Christian man?
w: Yes, if the children are Muslim
checks.why: A Muslim woman may only marry a Muslim man.

checks.q: What is the condition for marrying more than one wife?
checks.a: Justice between them in nights, housing and spending
w: Being able to afford a large house
checks.why: If he fears injustice, one only.

lessons.title: Whom you may never marry
lessons.about: The mahram relatives, by blood, by marriage and by nursing.

cards.x: A man may never marry his mother or grandmothers, daughters or granddaughters, sisters, aunts (father's or mother's sisters), or nieces. These are his mahrams: he may be alone with them and travel with them.

cards.ar: حُرِّمَتْ عَلَيْكُمْ أُمَّهَٰتُكُمْ وَبَنَاتُكُمْ وَأَخَوَٰتُكُمْ وَعَمَّـٰتُكُمْ وَخَٰلَٰتُكُمْ وَبَنَاتُ الْأَخِ وَبَنَاتُ الْأُخْتِ وَأُمَّهَٰتُكُمُ الَّـٰتِيٓ أَرْضَعْنَكُمْ وَأَخَوَٰتُكُم مِّنَ الرَّضَٰعَةِ وَأُمَّهَٰتُ نِسَآئِكُمْ وَرَبَـٰٓئِبُكُمُ الَّـٰتِي فِي حُجُورِكُم مِّن نِّسَآئِكُمُ الَّـٰتِي دَخَلْتُم بِهِنَّ فَإِن لَّمْ تَكُونُواْ دَخَلْتُم بِهِنَّ فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْكُمْ وَحَلَـٰٓئِلُ أَبْنَآئِكُمُ الَّذِينَ مِنْ أَصْلَٰبِكُمْ وَأَن تَجْمَعُواْ بَيْنَ الْأُخْتَيْنِ إِلَّا مَا قَدْ سَلَفَ إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ غَفُورٗا رَّحِيمٗا ﴿٢٣﴾
cards.x: Forbidden to you are your mothers, your daughters, your sisters, your fathers' sisters, your mothers' sisters, your brothers' daughters, your sisters' daughters, your mothers who nursed you, your sisters through nursing, your wives' mothers…

Also forbidden for ever: his wife's mother, his wife's daughter once he has consummated the marriage with the mother, his son's wife, and his father's wife. And while married, he may not combine two sisters, or a woman and her aunt.

Whatever blood makes forbidden, nursing makes forbidden. In the Hanafi school even a little milk counts, if the child nursed within the first two years (Abu Hanifah said thirty months). So the woman who nursed you is like your mother, and her children like your siblings.
Cousins, a brother-in-law or sister-in-law, and the spouse's siblings are not mahrams: they may marry, and the rules of covering and not being alone together apply to them.

checks.q: Is a cousin a mahram?
checks.why: Cousins are not mahram: they may marry, and the rules of covering apply between them.

checks.q: A woman nursed a baby boy within his first two years. Her daughter is to him…
checks.why: Nursing within the first two years makes her his foster-mother and her daughter his foster-sister, whom he may never marry.

checks.q: May a man be married to two sisters at the same time?
checks.why: Combining two sisters is forbidden.

lessons.title: The rights of the wife
lessons.about: What a husband owes his wife, before Allah and before the court.

cards.x: 'Live with them in kindness.' The Prophet ﷺ said: the most complete of the believers in faith are those best in character, and the best of you are the best to their wives.

cards.ar: يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ لَا يَحِلُّ لَكُمْ أَن تَرِثُواْ النِّسَآءَ كَرْهٗا وَلَا تَعْضُلُوهُنَّ لِتَذْهَبُواْ بِبَعْضِ مَآ ءَاتَيْتُمُوهُنَّ إِلَّآ أَن يَأْتِينَ بِفَٰحِشَةٖ مُّبَيِّنَةٖ وَعَاشِرُوهُنَّ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ فَإِن كَرِهْتُمُوهُنَّ فَعَسَىٰٓ أَن تَكْرَهُواْ شَيْـٔٗا وَيَجْعَلَ اللَّهُ فِيهِ خَيْرٗا كَثِيرٗا ﴿١٩﴾
cards.x: …and live with them in kindness. If you dislike them, it may be that you dislike something in which Allah has placed much good.
Her mahr is hers, and so is everything she owns or earns. The husband has no right to her money, and she is not required to spend on the household.
He must provide her food, clothing and housing according to his means, even if she is wealthy. A man's spending on his family, seeking Allah's reward, is charity.

In the Hanafi school she has the right to her own quarters, with a door she can lock and a place to cook, where none of his relatives live with her unless she agrees. Living with his parents is a kindness she may choose, not a duty.

He gives her his company and affection, does not stay away from her bed for long, keeps her secrets, and teaches her the religion or lets her learn it. With more than one wife, he is just between them.
cards.src: Ihya' 'Ulum al-Din, Book of the Etiquette of Marriage

cards.x: The Hanafi jurists say a court cannot force her to cook or clean, as it is not part of the contract. But serving the home is from good companionship, and the women of the Companions, Fatimah رضي الله عنها among them, did so.

checks.q: Whose is the money a wife earns?
checks.why: Her wealth is hers; maintenance is on him.

checks.q: In the Hanafi school, may a wife ask for housing separate from her in-laws?
w: No, she must live with them
checks.why: Al-Quduri: he houses her where none of his family live, unless she chooses.

checks.q: Who must pay for the household's food, clothing and housing?
checks.a: The husband, even if the wife is wealthy
checks.why: Maintenance is the husband's duty.

checks.q: The Prophet ﷺ said: 'The best of you are…'
checks.why: Narrated by al-Tirmidhi.

lessons.title: The rights of the husband
lessons.about: What a wife owes her husband.

cards.x: She follows him in what is right and reasonable in their married life. No one is obeyed in disobedience to Allah: if he tells her to sin, she refuses, gently.
cards.src: Ihya' 'Ulum al-Din, Book of the Etiquette of Marriage

cards.ar: وَالْمُطَلَّقَٰتُ يَتَرَبَّصْنَ بِأَنفُسِهِنَّ ثَلَٰثَةَ قُرُوٓءٖ وَلَا يَحِلُّ لَهُنَّ أَن يَكْتُمْنَ مَا خَلَقَ اللَّهُ فِيٓ أَرْحَامِهِنَّ إِن كُنَّ يُؤْمِنَّ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْأٓخِرِ وَبُعُولَتُهُنَّ أَحَقُّ بِرَدِّهِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ إِنْ أَرَادُوٓاْ إِصْلَٰحٗا وَلَهُنَّ مِثْلُ الَّذِي عَلَيْهِنَّ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ وَلِلرِّجَالِ عَلَيْهِنَّ دَرَجَةٞ وَاللَّهُ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمٌ ﴿٢٢٨﴾
cards.x: And they have rights like those upon them, in kindness, and men have a degree above them. Allah is Mighty, Wise.
She does not let into his home anyone he dislikes, and does not leave the home without his permission except for need, such as visiting her parents, which the Hanafi books allow once a week.
She guards his wealth, his honour and his secrets in his absence, and does not spend his money without his permission beyond what is customary.
cards.src: Ihya' 'Ulum al-Din, Book of the Etiquette of Marriage

cards.x: Each has a right to closeness from the other, and neither should refuse the other without a valid reason such as illness or menstruation.
cards.src: Ihya' 'Ulum al-Din, Book of the Etiquette of Marriage

cards.x: The Prophet ﷺ said: if a woman prays her five, fasts her month, guards her chastity and obeys her husband, she will be told: enter Paradise by whichever gate you wish.
cards.src: Musnad Ahmad, hadith of 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf

checks.q: A husband tells his wife to do something sinful. She…
checks.why: There is no obedience to a creature in disobedience to the Creator.
checks.src: Ihya' 'Ulum al-Din, Book of the Etiquette of Marriage

checks.q: May a wife let into the home someone her husband dislikes?
w: Yes, if they are her friends
checks.why: Guarding the home is his right.
checks.src: Ihya' 'Ulum al-Din, Book of the Etiquette of Marriage

checks.q: How often do the Hanafi books allow a wife to visit her parents?
checks.why: Visiting parents is her right even if he dislikes it.

lessons.title: Living together
lessons.about: The manners of intimacy, and what to do when there is discord.

cards.x: Say: 'Bismillah. Allahumma jannibna al-shaytan wa jannib al-shaytana ma razaqtana' (In the name of Allah. O Allah, keep Shaytan away from us and from what You give us).

cards.ar: وَإِنْ خِفْتُمْ شِقَاقَ بَيْنِهِمَا فَابْعَثُواْ حَكَمٗا مِّنْ أَهْلِهِ وَحَكَمٗا مِّنْ أَهْلِهَآ إِن يُرِيدَآ إِصْلَٰحٗا يُوَفِّقِ اللَّهُ بَيْنَهُمَآ إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ عَلِيمًا خَبِيرٗا ﴿٣٥﴾
cards.x: If you fear a split between the two, appoint an arbitrator from his family and an arbitrator from hers. If they want reconciliation, Allah will bring them together.
Intercourse during menstruation or nifas is haram, as is anal intercourse at any time. After intercourse ghusl is required before prayer.
The Prophet ﷺ said among the worst people before Allah on the Day of Judgement is a man who is intimate with his wife and she with him, and then he spreads her secret.

The Qur'an's way is gentle steps: advice, then distance in bed, then family arbitrators from both sides to reconcile them (al-Nisa' 34–35). The scholars restricted anything beyond that to the lightest gesture that leaves no mark, never the face, and the Prophet ﷺ never struck a woman or a servant with his ﷺ hand.
The Prophet ﷺ said: let no believing man hate a believing woman; if he dislikes one trait in her, he will be pleased with another.

checks.q: Intercourse during menstruation is…
checks.why: It is forbidden until her bleeding ends.

checks.q: What does the Qur'an prescribe when a couple's dispute grows serious?
w: Ask the imam to decide alone
checks.why: Allah says to appoint an arbitrator from his family and one from hers, to reconcile them (al-Nisa' 35).

checks.q: Did the Prophet ﷺ ever strike a woman?
checks.why: 'A'ishah رضي الله عنها reported he never struck a woman or servant with his hand.

lessons.title: Divorce, khul' and 'iddah
lessons.about: Ending a marriage the right way, and the waiting period.

cards.x: Talaq takes effect when said clearly, even in anger, by text, or as a joke: 'three things are serious in earnest and in jest: marriage, divorce and taking back.' Only someone who has lost his mind entirely is excused.
cards.src: Sunan Abi Dawud, Book of Divorce

cards.ar: الطَّلَٰقُ مَرَّتَانِ فَإِمْسَاكُ بِمَعْرُوفٍ أَوْ تَسْرِيحُ بِإِحْسَٰنٖ وَلَا يَحِلُّ لَكُمْ أَن تَأْخُذُواْ مِمَّآ ءَاتَيْتُمُوهُنَّ شَيْـًٔا إِلَّآ أَن يَخَافَآ أَلَّا يُقِيمَا حُدُودَ اللَّهِ فَإِنْ خِفْتُمْ أَلَّا يُقِيمَا حُدُودَ اللَّهِ فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْهِمَا فِيمَا افْتَدَتْ بِهِ تِلْكَ حُدُودُ اللَّهِ فَلَا تَعْتَدُوهَا وَمَن يَتَعَدَّ حُدُودَ اللَّهِ فَأُوْلَـٰٓئِكَ هُمُ الظَّـٰلِمُونَ ﴿٢٢٩﴾
cards.x: Divorce is twice; then either keep her in kindness or release her with good.
After one or two talaqs (raj'i), the husband may take her back during the 'iddah without a new nikah. After the 'iddah they need a new nikah, with her consent and a new mahr.

After three talaqs she is not lawful to him until she genuinely marries another man and that marriage ends. A pre-arranged 'halalah' to get around this is condemned: the Prophet ﷺ cursed the one who does it and the one it is done for.

If a wife wishes to leave and he will not divorce her, she may offer to return the mahr or something else in exchange for her release. If the fault is his, it is disliked for him to take anything; if it is hers, he should not take more than he gave.

Divorced and menstruating: three periods. No periods (young or past menopause): three months. Pregnant: until she gives birth. Widowed: four months and ten days. During it she stays in her home, and may not be proposed to openly; a widow also leaves adornment and perfume.

checks.q: A man says 'I divorce you' as a joke. It…
checks.why: Divorce is serious even in jest.
checks.src: Sunan Abi Dawud, Book of Divorce

checks.q: After one talaq, during the 'iddah, the husband may…
checks.a: Take her back without a new nikah
w: Take her back after another marriage
Take her back with a new mahr
checks.why: This is a revocable (raj'i) divorce.

checks.q: What is the 'iddah of a pregnant woman?
checks.why: Al-Talaq 4.

checks.q: What is khul'?
checks.a: The wife gives something back in return for her release
w: The husband divorces three times at once
A judge ends the marriage for a defect
The couple live apart for a set time
checks.why: Agreed separation at the wife's request.

lessons.title: The rights of parents
lessons.about: Honouring your parents, in their lives and after them.

cards.x: Allah joined thanks to Him with thanks to parents: 'Be grateful to Me and to your parents.' Disobeying parents is among the greatest of the major sins.
cards.src: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Good Manners (5976)

cards.ar: وَقَضَىٰ رَبُّكَ أَلَّا تَعْبُدُوٓاْ إِلَّآ إِيَّاهُ وَبِالْوَٰلِدَيْنِ إِحْسَٰنًا إِمَّا يَبْلُغَنَّ عِندَكَ الْكِبَرَ أَحَدُهُمَآ أَوْ كِلَاهُمَا فَلَا تَقُل لَّهُمَآ أُفّٖ وَلَا تَنْهَرْهُمَا وَقُل لَّهُمَا قَوْلٗا كَرِيمٗا ﴿٢٣﴾ وَاخْفِضْ لَهُمَا جَنَاحَ الذُّلِّ مِنَ الرَّحْمَةِ وَقُل رَّبِّ ارْحَمْهُمَا كَمَا رَبَّيَانِي صَغِيرٗا ﴿٢٤﴾
cards.x: Your Lord has decreed that you worship none but Him, and be good to parents. If one or both reach old age with you, do not say to them even 'uff', nor scold them, but speak to them with noble words. Lower to them the wing of humility out of mercy, and say: My Lord, have mercy on them as they raised me when I was small.

cards.ar: وَوَصَّيْنَا الْإِنسَٰنَ بِوَٰلِدَيْهِ حَمَلَتْهُ أُمُّهُ وَهْنًا عَلَىٰ وَهْنٖ وَفِصَٰلُهُ فِي عَامَيْنِ أَنِ اشْكُرْ لِي وَلِوَٰلِدَيْكَ إِلَيَّ الْمَصِيرُ ﴿١٤﴾
