cards.x: We enjoined on man care for his parents: his mother carried him, weakness upon weakness… Be grateful to Me and to your parents; to Me is the return.
A man asked who most deserves his good company. The Prophet ﷺ said: your mother, your mother, your mother, then your father. In another hadith (al-Nasa'i), Paradise lies at her feet.
cards.src: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Good Manners (5971)

cards.x: Obey them in all that is not sin, speak gently, never say even 'uff', serve them, ask their permission before long travel, and spend on them if they are in need: in the Hanafi school this is wajib on a child who can.

cards.t: Even if they are not Muslim
cards.x: If they are not Muslim, you still keep them company in this world with kindness, but do not obey them in leaving Islam or in sin.
The Prophet ﷺ said: the pleasure of the Lord is in the pleasure of the parent, and the anger of the Lord is in the anger of the parent.
Keep honouring them: make du'a and ask forgiveness for them, fulfil their promises, keep ties with their relatives, and honour their friends.
cards.src: Sunan Abi Dawud, Book of Good Manners

cards.x: Marriage does not end your duty to your parents, and your parents' rights do not cancel your spouse's. Give each their right without wronging the other.
cards.src: Ihya' 'Ulum al-Din, Book of the Etiquette of Marriage

checks.q: Your parents tell you to do something sinful. What do you do?
checks.a: Refuse gently, and keep being kind to them
checks.why: Obey them in everything except sin.

checks.q: Who did the Prophet ﷺ name three times as most deserving of good company?
checks.why: Mother three times, then father.
checks.src: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Good Manners (5971)

checks.q: Your parents are poor and you can support them. Spending on them is…
checks.why: Supporting needy parents is a duty on a child who can.

checks.q: How do you honour parents after they die?
checks.a: Du'a, charity and keeping their ties
w: A yearly gathering in their name
checks.why: Narrated by Abu Dawud.
checks.src: Sunan Abi Dawud, Book of Good Manners

lessons.title: The rights of children
lessons.about: Raising children on the deen, and who looks after them.

cards.x: 'Protect yourselves and your families from a Fire.' Each of you is a shepherd and will be asked about his flock: children are a trust you will be questioned about.

cards.ar: يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ قُوٓاْ أَنفُسَكُمْ وَأَهْلِيكُمْ نَارٗا وَقُودُهَا النَّاسُ وَالْحِجَارَةُ عَلَيْهَا مَلَـٰٓئِكَةٌ غِلَاظٞ شِدَادٞ لَّا يَعْصُونَ اللَّهَ مَآ أَمَرَهُمْ وَيَفْعَلُونَ مَا يُؤْمَرُونَ ﴿٦﴾
cards.x: O you who believe, protect yourselves and your families from a Fire whose fuel is people and stones.
Say the adhan in the baby's right ear, give a good name, shave the head and give charity, and the 'aqiqah on the seventh day is recommended in the later Hanafi books.
The father must provide for his children: a son until he can earn, a daughter until she marries.
Teach them belief, purity and the Qur'an. Tell them to pray at seven, and be firmer at ten, and separate their beds.
cards.src: Sunan Abi Dawud, Book of Prayer

cards.x: 'Fear Allah and be fair between your children.' Do not favour one child over another in gifts.

The mother has the first right to raise young children, then her mother, then the father's mother. A boy stays with her until he can eat, dress and clean himself (about seven); a girl until she reaches puberty. The father still pays their maintenance.

checks.q: Who must pay for the children's needs?
checks.why: Maintenance of children is on the father.

checks.q: At what age are children taught to pray?
checks.why: Teach at seven; be firmer at ten.
checks.src: Sunan Abi Dawud, Book of Prayer

checks.q: After divorce, who has the first right to raise a young child?
checks.why: The mother first, then her mother.

checks.q: Giving one child a big gift and not the others is…
w: Allowed if the others do not know
checks.why: 'Be fair between your children.'

lessons.title: Relatives and neighbours
lessons.about: Keeping ties of kinship and honouring the neighbour.

cards.x: Keeping ties with relatives (silat al-rahim) is wajib, and cutting them is a major sin: 'the one who cuts ties will not enter Paradise.' Visit them, help them, and keep in touch, even if they do not.
cards.src: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Good Manners

cards.ar: وَاعْبُدُواْ اللَّهَ وَلَا تُشْرِكُواْ بِهِ شَيْـٔٗا وَبِالْوَٰلِدَيْنِ إِحْسَٰنٗا وَبِذِي الْقُرْبَىٰ وَالْيَتَٰمَىٰ وَالْمَسَٰكِينِ وَالْجَارِ ذِي الْقُرْبَىٰ وَالْجَارِ الْجُنُبِ وَالصَّاحِبِ بِالْجَنبِ وَابْنِ السَّبِيلِ وَمَا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَٰنُكُمْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يُحِبُّ مَن كَانَ مُخْتَالٗا فَخُورًا ﴿٣٦﴾
cards.x: Worship Allah and associate nothing with Him, and be good to parents, relatives, orphans, the needy, the near neighbour, the distant neighbour, the companion at your side and the traveller.
The Prophet ﷺ said: whoever would like his provision increased and his life lengthened, let him keep ties with his relatives.
cards.src: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Good Manners

cards.x: Jibril عليه السلام kept advising the Prophet ﷺ about the neighbour until he ﷺ thought he would make him an heir. 'He is not a believer whose neighbour is not safe from his harm.'
cards.src: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Good Manners

cards.x: Greet them, share food, visit them when ill, help when asked, avoid noise and nuisance, and be patient with their faults, whether or not they are Muslim.

checks.q: Cutting ties with relatives is…
checks.why: Keeping ties is wajib.
checks.src: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Good Manners

checks.q: The Prophet ﷺ swore three times that someone is not a believer. Who?
checks.a: One whose neighbour is not safe from his harm
w: One who does not visit his neighbours
One who does not greet his neighbours
One whose neighbour is not Muslim
checks.why: Narrated by al-Bukhari.
checks.src: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Good Manners

checks.q: Do neighbours' rights apply to non-Muslim neighbours?
checks.why: Every neighbour has a right.

title: Dealing with Doubts
sub: What to do with doubts, from the Prophet ﷺ and Imam al-Ghazali

lessons.title: A doubt is not disbelief
lessons.about: What the Prophet ﷺ said to Companions troubled by thoughts.

cards.x: Some Companions told the Prophet ﷺ they found thoughts in themselves too terrible to speak. He ﷺ asked, 'Do you really find that?' They said yes. He ﷺ said: 'That is clear faith.'
cards.src: Hadith, Sahih Muslim, Book of Faith

cards.x: The Prophet ﷺ said Shaytan comes and asks: who created this, who created that, until he asks who created your Lord. When that happens, seek refuge in Allah and stop.
Being troubled by such a thought shows your faith rejects it. You are not blamed for a passing thought.
cards.src: Hadith, Sahih Muslim, Book of Faith

checks.q: Companions told the Prophet ﷺ of thoughts too terrible to speak of. What did he ﷺ call their hating these whispers?
checks.why: He said, 'That is clear faith', about the Companions who were troubled by them.

checks.q: When the thought 'who created Allah?' comes, you should…
checks.a: Seek refuge in Allah and stop
w: Debate it with others until it is settled
checks.why: The hadith's instruction is to seek refuge in Allah and stop.

checks.q: Is a person sinful for a passing doubt they dislike?
w: Yes, if it lasts a day
Yes, unless he is a scholar
checks.why: Disliking it shows faith; a passing thought is not held against you.

lessons.title: Al-Ghazali's own doubts
lessons.about: A great Imam's honest account of his crisis.

cards.x: Imam al-Ghazali رحمه الله wrote that doubt overcame him so strongly that for nearly two months he could not trust even the basic truths of the mind.
He was cured, he says, not by arranging proofs, but by a light that Allah cast into his breast. That light is the key to most knowledge.
Al-Ghazali warns that whoever thinks unveiling depends only on written proofs has narrowed the vast mercy of Allah.

checks.q: In al-Munqidh min al-Dalal, how long did al-Ghazali's worst doubt last?
checks.why: He says it lasted close to two months.

checks.q: What cured al-Ghazali, in his words?
checks.a: A light Allah cast into his breast
w: A debate he won against a philosopher
A book of philosophy he read
checks.why: Not arranged proofs but a light Allah cast into his breast.

checks.q: What does al-Ghazali say about Allah's mercy?
checks.a: It is wider than written proofs alone
w: It is kept for the scholars
checks.why: Thinking unveiling depends only on proofs narrows Allah's vast mercy.

lessons.title: Know the truth, then its people
lessons.about: Judging ideas by truth, not by who says them.

cards.x: Al-Ghazali quotes 'Ali ibn Abi Talib رضي الله عنه: 'Do not know the truth by men. Know the truth, and you will know its people.'
cards.src: al-Munqidh min al-Dalal, on the sciences of the philosophers

cards.x: He says it is the habit of weak minds to know truth by people, instead of knowing people by the truth.
cards.src: al-Munqidh min al-Dalal, on the sciences of the philosophers

cards.x: Al-Ghazali examined the theologians, the philosophers, the Batinis and the Sufis, and found what he sought in the way of the Sufis: knowledge joined with action.
cards.src: al-Munqidh min al-Dalal, the ways of the Sufis

checks.q: Who said 'Know the truth and you will know its people'?
checks.a: 'Ali ibn Abi Talib رضي الله عنه
checks.why: Al-Ghazali quotes it from 'Ali رضي الله عنه.

checks.q: Al-Ghazali calls knowing truth by people…
checks.why: He says the intelligent person knows people by the truth, not the other way round.

checks.q: Where did al-Ghazali find what he was seeking?
checks.why: He found it in the way of the Sufis, which joins knowledge and action.

lessons.title: How we know the Prophet ﷺ is true
lessons.about: Al-Ghazali's way to certainty about prophethood.

cards.x: Al-Ghazali says: if you know some medicine, you can recognise a real doctor by his words and his work. In the same way you can come to know the Prophet ﷺ by his ﷺ words and states.
cards.src: al-Munqidh min al-Dalal, the reality of prophethood

cards.x: Then strengthen it by experience: act on what he ﷺ taught about worship, and see how it purifies the heart.
cards.src: al-Munqidh min al-Dalal, the reality of prophethood

cards.x: Al-Ghazali cites: 'Whoever acts on what he knows, Allah gives him knowledge of what he did not know.' You will find it true.
cards.src: al-Munqidh min al-Dalal, the reality of prophethood

checks.q: Al-Ghazali compares knowing the Prophet ﷺ to knowing…
checks.a: A real doctor by his words and work
w: A king by his crown and palace
A rich man by his house and clothes
A stranger by his name and family
checks.why: As you can recognise a real doctor or faqih, you can recognise the Prophet ﷺ.

checks.q: How does al-Ghazali say certainty is strengthened?
checks.a: By acting on his teachings and seeing their effect on the heart
w: By reading the books of the philosophers closely
By waiting to see a miracle with his own eyes
By arguing with those who doubt until he wins
checks.why: Experience of his teachings purifying the heart strengthens certainty.

checks.q: Whoever acts on what he knows…
checks.a: Allah gives him knowledge of what he did not know
w: Has no more need of a teacher
Should stop learning and only act
checks.why: Al-Ghazali cites this saying as something you will find true by experience.

lessons.title: Leave what makes you doubt
lessons.about: Simple Prophetic advice for daily doubts.

cards.x: The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Leave what makes you doubt for what does not make you doubt.'
Allah says: 'Ask the people of remembrance if you do not know.' (al-Nahl 43) Doubts are answered by learning, not by hiding them.
Al-Ghazali describes leaving his position in Baghdad and turning to seclusion, disciplining the self and the remembrance of Allah.
cards.src: al-Munqidh min al-Dalal, the ways of the Sufis

checks.q: The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Leave what makes you doubt for…'
checks.a: What does not make you doubt
checks.why: The hadith: leave what makes you doubt for what does not.

checks.q: If you have a question about the religion, you should…
w: Ask whoever is most active online
Work it out from a translation of the Qur'an
Follow what most people around you do
checks.why: 'Ask the people of remembrance if you do not know.' (al-Nahl 43)

checks.q: What did al-Ghazali turn to besides study?
checks.why: In al-Munqidh he describes leaving Baghdad for seclusion, discipline and dhikr.

lessons.title: Questions people ask today
lessons.about: Short, sound answers to the doubts you are most likely to meet.

cards.x: This world is a test, not the final home. Allah created death and life to test which of you is best in deeds. Every wrong will be settled on the Day of Judgement, and the patient will be given their reward without measure.

cards.ar: الَّذِي خَلَقَ الْمَوْتَ وَالْحَيَوٰةَ لِيَبْلُوَكُمْ أَيُّكُمْ أَحْسَنُ عَمَلٗا وَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الْغَفُورُ ﴿٢﴾
cards.x: He who created death and life to test you, which of you is best in deeds. He is the Mighty, the Forgiving.

The Qur'an calls us again and again to study creation, and true knowledge never contradicts revelation. Where a theory clashes with what the Qur'an states clearly, such as Adam عليه السلام being created directly by Allah as the first human, the believer holds to revelation, because theories change and revelation does not.
cards.src: al-Munqidh min al-Dalal, on the sciences of the philosophers

cards.x: The hadith reached us through chains of named narrators, each one examined for honesty and precision. Scholars built a whole science to sort the sound from the weak, and no other record of history has been checked like it.
cards.src: Nuzhat al-Nazar, the kinds of hadith

cards.x: Islam gave women the right to own and earn, to inherit, and to consent to marriage. Paradise is at the feet of mothers, and Allah says: 'I will not let the deed of any of you be lost, male or female.'
Do not hide it and do not panic. Write it down, ask a qualified teacher, keep praying and making du'a. Al-Ghazali was cured not by arguing alone but by a light Allah placed in his heart.

checks.q: Why does Allah allow hardship in this world?
checks.a: It is a test, and every wrong will be settled
w: To show that this world is all there is
Because hardship comes from the stars
Only ever as punishment for sins
checks.why: 'He created death and life to test which of you is best in deeds.'

checks.q: A theory contradicts something the Qur'an states clearly. The believer…
checks.a: Holds to revelation, since theories change
w: Changes the meaning of the verse to fit
Follows the theory, since it is newer
checks.why: True knowledge and revelation do not contradict.
checks.src: al-Munqidh min al-Dalal, on the sciences of the philosophers

checks.q: How were the hadith checked?
checks.a: By examining their chains of narrators
w: By how famous the narrator was
By whether the words sounded wise
checks.why: The science of hadith sorts the sound from the weak.
checks.src: Nuzhat al-Nazar, the kinds of hadith

checks.q: You meet a doubt you cannot answer. What is best?
checks.a: Keep practising and ask a qualified teacher
w: Keep practising and look for answers online
Pause practising until you have an answer
Keep practising and debate those who raised it
checks.why: 'Ask the people of knowledge if you do not know.' (al-Nahl 43)

title: Seerah of the Prophet ﷺ
sub: His life ﷺ from birth to his passing
book: al-Fusul fi Sirat al-Rasul by Ibn Kathir

lessons.title: His lineage and birth ﷺ
lessons.about: The Prophet's ﷺ family and early years.

cards.x: Muhammad ﷺ, son of 'Abdullah, son of 'Abd al-Muttalib, son of Hashim, of Quraysh, from the descendants of Isma'il عليه السلام.
cards.src: al-Fusul fi Sirat al-Rasul, his lineage

cards.x: Trace his ﷺ line ﷺ: twenty-one generations to 'Adnan that all the scholars agree on, then, as the historians give it, through Isma'il and Ibrahim عليهما السلام back to Adam عليه السلام.
cards.src: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of the Merits of the Ansar

cards.x: He ﷺ was born on a Monday in Rabi' al-Awwal, in the Year of the Elephant, according to the sound view.
cards.src: al-Fusul fi Sirat al-Rasul, his birth and nursing

cards.x: His ﷺ father died before he ﷺ was born. His ﷺ mother Aminah died when he ﷺ was six, his ﷺ grandfather 'Abd al-Muttalib when he ﷺ was eight; then his ﷺ uncle Abu Talib took care of him ﷺ.
cards.src: al-Fusul fi Sirat al-Rasul, his birth and nursing

checks.q: On which day was the Prophet ﷺ born?
checks.why: Ibn Kathir: he was born on a Monday in Rabi' al-Awwal.

checks.q: In which year was he ﷺ born?
checks.why: The sound view is that he was born in the Year of the Elephant.

checks.q: Who raised him ﷺ after his ﷺ grandfather 'Abd al-Muttalib died?
w: His ﷺ uncle al-'Abbas رضي الله عنه
His ﷺ uncle Hamzah رضي الله عنه
checks.why: After 'Abd al-Muttalib, Abu Talib took care of him.

lessons.title: Childhood and youth ﷺ
lessons.about: With Halimah, Abu Talib, and his marriage to Khadijah رضي الله عنها.

cards.x: He ﷺ was nursed by Halimah al-Sa'diyyah among Banu Sa'd and stayed with her about four years. There his ﷺ chest was opened.
cards.src: al-Fusul fi Sirat al-Rasul, his birth, nursing and upbringing

cards.x: His ﷺ mother took him ﷺ to visit relatives in Madinah and died at al-Abwa' on the way back, when he ﷺ was six. Years later, passing al-Abwa' in the Year of the Opening, he ﷺ visited her grave and wept.
cards.src: al-Fusul fi Sirat al-Rasul, his birth, nursing and upbringing

cards.x: At twelve his ﷺ uncle Abu Talib took him ﷺ on a trade journey to Syria. Later he ﷺ travelled there again trading for Khadijah رضي الله عنها.
cards.src: al-Fusul fi Sirat al-Rasul, his birth, nursing and upbringing

cards.x: Khadijah رضي الله عنها saw his ﷺ honesty and character and wished to marry him ﷺ. He ﷺ married her when he ﷺ was twenty-five.
cards.src: al-Fusul fi Sirat al-Rasul, his birth, nursing and upbringing

checks.q: Who nursed the Prophet ﷺ in the desert among Banu Sa'd?
w: Khadijah bint Khuwaylid رضي الله عنها
Fatimah bint Asad رضي الله عنها
checks.why: He was nursed among Banu Sa'd by Halimah.

checks.q: Where did his ﷺ mother, Aminah, pass away?
checks.why: She died at al-Abwa' returning from Madinah.

checks.q: How old was he ﷺ when he married Khadijah رضي الله عنها?
checks.why: Ibn Kathir: he married her at twenty-five.

lessons.title: The first revelation
lessons.about: The Cave of Hira' and the first words of the Qur'an.

cards.x: He ﷺ was forty when revelation began. The first to believe was Khadijah رضي الله عنها; among free men Abu Bakr رضي الله عنه; among children 'Ali رضي الله عنه; and among freed slaves Zayd ibn Harithah رضي الله عنهم.

cards.ar: اقْرَأْ بِاسْمِ رَبِّكَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ ﴿١﴾ خَلَقَ الْإِنسَٰنَ مِنْ عَلَقٍ ﴿٢﴾ اقْرَأْ وَرَبُّكَ الْأَكْرَمُ ﴿٣﴾ الَّذِي عَلَّمَ بِالْقَلَمِ ﴿٤﴾ عَلَّمَ الْإِنسَٰنَ مَا لَمْ يَعْلَمْ ﴿٥﴾
cards.x: Read in the name of your Lord who created: created man from a clinging clot. Read, and your Lord is the Most Generous, who taught by the pen, taught man what he did not know.
Before prophethood, he ﷺ loved seclusion and would worship in the Cave of Hira' for nights at a time.
cards.src: Hadith, Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Revelation (3)

cards.x: The angel came and said 'Read!' He ﷺ said, 'I am not one who reads.' Then the angel recited: 'Read in the name of your Lord who created…' (al-'Alaq 1–5)
cards.src: Hadith, Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Revelation (3)

cards.x: He ﷺ returned trembling. Khadijah رضي الله عنها comforted him ﷺ: 'Allah will never disgrace you. You keep ties of kinship, carry the burdens of the weak and help the needy.'
cards.src: Hadith, Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Revelation (3)

checks.q: Where did the first revelation come to him ﷺ?
checks.why: He ﷺ was worshipping in the Cave of Hira' when the angel came.

checks.q: What were the first words revealed?
checks.a: 'Read in the name of your Lord who created'
w: 'In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful'
'O you wrapped in garments, arise and warn'
checks.why: The opening verses of Surah al-'Alaq were the first revealed.

checks.q: Who comforted him ﷺ when he ﷺ came home from the Cave of Hira' after the first revelation?
checks.why: Khadijah رضي الله عنها reassured him that Allah would never disgrace him.

checks.q: How old was the Prophet ﷺ when revelation began?
checks.why: He ﷺ received revelation at forty and lived twenty-three years after it.

lessons.title: Hardship in Makkah
lessons.about: Persecution, Abyssinia and the Year of Sorrow.

cards.x: Quraysh tortured the weak Muslims to make them leave Islam. They held firm.
cards.src: al-Fusul fi Sirat al-Rasul, the trial of the tortured

cards.x: The Prophet ﷺ allowed a group of Muslims to migrate to Abyssinia, to the just king al-Najashi, where they were safe.
cards.src: al-Fusul fi Sirat al-Rasul, the migration to Abyssinia

cards.x: Quraysh boycotted Banu Hashim. Later the Prophet ﷺ went to Ta'if to call its people, and they drove him ﷺ out. He ﷺ returned to Makkah under protection.
cards.src: al-Fusul fi Sirat al-Rasul, the boycott; going out to Ta'if

checks.q: To which land did the first Muslims migrate?
checks.why: They migrated to Abyssinia, to the just king al-Najashi.

checks.q: For three years Quraysh boycotted one clan, refusing to trade or marry with them. Which clan?
checks.why: Ibn Kathir has a chapter on Quraysh's boycott of Banu Hashim and Banu al-Muttalib.

checks.q: Who was the king of Abyssinia who sheltered the Muslims who migrated there?
checks.why: The Najashi, a just Christian king, protected them; he later accepted Islam, and the Prophet ﷺ prayed the funeral prayer for him in absence.

lessons.title: The Year of Sorrow and Ta'if
lessons.about: Losing Khadijah رضي الله عنها and Abu Talib, and the journey to Ta'if.

cards.x: In the tenth year of prophethood, Khadijah رضي الله عنها and his ﷺ uncle Abu Talib died within a short time of each other. Quraysh's harm grew, and that year was called the Year of Sorrow.
cards.src: al-Fusul fi Sirat al-Rasul, the death of Abu Talib and Khadijah رضي الله عنها

cards.x: He ﷺ went to Ta'if to call its people to Islam. They rejected him ﷺ and set their children and slaves on him ﷺ, throwing stones until his ﷺ feet bled.
cards.src: al-Fusul fi Sirat al-Rasul, the journey to Ta'if

cards.x: The angel of the mountains offered to crush the town between two mountains. He ﷺ said: rather, I hope Allah will bring from their descendants people who worship Allah alone.
cards.src: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of the Beginning of Creation

checks.q: Why is the tenth year of prophethood called the Year of Sorrow?
checks.a: Khadijah رضي الله عنها and Abu Talib both died that year
w: The Muslims were driven from Makkah
The Battle of Uhud was lost
checks.why: He ﷺ lost his wife and his protector within a short time.

checks.q: How did the people of Ta'if respond when he ﷺ invited them to Islam?
checks.a: They rejected and stoned him ﷺ
w: They sheltered him ﷺ for a year
checks.why: Yet he ﷺ did not curse them.

checks.q: After Ta'if, the angel of the mountains offered to crush its people. What did he ﷺ say?
checks.a: He ﷺ hoped their descendants would worship Allah
checks.why: A lesson in mercy and patience in calling to Allah.

lessons.title: The pledges of 'Aqabah
lessons.about: How Madinah opened its doors to Islam.

cards.x: At Hajj, twelve men from Yathrib (Madinah) met him ﷺ at 'Aqabah and pledged to worship Allah alone, not steal, not commit zina and not kill their children. He ﷺ sent Mus'ab ibn 'Umayr رضي الله عنه with them to teach.
cards.src: al-Fusul fi Sirat al-Rasul, the first 'Aqabah

cards.x: The next year, seventy-three men and two women pledged to protect him ﷺ as they protected their own families. This opened the way to the Hijrah.
cards.src: al-Fusul fi Sirat al-Rasul, the second 'Aqabah

checks.q: Who did the Prophet ﷺ send to Madinah to teach after the first pledge?
checks.why: He was the first teacher sent out in Islam.

checks.q: What did the people of Madinah pledge at the second 'Aqabah?
checks.a: To protect him ﷺ as they protected their own families
w: To pay him a yearly tax
checks.why: This pledge opened the way to the Hijrah.

checks.q: Where did the pledges of 'Aqabah take place?
checks.a: At 'Aqabah near Mina, during the Hajj season
checks.why: The Prophet ﷺ met the tribes when they came for Hajj.

lessons.title: The Night Journey and the Hijrah
lessons.about: From al-Isra' to the arrival in Madinah.

cards.x: Allah took His Messenger ﷺ by night from al-Masjid al-Haram to al-Masjid al-Aqsa, and up through the heavens. The five daily prayers were made fard on that night.
cards.src: al-Fusul fi Sirat al-Rasul, the Isra' and Mi'raj

cards.ar: سُبْحَٰنَ الَّذِيٓ أَسْرَىٰ بِعَبْدِهِ لَيْلٗا مِّنَ الْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرَامِ إِلَى الْمَسْجِدِ الْأَقْصَا الَّذِي بَٰرَكْنَا حَوْلَهُ لِنُرِيَهُ مِنْ ءَايَٰتِنَآ إِنَّهُ هُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْبَصِيرُ ﴿١﴾
cards.x: Glory be to the One who took His servant by night from the Sacred Masjid to the Furthest Masjid, whose surroundings We have blessed.
Believers from Madinah met him ﷺ at 'Aqabah and pledged to follow and protect him ﷺ. Islam spread in Madinah.
cards.src: al-Fusul fi Sirat al-Rasul, the first and second pledges of 'Aqabah

cards.x: He ﷺ migrated with Abu Bakr رضي الله عنه, hiding in the Cave of Thawr, then reached Quba' and Madinah, built the masjid and joined the Muhajirun and Ansar in brotherhood.
cards.src: al-Fusul fi Sirat al-Rasul, the Hijrah; brotherhood

checks.q: What was made fard on the night of the Mi'raj?
checks.why: The five prayers were made obligatory on that night.

checks.q: Who accompanied the Prophet ﷺ on the Hijrah from Makkah to Madinah?
checks.why: Abu Bakr رضي الله عنه was his ﷺ companion in the Hijrah and the cave.

checks.q: On the Hijrah, in which cave did the Prophet ﷺ and Abu Bakr رضي الله عنه hide for three nights?
checks.why: They hid in the Cave of Thawr.

lessons.title: Building Madinah
lessons.about: The masjid, the brotherhood, and a new community.

cards.x: On arriving in Madinah he ﷺ built his ﷺ masjid, working with his ﷺ own hands, carrying bricks with the Companions. It was the centre of worship, learning and community.
cards.src: al-Fusul fi Sirat al-Rasul, building the masjid

cards.x: He ﷺ joined each Muhajir (emigrant from Makkah) with an Ansari (helper from Madinah) as brothers. The Ansar shared their homes and wealth with them.
cards.src: al-Fusul fi Sirat al-Rasul, the brotherhood

cards.x: The adhan was given its words after 'Abdullah ibn Zayd رضي الله عنه saw it in a dream, and Bilal رضي الله عنه, with his beautiful voice, became the first mu'adhdhin.
cards.src: Sunan Abi Dawud, Book of Prayer

checks.q: What was the first thing the Prophet ﷺ built in Madinah?
checks.why: He ﷺ carried bricks with the Companions himself.

checks.q: Who were the Ansar?
checks.a: The Muslims of Madinah who helped the emigrants
checks.why: Ansar means helpers; the Muhajirun were the emigrants.

checks.q: Who was the first mu'adhdhin?
checks.why: 'Abdullah ibn Zayd رضي الله عنه saw the words in a dream; Bilal رضي الله عنه called it.

lessons.title: Badr, Uhud and the Trench
lessons.about: The great battles of the Madinan years.

cards.x: At Badr, in Ramadan of the second year, Allah gave victory to a small number of believers over a much larger army of Quraysh.
cards.src: al-Fusul fi Sirat al-Rasul, the great Battle of Badr

cards.ar: وَلَقَدْ نَصَرَكُمُ اللَّهُ بِبَدْرٖ وَأَنتُمْ أَذِلَّةٞ فَاتَّقُواْ اللَّهَ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَشْكُرُونَ ﴿١٢٣﴾
cards.x: Allah had already helped you at Badr when you were weak. So be mindful of Allah, so that you may be grateful.
At Uhud the archers left their post against the Prophet's ﷺ order, and the Muslims suffered. Hamzah رضي الله عنه was martyred.
cards.src: al-Fusul fi Sirat al-Rasul, the Battle of Uhud

cards.x: When the confederate tribes came to Madinah, the Muslims dug a trench. After a long siege, Allah sent a wind and the confederates left.
cards.src: al-Fusul fi Sirat al-Rasul, the Battle of the Trench

checks.q: In which month was the Battle of Badr fought, in 2 AH?
checks.why: Badr took place in Ramadan of the second year after the Hijrah.

checks.q: What turned the Battle of Uhud against the Muslims?
w: The Muslims ran out of water
checks.why: The archers left their position against his ﷺ order.

checks.q: In 5 AH the confederate tribes marched on Madinah. How did the Muslims defend it?
checks.why: Hence its name: the Battle of the Trench (al-Khandaq).

lessons.title: Hudaybiyah and Khaybar
lessons.about: A treaty that looked like a loss, and was a clear victory.

cards.x: In 6 AH the Prophet ﷺ set out for 'umrah with about 1,400 Companions. Quraysh blocked him ﷺ at al-Hudaybiyah, and a ten-year peace treaty was made. Its terms seemed hard on the Muslims.

cards.ar: إِنَّا فَتَحْنَا لَكَ فَتْحٗا مُّبِينٗا ﴿١﴾
cards.x: Truly, We have given you a clear victory.

cards.ar: لَّقَدْ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ إِذْ يُبَايِعُونَكَ تَحْتَ الشَّجَرَةِ فَعَلِمَ مَا فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ فَأَنزَلَ السَّكِينَةَ عَلَيْهِمْ وَأَثَٰبَهُمْ فَتْحٗا قَرِيبٗا ﴿١٨﴾
cards.x: Allah was pleased with the believers when they pledged to you under the tree.
When it was rumoured that 'Uthman رضي الله عنه had been killed, the Companions pledged to stand firm. Allah said He was pleased with them: the Pledge of Ridwan.
Allah called the treaty 'a clear victory'. In the peace, Islam spread faster than ever, and Khaybar was taken soon after.

checks.q: What did Allah call the Treaty of Hudaybiyah?
checks.why: 'Indeed, We have given you a clear victory.' (al-Fath 1)

checks.q: Why did the Companions make the Pledge of Ridwan?
checks.a: It was rumoured that 'Uthman رضي الله عنه had been killed
w: To begin the conquest of Makkah
checks.why: Allah said He was pleased with those who pledged under the tree.

checks.q: Why did the Prophet ﷺ set out for Makkah in 6 AH, the year of Hudaybiyah?
checks.why: He went in ihram with the sacrificial animals, intending peace.

lessons.title: Victory and farewell
lessons.about: Hudaybiyah, the opening of Makkah, and his passing ﷺ.

cards.x: In the sixth year he ﷺ set out for 'umrah and made a treaty with Quraysh at al-Hudaybiyah. Allah called it a clear victory.
In Ramadan of the eighth year he ﷺ entered Makkah with humility, cleared the Ka'bah of idols and forgave the people who had fought him ﷺ.
cards.src: al-Fusul fi Sirat al-Rasul, the opening of Makkah

cards.x: He ﷺ performed the Farewell Hajj in the tenth year, and passed away in Madinah in Rabi' al-Awwal of the eleventh year.
cards.src: al-Fusul fi Sirat al-Rasul, the Farewell Hajj; his passing

checks.q: When was Makkah opened to the Muslims?
checks.a: Ramadan, in the 8th year after the Hijrah
w: Shawwal, in the 8th year after the Hijrah
Ramadan, in the 6th year after the Hijrah
Muharram, in the 10th year after the Hijrah
checks.why: The opening of Makkah was in Ramadan of the eighth year.

checks.q: What did he ﷺ do with the people of Makkah when he ﷺ conquered it in 8 AH?
checks.why: He forgave those who had fought him.

checks.q: In which year was the Farewell Hajj?
checks.why: The Farewell Hajj was in the tenth year; he passed away in the eleventh.

lessons.title: The Farewell Hajj
lessons.about: His only Hajj ﷺ, and his last sermon.

cards.x: In 10 AH the Prophet ﷺ performed Hajj with over a hundred thousand Companions. It was his ﷺ only Hajj, and he ﷺ taught them its rites, saying: take your rites from me.

cards.ar: حُرِّمَتْ عَلَيْكُمُ الْمَيْتَةُ وَالدَّمُ وَلَحْمُ الْخِنزِيرِ وَمَآ أُهِلَّ لِغَيْرِ اللَّهِ بِهِ وَالْمُنْخَنِقَةُ وَالْمَوْقُوذَةُ وَالْمُتَرَدِّيَةُ وَالنَّطِيحَةُ وَمَآ أَكَلَ السَّبُعُ إِلَّا مَا ذَكَّيْتُمْ وَمَا ذُبِحَ عَلَى النُّصُبِ وَأَن تَسْتَقْسِمُواْ بِالْأَزْلَٰمِ ذَٰلِكُمْ فِسْقٌ الْيَوْمَ يَئِسَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ مِن دِينِكُمْ فَلَا تَخْشَوْهُمْ وَاخْشَوْنِ الْيَوْمَ أَكْمَلْتُ لَكُمْ دِينَكُمْ وَأَتْمَمْتُ عَلَيْكُمْ نِعْمَتِي وَرَضِيتُ لَكُمُ الْإِسْلَٰمَ دِينٗا فَمَنِ اضْطُرَّ فِي مَخْمَصَةٍ غَيْرَ مُتَجَانِفٖ لِّإِثْمٖ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٞ رَّحِيمٞ ﴿٣﴾
cards.x: Today I have perfected your religion for you, completed My favour upon you, and chosen Islam as your religion.
He ﷺ said your blood, wealth and honour are sacred to one another, ended the feuds and riba of the Days of Ignorance, urged kindness to women, and left them the Book of Allah.
At 'Arafah the verse came down: 'Today I have perfected your religion for you, completed My favour upon you, and chosen Islam as your religion.'

checks.q: How many times did the Prophet ﷺ perform Hajj after the Hijrah?
checks.why: Once, in 10 AH, the Farewell Hajj. He ﷺ also performed 'umrah four times.

checks.q: What did he ﷺ declare sacred in the Farewell Sermon?
w: The Ka'bah and the Black Stone
The cities of Makkah and Madinah
checks.why: Sacred as that day, that month and that land.

checks.q: Which verse came down at 'Arafah during the Farewell Hajj?
checks.a: 'Today I have perfected your religion for you'
w: 'Read in the name of your Lord'
checks.why: Al-Ma'idah 3.

lessons.title: His passing ﷺ
lessons.about: The last days, and how the Companions held firm.

cards.x: In Rabi' al-Awwal 11 AH he ﷺ fell ill. He ﷺ asked to be nursed in the room of 'A'ishah رضي الله عنها and told Abu Bakr رضي الله عنه to lead the people in prayer.
cards.src: al-Fusul fi Sirat al-Rasul, his illness

cards.ar: وَمَا مُحَمَّدٌ إِلَّا رَسُولٞ قَدْ خَلَتْ مِن قَبْلِهِ الرُّسُلُ أَفَإِيْن مَّاتَ أَوْ قُتِلَ انقَلَبْتُمْ عَلَىٰٓ أَعْقَٰبِكُمْ وَمَن يَنقَلِبْ عَلَىٰ عَقِبَيْهِ فَلَن يَضُرَّ اللَّهَ شَيْـٔٗا وَسَيَجْزِي اللَّهُ الشَّـٰكِرِينَ ﴿١٤٤﴾
cards.x: Muhammad is only a messenger; messengers have passed away before him. If he dies or is killed, will you turn back on your heels?
His ﷺ last advice included the prayer and kindness to those under your care. He ﷺ passed away on a Monday, aged sixty-three, saying: 'With the highest companion.'
cards.src: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Military Expeditions

cards.x: When some could not believe it, Abu Bakr رضي الله عنه said: whoever worshipped Muhammad, Muhammad has died; whoever worships Allah, Allah is Ever-Living and never dies. Then he recited Al 'Imran 144.
cards.src: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Military Expeditions

checks.q: How old was the Prophet ﷺ when he passed away?
checks.why: He ﷺ received revelation at forty and lived twenty-three years after.

checks.q: Whom did he ﷺ tell to lead the prayer during his ﷺ final illness?
checks.why: The Companions saw this as a sign of Abu Bakr's precedence.

checks.q: What did Abu Bakr رضي الله عنه remind the people when the Prophet ﷺ passed away?
checks.a: Allah is Ever-Living and never dies
w: That the Ansar should choose a leader
checks.why: Whoever worships Allah, Allah is Ever-Living and never dies.

lessons.title: His family ﷺ
lessons.about: His children and his wives, the Mothers of the Believers.

cards.x: All his ﷺ children were from Khadijah رضي الله عنها except Ibrahim, from Mariyah رضي الله عنها. They were al-Qasim (his ﷺ kunyah Abu al-Qasim is from him), Zaynab, Ruqayyah, Umm Kulthum, Fatimah رضي الله عنهن, 'Abdullah and Ibrahim رضي الله عنهم.
cards.src: al-Fusul fi Sirat al-Rasul, his children

cards.x: See his ﷺ parents, all eleven Mothers of the Believers, his ﷺ children and grandchildren together.
cards.src: Ibn Kathir, al-Fusul fi Sirat al-Rasul, his children

cards.x: All of his ﷺ children died before him ﷺ except Fatimah رضي الله عنها, who passed away a few months after him ﷺ.
cards.src: al-Fusul fi Sirat al-Rasul, his children

cards.x: His ﷺ first wife was Khadijah رضي الله عنها, the first to believe in him ﷺ. He ﷺ married no one else in her lifetime.
cards.src: al-Fusul fi Sirat al-Rasul, his wives

cards.x: Of his ﷺ wives, no woman of this Ummah is known to have reached her level of knowledge.
cards.src: al-Fusul fi Sirat al-Rasul, his wives

checks.q: Which of his ﷺ children outlived him ﷺ?
checks.why: All died before him except Fatimah رضي الله عنها, who died a few months after.

checks.q: Who was his ﷺ first wife?
checks.why: Khadijah رضي الله عنها was first, and he married no one else in her lifetime.

checks.q: Why was he ﷺ called Abu al-Qasim?
checks.why: Al-Qasim was his eldest, and the kunyah is from him.

lessons.title: His character ﷺ
lessons.about: How he looked and how he treated people.

cards.x: Anas رضي الله عنه described him ﷺ: neither very tall nor short, neither very white nor dark, his ﷺ hair neither tightly curled nor straight.

cards.ar: وَإِنَّكَ لَعَلَىٰ خُلُقٍ عَظِيمٖ ﴿٤﴾
cards.x: And truly you are of a tremendous character.

cards.ar: لَّقَدْ كَانَ لَكُمْ فِي رَسُولِ اللَّهِ أُسْوَةٌ حَسَنَةٞ لِّمَن كَانَ يَرْجُواْ اللَّهَ وَالْيَوْمَ الْأٓخِرَ وَذَكَرَ اللَّهَ كَثِيرٗا ﴿٢١﴾
cards.x: In the Messenger of Allah you have a beautiful example.
Anas رضي الله عنه served him ﷺ for ten years, and he ﷺ never once said 'uff' to him, nor asked 'why did you do that?'
'A'ishah رضي الله عنها was asked about his ﷺ character. She said: 'His ﷺ character was the Qur'an.'

checks.q: How long did Anas ibn Malik رضي الله عنه serve the Prophet ﷺ?
checks.why: Anas رضي الله عنه served him for ten years and never heard 'uff' from him.

checks.q: How did 'A'ishah رضي الله عنها describe his ﷺ character?
checks.why: Her answer: his character was the Qur'an.

checks.q: Which describes his height ﷺ?
w: Tall, like the tallest of them
checks.why: Anas رضي الله عنه described him as neither very tall nor short.

title: Qur'an: Revelation and Preservation
sub: How the Qur'an came down, was gathered and is preserved

lessons.title: The virtue of the Qur'an
lessons.about: Why learning and reciting it matters, from al-Tibyan.

cards.x: The Prophet ﷺ said: 'The best of you is the one who learns the Qur'an and teaches it.'
cards.src: al-Tibyan, chapter one; Hadith, Sahih al-Bukhari

cards.x: 'The one skilled in the Qur'an is with the noble, righteous scribes (angels), and the one who stumbles over it and finds it hard has two rewards.'
cards.src: al-Tibyan, chapter one; Hadith, al-Bukhari and Muslim

cards.x: 'Whoever reads a letter of the Book of Allah has a good deed, and a good deed is multiplied ten times. I do not say Alif Lam Mim is a letter: Alif is a letter, Lam is a letter and Mim is a letter.'

checks.q: Who is 'the best of you', in the hadith?
checks.a: The one who learns the Qur'an and teaches it
w: The one who memorises it but does not teach
The one who fasts and prays the most
The one who gives the most in charity
checks.why: Narrated by al-Bukhari and quoted by al-Nawawi in al-Tibyan.

checks.q: The one who stumbles while reciting…
checks.why: The hadith gives him two rewards for his effort.

checks.q: How much reward is there for reciting one letter of the Qur'an?
checks.a: One good deed, multiplied ten times
w: Ten good deeds for each word
One good deed for each verse
checks.why: Each letter is a good deed, multiplied by ten.

lessons.title: How revelation came
lessons.about: What the Prophet ﷺ said about receiving the wahy.

cards.x: Asked how revelation came, he ﷺ said: sometimes it comes like the ringing of a bell, and that is the hardest on me; then it leaves me and I have taken in what was said.
cards.src: Hadith, Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Revelation (2)

cards.x: 'And sometimes the angel comes to me in the form of a man, speaks to me, and I take in what he says.'
cards.src: Hadith, Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Revelation (2)

cards.x: 'A'ishah رضي الله عنها said she saw revelation come to him ﷺ on a very cold day, and when it left him ﷺ his ﷺ forehead was dripping with sweat.
cards.src: Hadith, Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Revelation (2)

checks.q: Which way of receiving revelation did he ﷺ say was hardest on him ﷺ?
checks.a: Like the ringing of a bell
checks.why: He said the bell-like way was the hardest on him.

checks.q: When Jibril عليه السلام came to the Prophet ﷺ in a visible form, how did he sometimes appear?
checks.a: In the form of a man
w: As a voice from a tree
checks.why: 'Sometimes the angel comes to me in the form of a man.'

checks.q: What did 'A'ishah رضي الله عنها see when revelation came to him ﷺ on a very cold day?
checks.a: His ﷺ forehead dripping with sweat
checks.why: Even on a cold day his forehead dripped with sweat from the weight of revelation.

lessons.title: Revealed bit by bit
lessons.about: Twenty-three years, and Jibril's yearly review.

cards.x: Allah sent the Qur'an down in parts over the years of prophethood: 'A Qur'an We have divided, so that you may recite it to people slowly.' (al-Isra' 106)

cards.ar: وَقُرْءَانٗا فَرَقْنَٰهُ لِتَقْرَأَهُ عَلَى النَّاسِ عَلَىٰ مُكْثٖ وَنَزَّلْنَٰهُ تَنزِيلٗا ﴿١٠٦﴾
cards.x: A Qur'an which We have divided into parts, so that you may recite it to people slowly, and We sent it down in stages.
Jibril عليه السلام met the Prophet ﷺ every night of Ramadan and studied the Qur'an with him ﷺ.
cards.src: Hadith, Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Revelation (6)

cards.x: Jibril عليه السلام reviewed the Qur'an with him ﷺ once every year, and twice in the year he ﷺ passed away.
cards.src: Hadith, Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of the Virtues of the Qur'an

checks.q: How was the Qur'an sent down?
w: All at once, in a single night
checks.why: 'A Qur'an We have divided, so that you may recite it slowly.' (al-Isra' 106)

checks.q: When did Jibril عليه السلام study the Qur'an with him ﷺ?
checks.why: Ibn 'Abbas رضي الله عنهما: Jibril عليه السلام met him every night of Ramadan and studied the Qur'an with him.

checks.q: How many times did Jibril عليه السلام review the Qur'an with him ﷺ in his ﷺ final year?
checks.why: Once every year, and twice in the year he passed away.

lessons.title: Gathered into one book
lessons.about: Abu Bakr's collection and 'Uthman's copies.

cards.x: After many reciters were martyred at Yamamah, 'Umar رضي الله عنه urged Abu Bakr رضي الله عنه to collect the Qur'an. Abu Bakr رضي الله عنه gave the task to Zayd ibn Thabit رضي الله عنه, a scribe of revelation.
cards.src: Hadith, Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of the Virtues of the Qur'an

cards.x: Zayd رضي الله عنه gathered it from palm stalks, flat stones and the memories of men. The sheets stayed with Abu Bakr, then 'Umar, then Hafsah رضي الله عنهم.
cards.src: Hadith, Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of the Virtues of the Qur'an

cards.x: When Hudhayfah رضي الله عنه saw people differing in recitation, 'Uthman رضي الله عنه had copies made from Hafsah's sheets and sent one to each region.
cards.src: Hadith, Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of the Virtues of the Qur'an

checks.q: Who first ordered the Qur'an to be collected into one book?
checks.why: Abu Bakr رضي الله عنه ordered it, on 'Umar's advice, after Yamamah.

checks.q: Who did Abu Bakr رضي الله عنه task with collecting the Qur'an?
checks.a: Zayd ibn Thabit رضي الله عنه
checks.why: Zayd ibn Thabit رضي الله عنه, a scribe of revelation, was given the task.

checks.q: Why did 'Uthman رضي الله عنه send standard copies of the Qur'an to the regions?
checks.why: Hudhayfah رضي الله عنه warned him of differences, so he sent unified copies from Hafsah's sheets.

lessons.title: Preserved by Allah
lessons.about: Seven modes, memorisers, and Allah's promise.

cards.x: 'Indeed it is We who sent down the Reminder, and indeed We will preserve it.' (al-Hijr 9)

cards.ar: إِنَّا نَحْنُ نَزَّلْنَا الذِّكْرَ وَإِنَّا لَهُ لَحَٰفِظُونَ ﴿٩﴾
cards.x: Truly, it is We who sent down the Reminder, and truly We will preserve it.
'Umar رضي الله عنه heard Hisham ibn Hakim رضي الله عنه recite differently and brought him to the Prophet ﷺ, who approved both and said the Qur'an was revealed in seven modes (ahruf).
cards.src: Hadith, Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of the Virtues of the Qur'an

cards.x: The Qur'an is preserved in hearts as well as written in copies, as Imam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله said. Every generation has had countless people who memorised it.

checks.q: Who preserves the Qur'an?
checks.why: 'It is We who sent down the Reminder, and We will preserve it.'

checks.q: In how many modes (ahruf) was the Qur'an revealed?
checks.why: The Prophet ﷺ said it was revealed in seven ahruf.

checks.q: 'Umar رضي الله عنه and Hisham رضي الله عنه recited a surah differently. What did the Prophet ﷺ do?
checks.why: He approved both and explained the seven modes.

lessons.title: Honouring the Qur'an
lessons.about: Al-Nawawi's manners with the Book of Allah.

cards.x: Recite in a state of purity, with a clean mouth, using the siwak, facing the qiblah and sitting with humility.
cards.src: al-Tibyan fi Adab Hamalat al-Qur'an, manners of the Qur'an

cards.ar: أَوْ زِدْ عَلَيْهِ وَرَتِّلِ الْقُرْءَانَ تَرْتِيلًا ﴿٤﴾
cards.x: And recite the Qur'an in measured recitation (tartil).

cards.ar: لَّا يَمَسُّهُٓ إِلَّا الْمُطَهَّرُونَ ﴿٧٩﴾
cards.x: None touch it except the purified.
Recite with tartil, reflecting on the meaning. Reflection is the whole purpose of recitation.
cards.src: al-Tibyan fi Adab Hamalat al-Qur'an, manners of the Qur'an

cards.x: In the Hanafi school, a person without wudu may not touch the Qur'an except with a separate cover. Someone in janabah may not recite it either.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, what is forbidden without purity

checks.q: What is the purpose of reciting the Qur'an?
checks.why: Al-Nawawi says reflection is the point of reciting.

checks.q: Without wudu, may you touch the Qur'an in the Hanafi school?
checks.a: No, except with a separate cover
checks.why: Nur al-Idah lists touching the Qur'an among what is forbidden without purity.

checks.q: Which is a manner of reciting the Qur'an?
w: Reciting as fast as you can
checks.why: A clean mouth and siwak are among the manners he gives.

title: Tasawwuf and Tazkiyah
sub: Purifying the heart, the stations of the path, the tariqahs and seeking a guide
book: al-Risalah al-Qushayriyyah, with Ihya' 'Ulum al-Din and Bidayat al-Hidayah

lessons.title: What is tasawwuf?
lessons.about: Ihsan, the third level of the religion, and the purification of the heart.

cards.x: When Jibril عليه السلام asked about the religion, the Prophet ﷺ taught Islam (the outward acts), iman (belief), and ihsan: 'that you worship Allah as though you see Him, and though you do not see Him, He sees you.' Tasawwuf is the science of ihsan.

cards.ar: قَدْ أَفْلَحَ مَن زَكَّىٰهَا ﴿٩﴾ وَقَدْ خَابَ مَن دَسَّىٰهَا ﴿١٠﴾
cards.x: Successful indeed is the one who purifies it, and lost is the one who buries it.

Fiqh governs the limbs, 'aqidah the beliefs, and tasawwuf the heart: purifying it of pride, envy, showing off and love of the world, and adorning it with sincerity, humility, patience, gratitude and love of Allah.

Al-Junayd رحمه الله was asked about tasawwuf and said: that the Truth makes you die to yourself and live by Him. Others said: it is good character, so whoever surpasses you in character surpasses you in tasawwuf.
Al-Junayd said: this knowledge of ours is bound by the Book and the Sunnah. Whoever has not memorised the Qur'an and written hadith is not to be followed in it.
cards.src: al-Risalah al-Qushayriyyah, the masters of the path

checks.q: In the hadith of Jibril عليه السلام, ihsan is…
checks.a: To worship Allah as though you see Him
checks.why: And though you do not see Him, He sees you.

checks.q: Tasawwuf is mainly concerned with…
checks.why: Fiqh for the limbs, 'aqidah for belief, tasawwuf for the heart.

checks.q: Al-Junayd said the knowledge of tasawwuf is bound by…
w: The customs of the Sufi lodges
checks.why: No path is sound outside the Shari'ah.
checks.src: al-Risalah al-Qushayriyyah, the masters of the path

lessons.title: Its roots
lessons.about: Tasawwuf in the Qur'an, the Sunnah and the early generations.

cards.x: Allah sent the Prophet ﷺ to recite His verses, purify the people (tazkiyah), and teach them the Book and wisdom. 'Successful is the one who purifies it.'

cards.ar: هُوَ الَّذِي بَعَثَ فِي الْأُمِّيِّـنَ رَسُولٗا مِّنْهُمْ يَتْلُواْ عَلَيْهِمْ ءَايَٰتِهِ وَيُزَكِّيهِمْ وَيُعَلِّمُهُمُ الْكِتَٰبَ وَالْحِكْمَةَ وَإِن كَانُواْ مِن قَبْلُ لَفِي ضَلَٰلٖ مُّبِينٖ ﴿٢﴾
cards.x: He is the One who sent among the unlettered a Messenger from among them, reciting to them His verses, purifying them, and teaching them the Book and wisdom.

He ﷺ withdrew to Hira' before revelation, stood in prayer until his ﷺ feet swelled, and lived simply though the world was offered to him ﷺ. He ﷺ said: there is a piece of flesh in the body; if it is sound, the whole body is sound, and that is the heart.
The People of the Suffah lived in the Prophet's ﷺ masjid for worship and learning. Abu Bakr رضي الله عنه gave all his wealth; Abu Dharr رضي الله عنه was known for his detachment.

The name 'Sufi' became common in the second century, when the world spread among people and those who devoted themselves to worship were singled out by it, just as the names 'fiqh' and 'tafsir' came later for sciences whose substance was there from the start.

Al-Hasan al-Basri, Rabi'ah al-'Adawiyyah, al-Fudayl ibn 'Iyad, Ma'ruf al-Karkhi, al-Sari al-Saqati and al-Junayd رحمهم الله are among the early people of the path. Al-Qushayri gathered their sayings in his Risalah, and al-Ghazali joined fiqh and tasawwuf in the Ihya'.
cards.src: al-Risalah al-Qushayriyyah, the masters of the path

checks.q: Which three tasks of the Prophet ﷺ does al-Jumu'ah 2 mention?
checks.a: Reciting the verses, purifying people, teaching the Book and wisdom
checks.why: Tazkiyah is one of the Prophet's ﷺ missions.

checks.q: Which piece of flesh did the Prophet ﷺ say makes the body sound?
checks.why: Narrated by al-Bukhari and Muslim.

lessons.title: Sincerity
lessons.about: Why you seek knowledge, and the weight of intention.

cards.x: Imam al-Ghazali رحمه الله begins by asking why you seek knowledge. If it is to compete, show off and win people's attention, you are tearing down your religion. If it is for guidance, the angels spread their wings for you as you walk.

cards.ar: وَمَآ أُمِرُوٓاْ إِلَّا لِيَعْبُدُواْ اللَّهَ مُخْلِصِينَ لَهُ الدِّينَ حُنَفَآءَ وَيُقِيمُواْ الصَّلَوٰةَ وَيُؤْتُواْ الزَّكَوٰةَ وَذَٰلِكَ دِينُ الْقَيِّمَةِ ﴿٥﴾
cards.x: They were only commanded to worship Allah, making the religion sincerely His.
The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Actions are only by intentions, and each person will have only what he intended.'

checks.q: Seeking knowledge to show off…
w: Lessens the reward, but is still worship
Is forgiven if the knowledge is taught
Spoils the knowledge, but not the religion
checks.why: Al-Ghazali says seeking knowledge to compete and show off tears down your religion.

checks.q: According to the hadith, actions are judged by…
checks.why: 'Actions are only by intentions, and each person will have only what he intended.'

checks.q: Which deeds are accepted by Allah?
checks.why: 'Actions are only by intentions.' Sincerity is the soul of every deed.

checks.q: You notice you want praise for a good deed. What should you do?
checks.a: Correct your intention and keep doing it for Allah
w: Stop doing it until your intention is pure
Do it only in secret from now on
Ignore the feeling and carry on as you were
checks.why: Don't leave good deeds for fear of riya'; purify the intention.

lessons.title: Repentance
lessons.about: What tawbah is and its three conditions.

cards.x: Repentance (tawbah) means turning back from what the Shari'ah blames to what it praises.

cards.ar: يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ تُوبُوٓاْ إِلَى اللَّهِ تَوْبَةٗ نَّصُوحًا عَسَىٰ رَبُّكُمْ أَن يُكَفِّرَ عَنكُمْ سَيِّـَٔاتِكُمْ وَيُدْخِلَكُمْ جَنَّـٰتٖ تَجْرِي مِن تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَٰرُ يَوْمَ لَا يُخْزِي اللَّهُ النَّبِيَّ وَالَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ مَعَهُ نُورُهُمْ يَسْعَىٰ بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَبِأَيْمَٰنِهِمْ يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنَآ أَتْمِمْ لَنَا نُورَنَا وَاغْفِرْ لَنَآ إِنَّكَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيْءٖ قَدِيرٞ ﴿٨﴾
cards.x: O you who believe, turn to Allah in sincere repentance.

cards.ar: وَقُل لِّلْمُؤْمِنَٰتِ يَغْضُضْنَ مِنْ أَبْصَٰرِهِنَّ وَيَحْفَظْنَ فُرُوجَهُنَّ وَلَا يُبْدِينَ زِينَتَهُنَّ إِلَّا مَا ظَهَرَ مِنْهَا وَلْيَضْرِبْنَ بِخُمُرِهِنَّ عَلَىٰ جُيُوبِهِنَّ وَلَا يُبْدِينَ زِينَتَهُنَّ إِلَّا لِبُعُولَتِهِنَّ أَوْ ءَابَآئِهِنَّ أَوْ ءَابَآءِ بُعُولَتِهِنَّ أَوْ أَبْنَآئِهِنَّ أَوْ أَبْنَآءِ بُعُولَتِهِنَّ أَوْ إِخْوَٰنِهِنَّ أَوْ بَنِيٓ إِخْوَٰنِهِنَّ أَوْ بَنِيٓ أَخَوَٰتِهِنَّ أَوْ نِسَآئِهِنَّ أَوْ مَا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَٰنُهُنَّ أَوِ التَّـٰبِعِينَ غَيْرِ أُوْلِي الْإِرْبَةِ مِنَ الرِّجَالِ أَوِ الطِّفْلِ الَّذِينَ لَمْ يَظْهَرُواْ عَلَىٰ عَوْرَٰتِ النِّسَآءِ وَلَا يَضْرِبْنَ بِأَرْجُلِهِنَّ لِيُعْلَمَ مَا يُخْفِينَ مِن زِينَتِهِنَّ وَتُوبُوٓاْ إِلَى اللَّهِ جَمِيعًا أَيُّهَ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ ﴿٣١﴾
cards.x: And turn to Allah all together, O believers, so that you may succeed.
Regret for what you did, stopping the sin straight away, and resolving never to return to it.
If the sin wronged another person, there is a fourth condition: freeing yourself of their right, by returning what you took or asking their forgiveness.

checks.q: Which is a condition of repentance?
checks.why: Regret is one of the three conditions, with stopping the sin and resolving never to return.
checks.src: al-Risalah al-Qushayriyyah, chapter on repentance · Riyad al-Salihin, chapter on repentance

checks.q: How many conditions does repentance have?
checks.why: Al-Qushayri gives three: regret, stopping straight away, and resolving never to go back.
checks.src: al-Risalah al-Qushayriyyah, chapter on repentance · Riyad al-Salihin, chapter on repentance

checks.q: Repentance means turning…
checks.a: From what the Shari'ah blames to what it praises
w: From one school of law to another
From people to a life alone
checks.why: Tawbah is turning back from what the Shari'ah blames to what it praises.
checks.src: al-Risalah al-Qushayriyyah, chapter on repentance · Riyad al-Salihin, chapter on repentance

lessons.title: Fear and hope
lessons.about: The two wings of the believer.

cards.x: The believer flies to Allah with two wings: fear of His punishment, which keeps him from sin, and hope in His mercy, which keeps him from despair. Without fear he becomes careless; without hope he gives up.

cards.ar: تَتَجَافَىٰ جُنُوبُهُمْ عَنِ الْمَضَاجِعِ يَدْعُونَ رَبَّهُمْ خَوْفٗا وَطَمَعٗا وَمِمَّا رَزَقْنَٰهُمْ يُنفِقُونَ ﴿١٦﴾
cards.x: Their sides leave their beds as they call on their Lord in fear and hope, and they spend from what We have given them.

Fear is the heart's pain at expecting something disliked. Its fruit is leaving sins. Al-Qushayri: the one who fears is not the one who weeps and wipes his eyes, but the one who leaves what he fears he will be punished for.
Hope is the heart's attachment to something loved that is coming, with effort to reach it. Hope without action is only wishful thinking.
In health and youth, let fear be stronger; at death, let hope be stronger. The Prophet ﷺ said: let none of you die except thinking well of Allah.

checks.q: What is the fruit of true fear of Allah?
checks.why: Fear is measured by what it makes you leave.

checks.q: Hope without action is…
checks.why: Real hope strives for what it hopes for.

checks.q: At the time of death, which should be stronger?
checks.why: 'Let none of you die except thinking well of Allah.'

lessons.title: The stations of the heart
lessons.about: Scrupulousness, detachment, gratitude, contentment and love.

cards.x: Leaving what is doubtful for fear of the haram. 'Leave what makes you doubt for what does not.'

cards.ar: يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ مَن يَرْتَدَّ مِنكُمْ عَن دِينِهِ فَسَوْفَ يَأْتِي اللَّهُ بِقَوْمٖ يُحِبُّهُمْ وَيُحِبُّونَهُٓ أَذِلَّةٍ عَلَى الْمُؤْمِنِينَ أَعِزَّةٍ عَلَى الْكَٰفِرِينَ يُجَٰهِدُونَ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ وَلَا يَخَافُونَ لَوْمَةَ لَآئِمٖ ذَٰلِكَ فَضْلُ اللَّهِ يُؤْتِيهِ مَن يَشَآءُ وَاللَّهُ وَٰسِعٌ عَلِيمٌ ﴿٥٤﴾
cards.x: Allah will bring a people whom He loves and who love Him, humble towards the believers, firm against the disbelievers.
Not that your hand is empty of the world, but that your heart is. Use the world, but do not let it own you.
Gratitude is with the heart (knowing every blessing is from Allah), the tongue (praising Him) and the limbs (using His blessings in obedience). 'If you are grateful, I will surely increase you.'
Being content with what Allah decrees, without objecting in the heart. It does not mean not making du'a or not trying to change things; it means not resenting His choice.
'He loves them and they love Him.' The sign of loving Allah is following His Messenger ﷺ: 'If you love Allah, follow me, and Allah will love you.'

checks.q: Zuhd means…
checks.a: The world is in your hand but not in your heart
checks.why: Detachment is of the heart.

checks.q: Gratitude is shown with…
checks.a: The heart, the tongue and the limbs
checks.why: Using blessings in obedience is gratitude of the limbs.

checks.q: What is the sign of loving Allah?
checks.why: Al 'Imran 31.

checks.q: Does contentment (rida) mean you stop making du'a?
checks.why: Rida is not resenting Allah's decree; du'a is itself worship, and the Prophet ﷺ made du'a in every state.

lessons.title: Sincerity and watching the self
lessons.about: Ikhlas, muraqabah and muhasabah.

cards.x: Doing the deed for Allah alone, not for people's praise. Al-Qushayri: sincerity is to single out Allah as the only aim in obedience. Deeds are by intentions.

cards.ar: قُلْ إِنَّمَآ أَنَا بَشَرٞ مِّثْلُكُمْ يُوحَىٰٓ إِلَيَّ أَنَّمَآ إِلَٰهُكُمْ إِلَٰهٞ وَٰحِدٞ فَمَن كَانَ يَرْجُواْ لِقَآءَ رَبِّهِ فَلْيَعْمَلْ عَمَلٗا صَٰلِحٗا وَلَا يُشْرِكْ بِعِبَادَةِ رَبِّهِٓ أَحَدَا ﴿١١٠﴾
cards.x: Whoever hopes to meet his Lord, let him do righteous deeds and associate no one in the worship of his Lord.
Knowing at every moment that Allah sees you. This is the root of ihsan: 'though you do not see Him, He sees you.' Whoever keeps it guards his limbs and his thoughts.
'Umar رضي الله عنه said: take account of yourselves before you are taken to account. Each night, look back: what did I do for Allah today, and what must I repent of?
cards.src: Sunan al-Tirmidhi, Book of the Description of the Resurrection

cards.x: Showing off can be hidden: loving to be praised, being more careful in worship when seen, hinting at one's good deeds. Keep some good deeds secret between you and Allah.
cards.src: Ihya' 'Ulum al-Din, Book of Condemning Status and Showing Off

checks.q: Sincerity means doing the deed…
w: Often, so it becomes a habit
checks.why: Deeds are by intentions.

checks.q: 'Take account of yourselves before you are taken to account' was said by…
checks.why: Narrated by al-Tirmidhi.
checks.src: Sunan al-Tirmidhi, Book of the Description of the Resurrection

checks.q: Which is a sign of hidden showing off?
checks.a: Praying more carefully when people are watching
checks.why: Keep some deeds secret.
checks.src: Ihya' 'Ulum al-Din, Book of Condemning Status and Showing Off

lessons.title: Guarding the tongue
lessons.about: Lying, backbiting and the other faults of the tongue.

cards.x: Al-Ghazali warns of the faults of the tongue, among them lying, backbiting, arguing, praising yourself and cursing.
cards.src: Bidayat al-Hidayah, the faults of the tongue

cards.x: The Prophet ﷺ described backbiting as mentioning your brother with something he would dislike. If it is true, it is backbiting; if it is false, it is slander.
The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him say what is good or stay silent.'

checks.q: Mentioning a brother's real fault behind his back is…
checks.why: If what you mention is true, it is backbiting. If it is false, it is slander.
checks.src: Bidayat al-Hidayah, the faults of the tongue · Hadith, Muslim · Hadith, al-Bukhari and Muslim

checks.q: What is backbiting (ghibah)?
checks.a: Saying something true about someone, that they would dislike
w: Saying something false about someone behind their back
Passing on someone's words to stir up trouble
Pointing out someone's fault to their face
checks.why: Even if it is true. If it is false, it is slander.

checks.q: The Prophet ﷺ said whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day should…
w: Speak little, even when it is good
checks.why: Narrated by al-Bukhari and Muslim.

lessons.title: Three illnesses of the heart
lessons.about: Envy, showing off and self-admiration.

cards.x: Envy (hasad) is wanting a blessing to leave someone, even when you gain nothing from it. Al-Ghazali quotes the hadith: 'Envy eats good deeds as fire eats wood.'
cards.src: Bidayat al-Hidayah, the faults of the heart

cards.x: Showing off (riya') is the hidden shirk: seeking a place in people's hearts through your worship. Al-Ghazali says most people are ruined by it.
cards.src: Bidayat al-Hidayah, the faults of the heart

cards.x: Self-admiration ('ujb) is being pleased with yourself and seeing yourself better than others. It leads to pride.
cards.src: Bidayat al-Hidayah, the faults of the heart

checks.q: Wishing someone's blessing would leave them is…
checks.why: Envy (hasad) is wanting a blessing to leave someone. 'Envy eats good deeds as fire eats wood.'
checks.src: Bidayat al-Hidayah, the faults of the heart

checks.q: Praying longer because people are watching is…
checks.why: Riya' is seeking a place in people's hearts through worship. Al-Ghazali calls it the hidden shirk.
checks.src: Bidayat al-Hidayah, the faults of the heart

checks.q: Seeing yourself as better than others is one of the illnesses of the heart. What is it called?
checks.why: Self-admiration leads to pride; gratitude sees the good as Allah's gift.
checks.src: Bidayat al-Hidayah, the faults of the heart

lessons.title: Remembrance of Allah
lessons.about: The heart is polished by dhikr.

cards.x: Allah commands it: 'O you who believe, remember Allah much.' (al-Ahzab 41) Dhikr is not an extra: al-Qushayri calls it the strongest pillar of the path to Allah.

cards.ar: فَاذْكُرُونِيٓ أَذْكُرْكُمْ وَاشْكُرُواْ لِي وَلَا تَكْفُرُونِ ﴿١٥٢﴾
cards.x: So remember Me; I will remember you. Be grateful to Me, and do not be ungrateful.

cards.ar: الَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَتَطْمَئِنُّ قُلُوبُهُم بِذِكْرِ اللَّهِ أَلَا بِذِكْرِ اللَّهِ تَطْمَئِنُّ الْقُلُوبُ ﴿٢٨﴾
cards.x: Truly, in the remembrance of Allah hearts find rest.
Allah says: 'So remember Me, I will remember you.' (al-Baqarah 152)
'Truly, in the remembrance of Allah hearts find rest.' (al-Ra'd 28)

checks.q: What is dhikr for the one travelling to Allah?
checks.a: The mainstay of the path to Allah
w: An extra for those who have finished their duties
A practice for the end of one's life
A practice for the scholars alone
checks.why: Al-Qushayri says dhikr is a strong pillar of the path to Allah, indeed its mainstay: no one reaches Allah except by constant remembrance.

checks.q: Allah says in al-Baqarah 152: 'Remember Me…'
checks.why: Al-Baqarah 152.

checks.q: In what do hearts find rest?
checks.why: Al-Ra'd 28.

lessons.title: Trust in Allah (tawakkul)
lessons.about: Relying on Allah while taking the means.

cards.x: 'Whoever puts his trust in Allah, He is enough for him.' (al-Talaq 3) Trust is in the heart; the limbs still take the means. The Prophet ﷺ said: tie your camel, then trust.

cards.ar: وَيَرْزُقْهُ مِنْ حَيْثُ لَا يَحْتَسِبُ وَمَن يَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَى اللَّهِ فَهُوَ حَسْبُهُٓ إِنَّ اللَّهَ بَٰلِغُ أَمْرِهِ قَدْ جَعَلَ اللَّهُ لِكُلِّ شَيْءٖ قَدْرٗا ﴿٣﴾
cards.x: Whoever puts his trust in Allah, He is enough for him.
'And upon Allah let the believers rely.' (Al 'Imran 122)
A man asked whether to tie his camel and trust Allah, or leave it and trust. The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Tie it, and trust.'

checks.q: Allah says in al-Talaq 3: 'Whoever puts his trust in Allah…'
w: '…He will make a way out for him'
checks.why: Al-Talaq 3, quoted at the start of al-Qushayri's chapter.

checks.q: Does trusting Allah mean leaving the means?
checks.a: No: tie your camel, then trust
w: Yes, once you have made du'a
Only in worldly matters, not religious ones
checks.why: The hadith joins taking the means with trust in Allah.

checks.q: Tawakkul is in the heart. What about working with the limbs?
w: It is only for those weak in faith
checks.why: Al-Qushayri: the place of tawakkul is the heart, and outward action does not contradict the heart's trust.

lessons.title: Patience (sabr)
lessons.about: Patience is by Allah's help.

cards.x: 'Be patient, and your patience is only by Allah.' (al-Nahl 127) Patience itself is a gift from Allah, so ask Him for it, and do not rely on your own strength.

cards.ar: يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ اسْتَعِينُواْ بِالصَّبْرِ وَالصَّلَوٰةِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ مَعَ الصَّـٰبِرِينَ ﴿١٥٣﴾
cards.x: O you who believe, seek help through patience and prayer. Truly Allah is with the patient.
'O you who believe, seek help through patience and prayer. Truly Allah is with the patient.' (al-Baqarah 153)
The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Patience is at the first blow.'

checks.q: Allah says in al-Nahl 127: 'Be patient, and your patience is only…'
checks.why: Al-Nahl 127, quoted at the start of al-Qushayri's chapter.

checks.q: Allah is with…
checks.why: Al-Baqarah 153.

checks.q: When does true patience count most?
checks.why: 'Patience is at the first blow.' (al-Bukhari and Muslim)

lessons.title: Advice to a student
lessons.about: Al-Ghazali's advice on knowledge, action and time.

cards.x: Al-Ghazali wrote to his student: 'Knowledge without action is madness, and action without knowledge does not happen.'
Knowledge will not keep you away from sins today, nor bring you to obey, unless you act on it.
Al-Ghazali says: your moments are your life, and your life is your capital. Every breath is a jewel that cannot be replaced once it is gone.
cards.src: Bidayat al-Hidayah, on guarding your time

checks.q: Knowledge without action is…
checks.why: Al-Ghazali, in Ayyuha al-Walad: 'Knowledge without action is madness, and action without knowledge does not happen.'
checks.src: Ayyuha al-Walad, the letter · Bidayat al-Hidayah, on guarding your time

checks.q: What makes knowledge benefit you?
checks.why: Knowledge only keeps you from sin and brings you to obedience when you act on it.
checks.src: Ayyuha al-Walad, the letter · Bidayat al-Hidayah, on guarding your time

checks.q: What is your life, in the words of the scholars of the heart?
checks.why: Al-Ghazali: your moments are your life, and your life is your capital. Every breath is a jewel.
checks.src: Ayyuha al-Walad, the letter · Bidayat al-Hidayah, on guarding your time

lessons.title: The tariqahs
lessons.about: The great Sufi paths, and what they share.

cards.x: A tariqah ('path') is a school of tazkiyah: a chain (silsilah) of teachers reaching back to the Prophet ﷺ, with a set of practices of dhikr, companionship and discipline, under a guide. Like the schools of fiqh, they differ in method, not in religion.

cards.ar: وَأَلَّوِ اسْتَقَٰمُواْ عَلَى الطَّرِيقَةِ لَأَسْقَيْنَٰهُم مَّآءً غَدَقٗا ﴿١٦﴾
cards.x: Had they kept straight on the way (al-tariqah), We would have given them abundant water to drink.

Among the best known: the Qadiri (Shaykh 'Abd al-Qadir al-Jilani, Baghdad, d. 561 AH), the Rifa'i (Ahmad al-Rifa'i, Iraq, d. 578 AH), the Suhrawardi (Shihab al-Din 'Umar al-Suhrawardi, Baghdad, d. 632 AH), the Chishti (spread in India by Khwajah Mu'in al-Din Chishti, d. 633 AH), the Shadhili (Abu al-Hasan al-Shadhili, d. 656 AH) and the Naqshbandi (Baha' al-Din Naqshband, Bukhara, d. 791 AH), قدس الله أسرارهم.
cards.src: Tarikh al-Khulafa', and the biographies of the masters

cards.x: Most tariqahs trace their chain through 'Ali رضي الله عنه; the Naqshbandi chain runs through Abu Bakr al-Siddiq رضي الله عنه. Every sound chain ends with the Prophet ﷺ.
cards.src: al-Risalah al-Qushayriyyah, the masters of the path

cards.x: Some emphasise dhikr aloud in gatherings, others silent dhikr of the heart; some emphasise service, others study or seclusion. The aim is one: a heart present with Allah and a life upon the Sunnah.
The Ahl al-Sunnah respect every sound tariqah and its masters. Belonging to one path never means looking down on another, or on Muslims who follow none.

checks.q: What is a silsilah?
checks.a: A chain of teachers going back to the Prophet ﷺ
w: The lodge where a shaykh teaches
A collection of a shaykh's sayings
checks.why: Every sound tariqah has a connected chain.
checks.src: al-Risalah al-Qushayriyyah, the masters of the path

checks.q: Through which Companion does the main Naqshbandi chain reach the Prophet ﷺ?
checks.a: Abu Bakr al-Siddiq رضي الله عنه
w: Khalid ibn al-Walid رضي الله عنه
checks.why: Most other chains pass through 'Ali رضي الله عنه.
checks.src: al-Risalah al-Qushayriyyah, the masters of the path

checks.q: The Qadiri tariqah is named after…
checks.why: He taught in Baghdad and died in 561 AH.
checks.src: Tarikh al-Khulafa', and the biographies of the masters

checks.q: The tariqahs differ in…
checks.why: Like the schools of fiqh.

lessons.title: The shaykh and companionship
lessons.about: Why the masters advise taking a guide, and how to know a true one.

cards.x: Faults of the self are hard to see in oneself. As one learns fiqh from a faqih and Qur'an from a qari, one learns the path from someone who has travelled it. Al-Ghazali, after searching alone, found his cure with the people of the path.
cards.src: al-Munqidh min al-Dalal, the way of the Sufis

cards.ar: وَاصْبِرْ نَفْسَكَ مَعَ الَّذِينَ يَدْعُونَ رَبَّهُم بِالْغَدَوٰةِ وَالْعَشِيِّ يُرِيدُونَ وَجْهَهُ وَلَا تَعْدُ عَيْنَاكَ عَنْهُمْ تُرِيدُ زِينَةَ الْحَيَوٰةِ الدُّنْيَا وَلَا تُطِعْ مَنْ أَغْفَلْنَا قَلْبَهُ عَن ذِكْرِنَا وَاتَّبَعَ هَوَىٰهُ وَكَانَ أَمْرُهُ فُرُطٗا ﴿٢٨﴾
cards.x: Keep yourself patiently with those who call on their Lord morning and evening, seeking His face.

cards.ar: يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ اتَّقُواْ اللَّهَ وَكُونُواْ مَعَ الصَّـٰدِقِينَ ﴿١١٩﴾
cards.x: O you who believe, be mindful of Allah and be with the truthful.
The Companions were made Companions by sitting with the Prophet ﷺ. Allah says: keep yourself patiently with those who call on their Lord morning and evening, and: be with the truthful.

He holds firmly to the Shari'ah, has sound knowledge of the deen, a connected chain, good character, and his company increases you in remembrance of Allah and following the Sunnah. The Prophet ﷺ said the best of people are those who, when seen, remind you of Allah.
cards.src: Sunan Ibn Majah, Book of Zuhd

cards.x: Anyone who neglects the prayer, permits the haram, takes people's wealth, demands blind obedience in sin, or says the Shari'ah is not for him is no guide, whatever wonders are claimed.

Taking a pledge (bay'ah) with a shaykh is a promise to keep to the Shari'ah and the practices of the path under his guidance. The Companions pledged to the Prophet ﷺ on more than belief, such as 'not to ask people for anything'.

checks.q: What is a sign of a true spiritual guide?
checks.a: His company increases you in remembrance and the Sunnah
w: He has a long chain of shaykhs
checks.why: The best are those whose sight reminds you of Allah.
checks.src: Sunan Ibn Majah, Book of Zuhd

checks.q: Someone claiming to be a shaykh asks you to commit a sin. You…
w: Ask him to pray for you first
checks.why: No one may be obeyed in disobedience to Allah; one who calls to sin is no guide.

checks.q: In al-Kahf 28, Allah tells the Prophet ﷺ to keep company with whom?
checks.a: Those who call on their Lord morning and evening
w: Those most learned in the law
Those of noble lineage and rank
Those who have left the world entirely
checks.why: 'Keep yourself patiently with those who call on their Lord morning and evening.'

lessons.title: States, wonders and the Shari'ah
lessons.about: Keeping experiences in their place.

cards.x: A state (hal) is something that comes over the heart as a gift, like awe or longing, and passes; a station (maqam) is what is earned by effort and stays, like repentance and patience. Neither is a goal in itself.
cards.src: al-Risalah al-Qushayriyyah, chapter on states and stations

cards.ar: أَلَآ إِنَّ أَوْلِيَآءَ اللَّهِ لَا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ ﴿٦٢﴾ الَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَكَانُواْ يَتَّقُونَ ﴿٦٣﴾
cards.x: Truly the friends of Allah: no fear shall be upon them, nor shall they grieve. Those who believe and are mindful of Allah.

Ahl al-Sunnah believe Allah honours His friends with wonders (karamat), as with Maryam's provision and the companions of the cave. A karamah of a wali is a sign of the truth of the Prophet ﷺ he follows.

cards.t: But they are not the measure
cards.x: Abu Yazid al-Bistami said: if you see a man given wonders, even sitting cross-legged in the air, do not be deceived until you see how he keeps the commands and prohibitions and the limits of the Shari'ah.
cards.src: al-Risalah al-Qushayriyyah, the masters of the path

cards.x: A good dream can be glad tidings, but dreams and inner experiences never make anything halal or haram, and never override the Qur'an, the Sunnah or the scholars.

checks.q: A man performs wonders but ignores the Shari'ah. He is…
checks.why: Abu Yazid: look at how he keeps the commands and prohibitions.
checks.src: al-Risalah al-Qushayriyyah, the masters of the path

checks.q: Can a dream make something halal or haram?
w: Yes, if the dreamer is pious
checks.why: Rulings come from the Qur'an and Sunnah.

checks.q: A station (maqam) differs from a state (hal) in that it is…
checks.why: States come and go; stations are earned.
checks.src: al-Risalah al-Qushayriyyah, chapter on states and stations

lessons.title: "Isn't tasawwuf an innovation?"
lessons.about: Answering the common objection with knowledge and good manners.

cards.x: Some say tasawwuf is not from Islam because the word is not in the Qur'an or hadith, or because of things some people calling themselves Sufis have done.

cards.ar: وَإِن جَٰهَدَاكَ عَلَىٰٓ أَن تُشْرِكَ بِي مَا لَيْسَ لَكَ بِهِ عِلْمٞ فَلَا تُطِعْهُمَا وَصَاحِبْهُمَا فِي الدُّنْيَا مَعْرُوفٗا وَاتَّبِعْ سَبِيلَ مَنْ أَنَابَ إِلَيَّ ثُمَّ إِلَيَّ مَرْجِعُكُمْ فَأُنَبِّئُكُم بِمَا كُنتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ ﴿١٥﴾
cards.x: …and follow the way of the one who turns to Me.
Ihsan, tazkiyah, dhikr, repentance, sincerity and good character are in the Qur'an and Sunnah. A new name for a sound science is like 'fiqh', 'usul' or 'tajweed'.

The great scholars of Ahl al-Sunnah, such as al-Qushayri, al-Ghazali, al-Nawawi, Ibn 'Abidin and Shah Wali Allah, praised and practised tasawwuf bound by the Shari'ah, and criticised anything against it. Wrong actions by some are judged by the Shari'ah, not blamed on the science.
cards.src: al-Munqidh min al-Dalal, the way of the Sufis

cards.x: Answer with knowledge and gentleness, not argument for its own sake. The best invitation to tasawwuf is the character of the one who practises it.

checks.q: Some call tasawwuf an innovation because the name came later. How do the scholars answer?
checks.a: Fiqh and tajweed were named later too; the substance was there from the start
w: The name is an innovation, but the practice is allowed
It is an innovation, but a good one (bid'ah hasanah)
The name was already used by the Companions
checks.why: The substance is from the Qur'an and Sunnah.

checks.q: Wrong actions by some who call themselves Sufis are…
checks.a: Judged by the Shari'ah, not blamed on the science
checks.why: The same is true of any science.
checks.src: al-Munqidh min al-Dalal, the way of the Sufis

checks.q: What is the best invitation to tasawwuf?
checks.a: The good character of those who practise it
checks.why: Good character is at the heart of it.

lessons.title: Seeking a path
lessons.about: Taking the first steps towards a guide, without rushing.

cards.x: Keep the obligations, leave the sins, and hold to a small daily wird: the morning and evening adhkar, some Qur'an, salawat on the Prophet ﷺ and seeking forgiveness. The deeds most loved by Allah are the most constant, even if small.
cards.src: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Softening the Heart

cards.ar: وَالَّذِينَ جَٰهَدُواْ فِينَا لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَنَا وَإِنَّ اللَّهَ لَمَعَ الْمُحْسِنِينَ ﴿٦٩﴾
cards.x: And those who strive for Us, We will surely guide them to Our paths. Truly Allah is with those who do good.
'Those who strive for Us, We will surely guide them to Our paths.' Make du'a sincerely to be shown a guide, and pray istikharah.
Attend gatherings of knowledge and dhikr, sit with the righteous, and ask scholars you trust about the guides they know. A person follows the religion of his close friend.
cards.src: Sunan Abi Dawud, Book of Good Manners

cards.x: Watch before you pledge: is the guide firm on the Shari'ah, knowledgeable, of good character, and does his company bring you closer to Allah? Then take the step, with sincerity and respect, and stay with it.
The search itself is a gift from Allah. Whoever turns to Him a hand's span, He turns to him an arm's length, and whoever walks to Him, He comes to him running.

checks.q: Which deeds are most loved by Allah?
checks.a: The most constant, even if small
checks.why: A small wird kept daily beats a large one dropped.
checks.src: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Softening the Heart

checks.q: What matters most when choosing a spiritual guide?
checks.a: That he is firm on the Shari'ah and the Sunnah
w: That he has a long, famous chain
That he is known for wonders (karamat)
That he comes from a family of shaykhs
checks.why: Do not rush; watch first.

title: The Companions and Ahl al-Bayt
sub: The four caliphs, the ten, the Mothers of the Believers and the Prophet's family ﷺ

lessons.title: Who the Companions are
lessons.about: Their rank, and why we love them.

cards.x: A Companion (sahabi) is someone who met the Prophet ﷺ as a believer and died as a Muslim. They carried the Qur'an and the Sunnah to us.

cards.ar: وَالسَّـٰبِقُونَ الْأَوَّلُونَ مِنَ الْمُهَٰجِرِينَ وَالْأَنصَارِ وَالَّذِينَ اتَّبَعُوهُم بِإِحْسَٰنٖ رضي الله عنهم وَرَضُواْ عَنْهُ وَأَعَدَّ لَهُمْ جَنَّـٰتٖ تَجْرِي تَحْتَهَا الْأَنْهَٰرُ خَٰلِدِينَ فِيهَآ أَبَدٗا ذَٰلِكَ الْفَوْزُ الْعَظِيمُ ﴿١٠٠﴾
cards.x: And the foremost, the first of the Muhajirun and the Ansar, and those who followed them in excellence: Allah is pleased with them and they are pleased with Him.

cards.ar: مُّحَمَّدٞ رَّسُولُ اللَّهِ وَالَّذِينَ مَعَهُٓ أَشِدَّآءُ عَلَى الْكُفَّارِ رُحَمَآءُ بَيْنَهُمْ تَرَىٰهُمْ رُكَّعٗا سُجَّدٗا يَبْتَغُونَ فَضْلٗا مِّنَ اللَّهِ وَرِضْوَٰنٗا سِيمَاهُمْ فِي وُجُوهِهِم مِّنْ أَثَرِ السُّجُودِ ذَٰلِكَ مَثَلُهُمْ فِي التَّوْرَىٰةِ وَمَثَلُهُمْ فِي الْإِنجِيلِ كَزَرْعٍ أَخْرَجَ شَطْـَٔهُ فَـَٔازَرَهُ فَاسْتَغْلَظَ فَاسْتَوَىٰ عَلَىٰ سُوقِهِ يُعْجِبُ الزُّرَّاعَ لِيَغِيظَ بِهِمُ الْكُفَّارَ وَعَدَ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ الصَّـٰلِحَٰتِ مِنْهُم مَّغْفِرَةٗ وَأَجْرًا عَظِيمَا ﴿٢٩﴾
cards.x: Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, and those with him are firm against the disbelievers, merciful to one another.

The Prophet ﷺ said: the best of people are my generation, then those after them, then those after them. Allah said He is pleased with the foremost Muhajirun and Ansar, and those who follow them in excellence.

We love them all, go to excess about none of them, disown none, speak of them only with good, and keep silent about the disputes between them. Loving them is religion and faith; hating them is disbelief, hypocrisy and transgression.

checks.q: Who counts as a Companion (sahabi)?
checks.a: One who met the Prophet ﷺ as a believer and died Muslim
w: Anyone who lived in his ﷺ time
checks.why: Even a brief meeting as a believer is enough.

checks.q: Which generation did the Prophet ﷺ call the best of people?
checks.why: Then those after them, then those after them.

checks.q: How do we speak about the disputes between the Companions?
checks.a: We keep silent and speak of them only with good
checks.why: They were people of excellence; Allah will judge between them.

checks.q: Loving the Companions is…
w: Recommended, but not part of faith
Required for the Ahl al-Bayt, not the rest
checks.why: And hating them is disbelief, hypocrisy and transgression.
