lessons.title: Abu Bakr al-Siddiq رضي الله عنه
lessons.about: The first caliph, and the best of the Ummah after its Prophet ﷺ.

cards.x: 'Abdullah ibn Abi Quhafah, the first free man to believe. He was called al-Siddiq (the truthful) for affirming the Night Journey at once: 'If he said it, then it is true.'
cards.src: Tarikh al-Khulafa', Abu Bakr رضي الله عنه

cards.ar: إِلَّا تَنصُرُوهُ فَقَدْ نَصَرَهُ اللَّهُ إِذْ أَخْرَجَهُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ ثَانِيَ اثْنَيْنِ إِذْ هُمَا فِي الْغَارِ إِذْ يَقُولُ لِصَٰحِبِهِ لَا تَحْزَنْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ مَعَنَا فَأَنزَلَ اللَّهُ سَكِينَتَهُ عَلَيْهِ وَأَيَّدَهُ بِجُنُودٖ لَّمْ تَرَوْهَا وَجَعَلَ كَلِمَةَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ السُّفْلَىٰ وَكَلِمَةُ اللَّهِ هِيَ الْعُلْيَا وَاللَّهُ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمٌ ﴿٤٠﴾
cards.x: …the second of two, when they were in the cave, when he said to his companion: 'Do not grieve, Allah is with us.'
He accompanied the Prophet ﷺ on the Hijrah and hid with him ﷺ in the Cave of Thawr. Allah mentions him: 'the second of two, when they were in the cave.'
He was caliph for about two years. He stood firm against those who refused zakat and against the false prophets, and began the gathering of the Qur'an into one volume.
cards.src: Tarikh al-Khulafa', Abu Bakr رضي الله عنه

checks.q: Why was Abu Bakr رضي الله عنه called al-Siddiq?
checks.a: For affirming the Prophet ﷺ at once
checks.why: He affirmed the Prophet ﷺ without hesitation, most famously the Night Journey, which others doubted.

checks.q: Who was with the Prophet ﷺ in the Cave of Thawr on the Hijrah?
w: Zayd ibn Harithah رضي الله عنه
checks.why: 'The second of two, when they were in the cave.' (al-Tawbah 40)

checks.q: What did Abu Bakr رضي الله عنه begin during his caliphate?
checks.a: Gathering the Qur'an into one volume
w: Building the Dome of the Rock
checks.why: Zayd ibn Thabit رضي الله عنه gathered it at his command.

checks.q: Who is the best of this Ummah after the Prophet ﷺ, according to Ahl al-Sunnah?
checks.a: Abu Bakr, then 'Umar, then 'Uthman, then 'Ali رضي الله عنهم
w: 'Ali, then Abu Bakr رضي الله عنهما
'Umar, then Abu Bakr رضي الله عنهما
checks.why: The order of their caliphate is the order of their excellence.

lessons.title: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab رضي الله عنه
lessons.about: Al-Faruq, the second caliph.

cards.x: His acceptance of Islam was a great strength for the Muslims; after it they prayed openly at the Ka'bah. He was named al-Faruq, the one who separates truth from falsehood.
Caliph for ten years, he was known for justice and fearing Allah. Under him Syria, Iraq, Persia and Egypt opened, and Jerusalem was received peacefully.
He began the Hijri calendar, gathered the people for tarawih behind one imam, and set up the public treasury and offices. He was martyred while leading the Fajr prayer.

checks.q: What title was 'Umar رضي الله عنه given?
checks.why: The one who separates truth from falsehood.

checks.q: Which calendar did 'Umar رضي الله عنه begin?
checks.why: Counting from the Hijrah of the Prophet ﷺ.

checks.q: How was 'Umar رضي الله عنه martyred?
checks.a: Stabbed while leading the Fajr prayer
checks.why: He was stabbed by Abu Lu'lu'ah in the masjid.

checks.q: Which city was received peacefully in 'Umar's رضي الله عنه caliphate, with him coming to accept its keys?
checks.why: 'Umar رضي الله عنه travelled to receive it himself.

lessons.title: 'Uthman ibn 'Affan رضي الله عنه
lessons.about: Dhu al-Nurayn, the third caliph.

cards.x: He married two daughters of the Prophet ﷺ, Ruqayyah رضي الله عنها and then Umm Kulthum رضي الله عنهما, and was called Dhu al-Nurayn, the possessor of two lights. He was known for his modesty; even the angels were shy of him.
He bought the well of Rumah for the Muslims and equipped the army of Tabuk from his own wealth.
As caliph for twelve years, he had the Qur'an copied in one standard text from Abu Bakr's volume and sent to the cities. He was martyred in his house while reading the Qur'an.

checks.q: Why was 'Uthman رضي الله عنه called Dhu al-Nurayn?
checks.a: He married two daughters of the Prophet ﷺ
checks.why: Ruqayyah رضي الله عنها, then after her death Umm Kulthum رضي الله عنهما.

checks.q: What did 'Uthman رضي الله عنه do with the Qur'an?
checks.a: Had standard copies sent to the cities
w: First gathered it into one volume
checks.why: Abu Bakr رضي الله عنه gathered it; 'Uthman رضي الله عنه made the standard copies.

checks.q: Which quality was 'Uthman رضي الله عنه especially known for?
checks.why: The Prophet ﷺ said: shall I not be shy of a man of whom the angels are shy?

lessons.title: 'Ali ibn Abi Talib رضي الله عنه
lessons.about: The fourth caliph, the Prophet's ﷺ cousin and son-in-law.

cards.x: He was raised in the Prophet's ﷺ home and was the first child to accept Islam. He slept in the Prophet's ﷺ bed on the night of the Hijrah, and married Fatimah رضي الله عنها.
The Prophet ﷺ said to him: you are to me as Harun was to Musa, except there is no prophet after me. At Khaybar he was given the banner and the fort was opened at his hands.
cards.src: Sahih al-Bukhari, Virtues of the Companions

cards.x: He was caliph for about five years in a time of trials, and was martyred in Kufah on his way to Fajr. Many chains of the Sufis and scholars go back through him.

checks.q: Who slept in the Prophet's ﷺ bed on the night of the Hijrah?
w: Zayd ibn Harithah رضي الله عنه
checks.why: He risked his life so the Prophet ﷺ could leave safely.

checks.q: The Prophet ﷺ told 'Ali رضي الله عنه: 'You are to me as … was to Musa.'
checks.why: Except that there is no prophet after me.

checks.q: Which daughter of the Prophet ﷺ did 'Ali رضي الله عنه marry?
checks.why: Their sons were al-Hasan and al-Husayn رضي الله عنهما.

checks.q: Where was 'Ali رضي الله عنه martyred?
checks.a: In Kufah, on his way to Fajr
checks.why: Karbala is where his son al-Husayn رضي الله عنه was martyred.

lessons.title: The ten promised Paradise
lessons.about: The Companions named together in one hadith.

cards.x: The Prophet ﷺ named ten Companions in one sitting as people of Paradise: Abu Bakr, 'Umar, 'Uthman, 'Ali, Talhah, al-Zubayr, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf, Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, Sa'id ibn Zayd and Abu 'Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah رضي الله عنهم.
The ten are not the only ones promised Paradise. Others were given glad tidings too, such as Khadijah, Fatimah, al-Hasan, al-Husayn, Bilal رضي الله عنهم and the people of Badr.

checks.q: Which of these is one of the ten promised Paradise?
checks.a: Abu 'Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah رضي الله عنه
w: Khalid ibn al-Walid رضي الله عنه
Mu'adh ibn Jabal رضي الله عنه
checks.why: Named with Abu Bakr, 'Umar, 'Uthman, 'Ali, Talhah, al-Zubayr, 'Abd al-Rahman, Sa'd and Sa'id رضي الله عنهم.

checks.q: Are the ten the only people promised Paradise?
checks.a: No, others were given glad tidings too
w: Yes, the ten and the Prophets
checks.why: Such as Khadijah, Fatimah, al-Hasan, al-Husayn رضي الله عنهم and the people of Badr.

checks.q: Which of these is not among the ten promised Paradise?
checks.a: Bilal ibn Rabah رضي الله عنه
w: Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas رضي الله عنه
al-Zubayr ibn al-'Awwam رضي الله عنه
checks.why: Bilal رضي الله عنه was also given glad tidings of Paradise, in another hadith.

lessons.title: The Mothers of the Believers
lessons.about: The wives of the Prophet ﷺ.

cards.x: Allah called the Prophet's ﷺ wives the Mothers of the Believers. We honour them as our mothers.

cards.ar: النَّبِيُّ أَوْلَىٰ بِالْمُؤْمِنِينَ مِنْ أَنفُسِهِمْ وَأَزْوَٰجُهُٓ أُمَّهَٰتُهُمْ وَأُوْلُواْ الْأَرْحَامِ بَعْضُهُمْ أَوْلَىٰ بِبَعْضٖ فِي كِتَٰبِ اللَّهِ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَالْمُهَٰجِرِينَ إِلَّآ أَن تَفْعَلُوٓاْ إِلَىٰٓ أَوْلِيَآئِكُم مَّعْرُوفٗا كَانَ ذَٰلِكَ فِي الْكِتَٰبِ مَسْطُورٗا ﴿٦﴾
cards.x: The Prophet is closer to the believers than their own selves, and his wives are their mothers.

Khadijah bint Khuwaylid رضي الله عنها was his first wife, the first to believe, and the mother of his children except Ibrahim. 'A'ishah bint Abi Bakr رضي الله عنها was among the most learned of the Companions; many of the Sunnah's rulings come through her.
cards.src: al-Fusul fi Sirat al-Rasul, his wives

cards.x: See the Mothers of the Believers in the order he ﷺ married them, with a line about each.
cards.src: Ibn Kathir, al-Fusul fi Sirat al-Rasul, his wives

cards.x: Sawdah, Hafsah, Zaynab bint Khuzaymah, Umm Salamah, Zaynab bint Jahsh, Juwayriyah, Umm Habibah, Safiyyah and Maymunah رضي الله عنهن.
cards.src: al-Fusul fi Sirat al-Rasul, his wives

checks.q: What did Allah call the wives of the Prophet ﷺ?
checks.why: 'And his wives are their mothers.' (al-Ahzab 6)

checks.q: Who was the first wife of the Prophet ﷺ and the first to believe?
checks.why: She supported him with her wealth and her heart.

checks.q: Which Mother of the Believers was among the most learned of the Companions?
checks.why: Senior Companions came to her with their questions.

checks.q: Hafsah رضي الله عنها was the daughter of…
checks.why: 'A'ishah رضي الله عنها was the daughter of Abu Bakr.

lessons.title: The Ahl al-Bayt
lessons.about: The family of the Prophet ﷺ, and loving them.

cards.x: The Ahl al-Bayt are the family of the Prophet ﷺ: his ﷺ wives, Fatimah, 'Ali, al-Hasan, al-Husayn رضي الله عنهم and their descendants, and the believers of Banu Hashim. Zakat may not be given to them, out of honour.

cards.ar: وَقَرْنَ فِي بُيُوتِكُنَّ وَلَا تَبَرَّجْنَ تَبَرُّجَ الْجَٰهِلِيَّةِ الْأُولَىٰ وَأَقِمْنَ الصَّلَوٰةَ وَءَاتِينَ الزَّكَوٰةَ وَأَطِعْنَ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُٓ إِنَّمَا يُرِيدُ اللَّهُ لِيُذْهِبَ عَنكُمُ الرِّجْسَ أَهْلَ الْبَيْتِ وَيُطَهِّرَكُمْ تَطْهِيرٗا ﴿٣٣﴾
cards.x: Allah only wishes to remove impurity from you, O people of the House, and to purify you completely.
His ﷺ youngest daughter. He ﷺ said: Fatimah is a part of me; whoever angers her angers me. She is the leader of the women of Paradise.
cards.src: Sahih al-Bukhari, Virtues of the Companions

cards.t: Al-Hasan and al-Husayn رضي الله عنه
cards.x: He ﷺ called them his ﷺ two sweet basils of this world, and said they are the leaders of the youth of Paradise. Al-Husayn رضي الله عنه was martyred at Karbala in 61 AH, a great tragedy for the Ummah.
He ﷺ said: I leave among you two weighty things: the Book of Allah, and the people of my house. I remind you of Allah regarding the people of my house. Loving them is part of loving him ﷺ.
cards.src: Sahih Muslim, Virtues of the Companions

checks.q: Who did the Prophet ﷺ call the leaders of the youth of Paradise?
checks.a: Al-Hasan and al-Husayn رضي الله عنهما
w: Abu Bakr and 'Umar رضي الله عنهما
Zayd and Usamah رضي الله عنهما
checks.why: Narrated by al-Tirmidhi.

checks.q: Where was al-Husayn رضي الله عنه martyred?
checks.why: In 61 AH, on the day of 'Ashura'.

checks.q: What did the Prophet ﷺ say he ﷺ left among us, in Sahih Muslim?
checks.a: The Book of Allah and the people of his house
w: The Book of Allah and the Ka'bah
The Book of Allah and the Companions
checks.why: 'I remind you of Allah regarding the people of my house,' three times.

checks.q: Why may zakat not be given to Banu Hashim?
checks.a: Out of honour for the Prophet's ﷺ family
checks.why: Help them with gifts and charity that is not zakat.

lessons.title: Loving both, the way of Ahl al-Sunnah
lessons.about: Holding the Companions and the Ahl al-Bayt together in the heart.

cards.x: Ahl al-Sunnah love the Companions and the Ahl al-Bayt together, with no contradiction. 'Ali رضي الله عنه named his sons Abu Bakr, 'Umar and 'Uthman, and 'Umar رضي الله عنهم married Umm Kulthum رضي الله عنها, daughter of 'Ali and Fatimah رضي الله عنها.
We believe the caliphate after the Prophet ﷺ was for Abu Bakr, then 'Umar, then 'Uthman, then 'Ali رضي الله عنهم, the Rightly Guided Caliphs, and their excellence is in that order.

We do not curse any Companion, as some do, and we do not belittle the Ahl al-Bayt, as others do. Whoever speaks well of the Companions, the Prophet's ﷺ wives and his ﷺ descendants is free of hypocrisy.

checks.q: Who are the four Rightly Guided Caliphs, in order?
checks.why: Their excellence follows the order of their caliphate.

checks.q: Which shows the love between 'Ali رضي الله عنه and the caliphs before him?
checks.a: 'Ali رضي الله عنه named his sons Abu Bakr, 'Umar and 'Uthman رضي الله عنهم
w: He refused to speak to them
He refused to pray behind them
checks.why: Names a father gives his sons show his love.

checks.q: What is the way of Ahl al-Sunnah with the Companions and the Ahl al-Bayt?
checks.why: Al-Tahawi: whoever speaks well of them is free of hypocrisy.

title: Daily life: adab and adhkar
sub: The sunnah way to wake, eat, dress, greet, sleep, and guard the limbs
book: Bidayat al-Hidayah, al-Adhkar and Riyad al-Salihin

lessons.title: Waking up and the morning
lessons.about: Starting the day the sunnah way.

cards.x: Say: 'Al-hamdu lillahi alladhi ahyana ba'da ma amatana wa ilayhi al-nushur' (praise be to Allah who gave us life after He caused us to die, and to Him is the return). Use the siwak.
Al-Ghazali advises waking before dawn, making wudu, praying the two sunnah rak'ahs of Fajr at home, then going to pray Fajr in congregation.
cards.src: Bidayat al-Hidayah, the adab of waking

cards.x: Sitting in remembrance of Allah after Fajr until the sun has risen, then praying two rak'ahs, carries the reward of a complete Hajj and 'umrah, as in the hadith.

checks.q: What do you say on waking up?
checks.a: 'Al-hamdu lillahi alladhi ahyana ba'da ma amatana…'
checks.why: Praise to Allah who gave us life after death (sleep). The second option is said before sleeping.

checks.q: What reward is in the hadith for staying in dhikr after Fajr until sunrise, then praying two rak'ahs?
checks.why: Narrated by al-Tirmidhi.

checks.q: Where is it best to pray the sunnah of Fajr?
checks.a: At home, before going to the masjid
w: In the masjid, before the fard
In the masjid, after the fard
checks.why: The sunnah prayers are best at home.

lessons.title: Morning and evening adhkar
lessons.about: The daily protection every Muslim should keep.

cards.x: Recite Surat al-Ikhlas, al-Falaq and al-Nas three times in the morning and three in the evening; the Prophet ﷺ said they will suffice you against everything.
cards.src: Sunan Abi Dawud, Book of Manners

cards.x: Whoever recites Ayat al-Kursi in the morning is protected until evening, and in the evening until morning.

O Allah, You are my Lord; there is no god but You. You created me and I am Your servant, and I keep Your covenant and promise as far as I am able. I seek refuge in You from the evil of what I have done. I acknowledge Your favour upon me, and I acknowledge my sin, so forgive me, for none forgives sins but You. Whoever says it with certainty in the morning and dies that day is of the people of Paradise; the same for the evening.
cards.ar: اللَّهُمَّ أَنْتَ رَبِّي لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ، خَلَقْتَنِي وَأَنَا عَبْدُكَ، وَأَنَا عَلَى عَهْدِكَ وَوَعْدِكَ مَا اسْتَطَعْتُ، أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا صَنَعْتُ، أَبُوءُ لَكَ بِنِعْمَتِكَ عَلَيَّ، وَأَبُوءُ لَكَ بِذَنْبِي، فَاغْفِرْ لِي، فَإِنَّهُ لَا يَغْفِرُ الذُّنُوبَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ

cards.x: 'Subhan Allahi wa bi-hamdih' a hundred times a day wipes away sins even if they are like the foam of the sea.

checks.q: How many times are the three Quls (al-Ikhlas, al-Falaq and al-Nas) recited morning and evening?
checks.why: The Prophet ﷺ said they suffice against everything.

checks.q: Which du'a did the Prophet ﷺ call 'Sayyid al-Istighfar'?
checks.a: 'Allahumma anta rabbi, la ilaha illa ant…'
checks.why: 'Allahumma anta rabbi…', the master of seeking forgiveness; whoever says it with certainty and dies that day or night is of the people of Paradise.

checks.q: Saying 'Subhan Allahi wa bi-hamdih' a hundred times a day…
checks.a: Wipes away sins, even like the foam of the sea
w: Protects you from harm until evening
checks.why: Narrated by al-Bukhari.

checks.q: Which verse protects you from morning until evening when recited?
checks.why: Al-Baqarah 255.

lessons.title: After the prayer
lessons.about: What the Prophet ﷺ said after every fard prayer.

cards.x: After the salam, say 'Astaghfirullah' three times, then 'Allahumma anta al-salam wa minka al-salam, tabarakta ya dha al-jalali wa al-ikram.'

Say 'Subhan Allah' 33 times, 'Al-hamdu lillah' 33 times and 'Allahu akbar' 34 times (or 33 and then 'La ilaha illa Allahu wahdahu la sharika lah…'). Sins are forgiven even if like the foam of the sea.
Whoever recites Ayat al-Kursi after every fard prayer, nothing stands between him and Paradise except death.
cards.src: Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, After the prayer

checks.q: What is said three times right after the salam?
checks.why: Then 'Allahumma anta al-salam…'.

checks.q: What reward is mentioned for Ayat al-Kursi after every fard prayer?
checks.a: Only death stands between him and Paradise
w: Sins forgiven, even like the foam of the sea
checks.why: Narrated by al-Nasa'i.

lessons.title: Greeting with salam
lessons.about: Spreading salam, and how to reply.

cards.x: The Prophet ﷺ said: you will not enter Paradise until you believe, and you will not believe until you love one another. Shall I tell you what will make you love one another? Spread salam among you.

cards.ar: وَإِذَا حُيِّيتُم بِتَحِيَّةٖ فَحَيُّواْ بِأَحْسَنَ مِنْهَآ أَوْ رُدُّوهَآ إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ حَسِيبًا ﴿٨٦﴾
cards.x: When you are greeted with a greeting, reply with a better one, or return it.
Beginning the salam is a sunnah; replying is wajib. Reply with the same or better: to 'al-salamu 'alaykum' reply 'wa 'alaykum al-salam wa rahmatullah'.
cards.src: Riyad al-Salihin, the chapter on salam

cards.x: The rider greets the one walking, the walker the one sitting, the smaller group the larger, and the young the old.
cards.src: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Seeking Permission

checks.q: What is the ruling of replying to a salam?
checks.why: Beginning it is sunnah; replying is wajib.

checks.q: What did the Prophet ﷺ say makes people love one another?
checks.why: Narrated by Muslim.

checks.q: Who should greet first, the one walking or the one sitting?
checks.why: And the rider greets the walker, the few greet the many.

checks.q: Someone says 'al-salamu 'alaykum wa rahmatullah'. What is the better reply?
checks.why: Reply with the same or better.

lessons.title: Eating and drinking
lessons.about: The sunnahs of the table.

cards.x: Wash the hands, say 'Bismillah', and eat with the right hand from what is in front of you. If you forget bismillah, say 'Bismillahi awwalahu wa akhirah.'

cards.ar: يَٰبَنِيٓ ءَادَمَ خُذُواْ زِينَتَكُمْ عِندَ كُلِّ مَسْجِدٖ وَكُلُواْ وَاشْرَبُواْ وَلَا تُسْرِفُوٓاْ إِنَّهُ لَا يُحِبُّ الْمُسْرِفِينَ ﴿٣١﴾
cards.x: Eat and drink, but do not waste. Truly He does not love the wasteful.
Do not fill the stomach: a third for food, a third for drink and a third for breath. Never criticise food: eat it if you like it, leave it if you don't.
Drink sitting, in three breaths, with the right hand, and not from the mouth of a container. Gold and silver vessels are haram.
cards.src: Bidayat al-Hidayah, the adab of eating

cards.x: Lick the fingers, and say 'Al-hamdu lillahi alladhi at'amani hadha wa razaqanihi min ghayri hawlin minni wa la quwwah.'
cards.src: Sunan Abi Dawud, Book of Clothing

checks.q: You forgot to say bismillah at the start of the meal. What do you say?
checks.why: In the name of Allah at its beginning and its end.

checks.q: How did the Prophet ﷺ describe the right amount to eat?
checks.a: A third food, a third drink, a third air
w: Half food, half drink, nothing left
One full meal a day, nothing else
checks.why: Narrated by al-Tirmidhi.

checks.q: Which hand do you eat and drink with?
w: The right for eating, the left for drinking
checks.why: Shaytan eats and drinks with his left.

checks.q: What did the Prophet ﷺ do with food he ﷺ did not like?
checks.why: He never found fault with food.

lessons.title: Dressing and the sunnahs of the body
lessons.about: Clothing, and the fitrah.

cards.x: Begin with the right when dressing and the left when undressing. Say 'Al-hamdu lillahi alladhi kasani hadha wa razaqanihi…' when putting on clothes.
Gold and silk are haram for men. A man's garment should not drag below the ankles out of pride.
The acts of the fitrah: circumcision, removing pubic hair, plucking the armpits, trimming the moustache and clipping the nails. Do not leave them more than forty days.

checks.q: Which foot or sleeve do you begin with when dressing?
checks.why: Right when dressing, left when undressing.

checks.q: Trimming the nails and moustache and removing body hair: what is the longest they should be left?
checks.why: Anas رضي الله عنه narrated the limit of forty days.

checks.q: Which of these is haram for men to wear?
checks.why: A silver ring of modest weight is allowed for men.

lessons.title: The home and the masjid
lessons.about: Entering, leaving, and the adab of the masjid.

cards.x: Say: 'Bismillah, tawakkaltu 'ala Allah, wa la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah.' It is said to him: you are guided, protected and sufficed.
cards.src: Sunan Abi Dawud, Book of Manners

cards.x: Enter with the right foot saying 'Allahumma iftah li abwaba rahmatik', and leave with the left saying 'Allahumma inni as'aluka min fadlik.' Pray two rak'ahs greeting the masjid before sitting.
Do not come after eating raw onion or garlic, do not raise your voice, do not pass in front of someone praying, and do not trade or look for lost things in it.
cards.src: Bidayat al-Hidayah, the adab of the masjid

checks.q: With which foot do you enter the masjid?
checks.why: Right to enter the masjid; left to enter the toilet.

checks.q: What do you say when entering the masjid?
checks.why: Open for me the doors of Your mercy. The second is said when leaving.

checks.q: What should you avoid before going to the masjid?
checks.why: Their smell harms the people and the angels.

checks.q: What is the prayer on entering the masjid before sitting?
checks.why: Tahiyyat al-masjid, at a time when prayer is not disliked.

lessons.title: Sneezing, the sick and the funeral
lessons.about: Small acts with great reward.

cards.x: Whoever sneezes says 'Al-hamdu lillah'; the one who hears replies 'Yarhamuk Allah'; the sneezer answers 'Yahdikumu Allahu wa yuslihu balakum.' When yawning, cover the mouth and hold it back as much as you can.
Visiting the sick is among the rights of a Muslim. Whoever visits a sick person is among the fruits of Paradise until he returns. Pray for him: 'La ba's, tahurun in sha' Allah.'

Six rights of a Muslim over another: return his salam, answer his invitation, give him sincere advice, reply when he sneezes and praises Allah, visit him when ill, and follow his funeral when he dies.

checks.q: Someone sneezes and says 'Al-hamdu lillah'. What do you reply?
checks.why: May Allah have mercy on you.

checks.q: Which is one of the six rights of a Muslim over another?
checks.a: To visit him when he is ill
w: To lend him money whenever asked
checks.why: Narrated by Muslim.

checks.q: What should you do when yawning?
checks.a: Cover the mouth and hold it back
checks.why: Yawning is from Shaytan; hold it back as much as you can.

lessons.title: Before sleeping
lessons.about: Ending the day the sunnah way.

cards.x: Sleep in wudu, dust the bed, lie on the right side with the right hand under the cheek. Close the doors and cover the vessels saying bismillah.
Ayat al-Kursi, the three Quls (blowing into the hands and wiping over the body three times), the last two verses of al-Baqarah, and 'Subhan Allah' 33, 'Al-hamdu lillah' 33, 'Allahu akbar' 34.
cards.src: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Virtues of the Qur'an

cards.x: Say 'Bismika Allahumma amutu wa ahya' (in Your name, O Allah, I die and I live), and take account of your day: thank Allah for the good and repent of the wrong.
cards.src: Bidayat al-Hidayah, the adab of sleeping

checks.q: On which side is it sunnah to sleep?
checks.why: With the right hand under the cheek.

checks.q: What do you say just before sleeping?
checks.why: In Your name, O Allah, I die and I live.

checks.q: Which tasbih did the Prophet ﷺ teach 'Ali and Fatimah رضي الله عنهما for bedtime?
checks.a: Subhan Allah 33, al-hamdu lillah 33, Allahu akbar 34
w: Subhan Allah, al-hamdu lillah and Allahu akbar, 10 each
checks.why: Subhan Allah 33, al-hamdu lillah 33, Allahu akbar 34: better for them than a servant, he ﷺ said.

checks.q: What is it good to do before sleep?
checks.why: Thank Allah for the good and repent of the wrong.

lessons.title: Guarding the seven limbs
lessons.about: Al-Ghazali's guide to avoiding sins.

cards.x: Al-Ghazali says religion has two parts: doing what is commanded and leaving what is forbidden, and leaving sins is the harder and more important. Guard seven limbs: the eyes, ears, tongue, stomach, private parts, hands and feet.

cards.ar: وَلَا تَقْفُ مَا لَيْسَ لَكَ بِهِ عِلْمٌ إِنَّ السَّمْعَ وَالْبَصَرَ وَالْفُؤَادَ كُلُّ أُوْلَـٰٓئِكَ كَانَ عَنْهُ مَسْـُٔولٗا ﴿٣٦﴾
cards.x: Do not follow what you have no knowledge of. Truly the hearing, the sight and the heart: each of these will be asked about.
Lower the gaze from what is haram, and do not look at a Muslim with contempt. Do not listen to backbiting, obscenity or idle talk about others' faults; the listener shares the sin of the speaker.
cards.src: Bidayat al-Hidayah, the eye and the ear

cards.x: Guard it from eight things: lying, breaking promises, backbiting, arguing, praising yourself, cursing, praying against people, and joking that hurts or mocks.
Eat only halal, and not too much. Do not use the hands to harm, take or write what is haram. Do not walk to a ruler's door to flatter, or anywhere sinful.
cards.src: Bidayat al-Hidayah, the stomach, hands and feet

checks.q: Which part of religion is harder: doing good, or leaving sins?
checks.why: Al-Ghazali, in Bidayat al-Hidayah: anyone can do good deeds; only the truthful leave their desires.

checks.q: Listening to backbiting…
w: Is fine if you say nothing
Is a sin only if you agree with it
checks.why: Stop it, leave, or at least hate it in your heart.

checks.q: Which of these is a sin of the tongue?
w: Speaking of Allah's blessings on you
checks.why: Along with lying, broken promises, backbiting, arguing, cursing, praying against others and hurtful joking.

checks.q: How many limbs must we guard from sin?
checks.why: Al-Ghazali, in Bidayat al-Hidayah, names seven: the eyes, ears, tongue, stomach, private parts, hands and feet.

lessons.title: Seeking knowledge and passing it on
lessons.about: You have learnt the basics. Now keep learning, and teach.

cards.x: The Prophet ﷺ said: seeking knowledge is an obligation on every Muslim. Al-Ghazali explains that fard al-'ayn grows with your situation: when a prayer time comes you must know how to pray; before you marry, learn the rulings of marriage; before you trade, learn the rulings of trade. Going deeper is a virtue, and some must do it for the whole community.

cards.ar: فَتَعَٰلَى اللَّهُ الْمَلِكُ الْحَقُّ وَلَا تَعْجَلْ بِالْقُرْءَانِ مِن قَبْلِ أَن يُقْضَىٰٓ إِلَيْكَ وَحْيُهُ وَقُل رَّبِّ زِدْنِي عِلْمٗا ﴿١١٤﴾
cards.x: And say: My Lord, increase me in knowledge.

cards.ar: أَمَّنْ هُوَ قَٰنِتٌ ءَانَآءَ الَّيْلِ سَاجِدٗا وَقَآئِمٗا يَحْذَرُ الْأٓخِرَةَ وَيَرْجُواْ رَحْمَةَ رَبِّهِ قُلْ هَلْ يَسْتَوِي الَّذِينَ يَعْلَمُونَ وَالَّذِينَ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ إِنَّمَا يَتَذَكَّرُ أُوْلُواْ الْأَلْبَٰبِ ﴿٩﴾
cards.x: Say: Are those who know equal to those who do not know?
He ﷺ said: convey from me, even one verse. And: whoever guides to good has the reward of the one who does it. Teach your family first what you have learnt.
cards.src: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of the Prophets

cards.x: Teach only what you know well, say 'I don't know' when you don't, mention your source, be gentle and make it easy.
cards.src: Bidayat al-Hidayah, the adab of the scholar

cards.x: Al-Ghazali warns: knowledge that is not acted on is a proof against you. Act on what you learn, then study further with a teacher, in the Course and in our live classes.

checks.q: What did the Prophet ﷺ say about passing on knowledge?
checks.why: Narrated by al-Bukhari.

checks.q: Someone asks you a question you are unsure about. What should you do?
checks.a: Say 'I don't know', or refer them on
w: Give the view that seems most likely to you
Give the easiest view, to make it light for them
checks.why: Speaking about the religion without knowledge is a grave sin; 'I don't know' protects you.

checks.q: Who should you teach first?
checks.why: 'Protect yourselves and your families from a Fire.' (al-Tahrim 6)

checks.q: What is knowledge that is not acted on?
checks.a: It is a proof against you
checks.why: Act on what you learn.
